They stay inside this one row rather than opening fresh rows not because each 'launches directly into an uninterrupted beno-suffix chain' -- false for Kohath, whose chain stops headless of beno at oshb 6:10 and again at 6:13 (per-verse beno-count across oshb 6:7-6:15 runs 3,3,4,0,3,3,0,3,3), re-heading each time with a resumptive Elkanah (oshb 6:11) -- but because no head inside the span, including those three intervening re-heads (oshb 6:10, 6:11, 6:13), carries a toledot or dated closure of its own. That property holds for both clans, though unbrokenly only for Merari's re-entry (בְּנֵ֥י מְרָרִ֖י..., 6:29, running without a break to 6:30), functioning as a resumptive re-pick of a name decision 035 already introduced -- the same pivot 6:20's own opening “Of Gershom” performs -- rather than as a register-opening head. Along the way, a one-verse Samuel notice names WEB's 'firstborn, Joel' at 6:28: WEB reads “The sons of Samuel: the firstborn, Joel, and the second, Abijah.” (web 6:28), but that rendering supplies the name Joel from a source outside this campaign's evidence base (no 1 Samuel witness is available to verify it), not from the Hebrew of this verse -- oshb 6:13's own wording, “וּבְנֵ֧י שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל הַבְּכֹ֥ר וַשְׁנִ֖י וַאֲבִיָּֽה” (weak samekh, single-witness), names only 'the firstborn ... and the second, Abijah,' with no Joel in it; the Hebrew name Joel this campaign can cite for Samuel's line sits five verses on in the MT, at oshb 6:18 (web 6:33), one row later (decision M8-1Chr-037, span 6:31-6:38), inside Heman's own ancestry. It closes at 6:30, “שִׁמְעָ֥א בְנ֛וֹ חַגִּיָּ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ עֲשָׂיָ֥ה בְנֽוֹ” (WEB “Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.”; weak pe, single-witness), immediately before 6:31 opens an unrelated unit with its own occasion-dated appointment head rather than a further “his son” link.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the 6:22 and 6:29 clan re-entries as fresh register-opening heads, matching decisions 033/035's row-constituting formula, is the strongest rival, but neither carries the toledot or dated closure those rows use to seal a head before a new one opens; both launch directly into an uninterrupted beno-suffix chain, marking them as resumptive re-picks of names decision 035 already introduced rather than as seams.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 6:31 with an appointment formula unlike anything in decisions 03-04: “These are they whom David set over the service of song in Yahweh's house” over וְאֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶעֱמִ֥יד דָּוִ֛יד עַל יְדֵי שִׁ֖יר בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה (oshb 6:16), dated “after the ark came to rest” — a narrative-anchored occasion, not a bare genealogical head. 6:32 extends the frame (ministry “until Solomon had built Yahweh's house,” duties “according to their order”), and 6:33 re-heads the singers specifically (“these are those who served, and their sons”) before naming Heman and tracing his Kohathite ancestry without a break through 6:38's terminus, “the son of Levi, the son of Israel” over בֶּן לֵוִ֖י בֶּן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb 6:23) — reaching the tribal eponym himself, the deepest point any chain in this chapter reaches, functioning as a completion marker. 6:39 then opens a matching but distinct chain, “His brother Asaph,” tied to Heman by kinship rather than continuing his line, confirming the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 31-48 as one row would submerge the tier-1 form-shift at 6:31 (an occasion-dated royal appointment, not a register head) and the parallel triad structure the text repeats at 39 and 44.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 6:39 with the possessive tie that marks this as Heman's counterpart rather than a fresh register head: “His brother Asaph, who stood on his right hand” over וְאָחִ֣יו אָסָ֔ף הָעֹמֵ֖ד עַל יְמִינ֑וֹ אָסָ֥ף בֶּן בֶּרֶכְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן שִׁמְעָֽא (oshb 6:24), then traces Asaph's Gershomite ancestry in the same “son of” chain form decision 037 used for Heman. It closes at 6:43 with a terminus formula one generation short of Israel: “the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi” over בֶּן יַ֥חַת בֶּן גֵּרְשֹׁ֖ם בֶּן לֵוִֽי (oshb 6:28, samekh, single-witness) -- reaching Levi and stopping. In all three singer chains Israel sits one generation above Levi, so a branch identified below Levi -- Izharite, Gershomite, or Merarite -- cannot by itself explain whether a chain reaches up to Israel; what is observable instead is that oshb 6:28 (Asaph's Gershomite terminus, quoted above) and oshb 6:32 (Ethan's Merarite terminus, בֶּן מְרָרִ֖י בֶּן לֵוִֽי, decision 039) both stop at 'son of Levi' with no further ascent, while only oshb 6:23 (Heman's Kohathite terminus, בֶּן יִצְהָ֣ר בֶּן קְהָ֔ת בֶּן לֵוִ֖י בֶּן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, decision 037) continues on to 'son of Israel.' 6:44 opens the third of the triad with its own positional marker, “On the left hand,” confirming that the text itself organizes these as parallel, paired chains rather than one continuous list.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging Asaph's line with Heman's into a single 31-43 row would obscure the fraternal 'right hand / left hand' framing the text uses to keep the two chains formally distinct.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 6:44 with the paired positional marker that completes decision 038's frame: “On the left hand their brothers the sons of Merari: Ethan…” over וּבְנֵ֧י מְרָרִ֛י אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם עַֽל הַשְּׂמֹ֑אול אֵיתָן֙ בֶּן קִישִׁ֔י בֶּן עַבְדִּ֖י בֶּן מַלּֽוּךְ (oshb 6:29) -- a waw-prefixed construct head, וּבְנֵ֧י מְרָרִ֛י, that holds its own positional tag, עַֽל הַשְּׂמֹ֑אול, to the clause's end, mirrored by decision 038's own opening at oshb 6:24 (= web 6:39, Asaph's 'His brother' notice), which fronts the kinship term וְאָחִ֣יו אָסָ֔ף ahead of its own position phrase; the two openings are not structurally parallel at their start, only their matched position nouns (right hand / left hand) pair up. The chain traces Ethan's line to its own Levite terminus at 6:47, reaching “בֶּן מְרָרִ֖י בֶּן לֵוִֽי” in oshb 6:32 (weak samekh, single-witness) -- son of Merari, son of Levi. It closes at 6:48 with a colophon that shifts from named individuals back to the class as a whole: “Their brothers the Levites were appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of God's house” over וַאֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַלְוִיִּ֑ם נְתוּנִ֕ים לְכָ֨ל עֲבוֹדַ֔ת מִשְׁכַּ֖ן בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים (oshb 6:33). That reading is contested rather than settled: oshb 6:33 and oshb 6:34 (decision 040's own opening) share one syntactic template -- waw, fronted compound subject, participle, duty-scope clause -- so reading 6:33-6:34 together as a matched pair of duty notices (the remaining Levites' general service beside Aaron's altar-specific service) is at least as natural as reading 6:33 as a summary sealing off the singers' section before 6:49 turns to the priestly altar-function.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving 6:48 its own one-verse row would sever a colophon from the triad it summarizes; the genuinely live rival is not that split but reading 6:33-6:34 together as a matched pair of duty notices rather than as a seal followed by a fresh unit, a question this row's now-lowered confidence reflects rather than resolves.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 6:49 with וְֽאַהֲרֹ֨ן וּבָנָ֜יו מַקְטִירִ֨ים עַל מִזְבַּ֤ח הָֽעוֹלָה֙ וְעַל מִזְבַּ֣ח הַקְּטֹ֔רֶת לְכֹ֕ל מְלֶ֖אכֶת קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים וּלְכַפֵּר֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֥בֶד הָאֱלֹהִֽים (oshb 6:34) -- a plain conjunctive waw on a fronted compound subject followed by a participle, with no adversative particle anywhere in the clause; WEB's “But Aaron and his sons offered...” (web 6:49) is the translator's rendering, not a feature of the Hebrew itself, so the attachment forward rather than back does not rest on that word. It rests instead on the referential link from this clause's subject, Aaron and his sons, to the register head that follows in the very next verse, “these are the sons of Aaron” (oshb 6:35 = web 6:50) -- the notice at 6:49 introduces the names that head unpacks. A weak PE stands after oshb 6:34 (single-witness); under the convention that a mark keyed to verse X follows that verse, it corroborates the internal division between this altar-function notice and the Aaronide list at 6:50, not the 6:48/6:49 edge itself. The “his son” chain that follows closes at 6:53, “Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son” (oshb 6:38, samekh, single-witness) -- the same Eleazar-to-Ahimaaz span decision 034 already traced for the pre-exilic high-priestly line, here repeated as a short standalone unit before 6:54's dwelling-places formula opens the settlement register.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 6:49 as closing the singers' section (paired with 6:48) rather than opening the priestly line would lose the referential tie from 6:49's Aaron-and-his-sons subject forward to the register head that names them at 6:50, a tie that does not depend on WEB's 'But' or on any adversative reading of the Hebrew conjunction.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 6:54 with the settlement register's own two tier-1 elements: the formula “וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ מוֹשְׁבוֹתָ֔ם לְטִירוֹתָ֖ם בִּגְבוּלָ֑ם” ("now these are their dwelling places, by their encampments, in their borders") and the scoping phrase that follows it, “לִבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ לְמִשְׁפַּחַ֣ת הַקְּהָתִ֔י” ("to the sons of Aaron, of the family of the Kohathites") -- WEB renders the clause that follows, כִּ֥י לָהֶ֖ם הָיָ֥ה הַגּוֹרָֽל, as “(for theirs was the first lot)” (web 6:54), but that ordinal has no Hebrew counterpart: the clause itself reads only 'for theirs was the lot,' and a sweep of the whole offset zone for the root ראש returns no occurrence anywhere in it. The settlement formula and Aaronic/Kohathite scoping, not any priority ordinal, are what mark this as its own register: WEB 6:61-6:62 open instead with וְלִבְנֵ֨י, a waw-prefixed libne-X construct head naming which clan receives cities from a tribal source, not a settlement-and-dwelling-place notice; WEB 6:63, by contrast, opens the same construct head waw-less (לִבְנֵ֨י מְרָרִ֜י), and the same waw-less libne-X formula recurs again at oshb 6:56 and oshb 6:62 (= web 6:71, 6:77), so it is the libne-X head with its tribal source and numeral, not the waw, that is the stable mark of the device. The unit carries the Caleb aside (6:56, fields given “to Caleb the son of Jephunneh” rather than to the Levites, a named exception the text itself flags) through the cities-of-refuge list, closing at 6:60 with a tally distinctive to this sub-grant: “All their cities throughout their families were thirteen cities” over כָּל עָרֵיהֶ֛ם שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה עִ֖יר בְּמִשְׁפְּחוֹתֵיהֶֽם (oshb 6:45, weak samekh, single-witness). 6:61 opens a parallel grant for Kohath's remaining, not-yet-allotted families, with its own tally and its own wə-libnê opening rather than 6:54's settlement-notice formula, confirming the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this row through 6:65 would blur the settlement-notice formula and Aaronic/Kohathite scoping that opens 6:54 into the undifferentiated by-lot tallies of 6:61-6:63, which open instead with 'to the rest of the sons of Kohath' (oshb 6:46) naming a distinct sub-group under a different formula, not a repetition of 6:54's own scoping.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 6:61 with “the rest of the sons of Kohath” receiving cities “by lot” out of half-Manasseh -- a plain by-lot tally, tribal source plus numeral only, no city named -- and runs the matching Gershomite (62) and Merarite (63) tallies, each closing with its own city-count. It closes at 6:64-65 with a two-part colophon on the whole Levitical distribution begun at 6:54 (decision 041), not merely on this row's own 61-63: v.64, “The children of Israel gave to the Levites the cities with their pasture lands” (וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֶת הֶעָרִ֖ים וְאֶת מִגְרְשֵׁיהֶֽם, oshb 6:49), is the general summary sentence covering both decision 041's named Aaronic grant and this row's own tribal-tally grant; v.65 then recapitulates specifically the Judah/Simeon/Benjamin portion within its own clause, “וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ בַגּוֹרָ֗ל מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בְנֵי יְהוּדָה֙ וּמִמַּטֵּ֣ה בְנֵי שִׁמְע֔וֹן וּמִמַּטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן אֵ֚ת הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר יִקְרְא֥וּ אֶתְהֶ֖ם בְּשֵׁמֽוֹת” (oshb 6:50, weak samekh, single-witness) -- an attributive demonstrative on the object of the giving-verb, “they gave by lot ... these cities which are mentioned by name,” not a verbless 'these are' formula (contrast the genuine nominal אלה-clause this cluster demotes to internal bookkeeping at oshb 7:17). The antecedent of “mentioned by name” is not this row's own 61-63, which names only tribes and numerals, but decision 041's already-named Aaronic cities (Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Hilen, Debir, Ashan, Beth-Shemesh, Geba, Alemeth, Anathoth) -- v.65's Judah/Simeon/Benjamin tribe list does not match that earlier grant exactly, though it can be reconciled with it verse by verse: Benjamin is named as a tribe at oshb 6:45 (וּמִמַּטֵּ֣ה בִנְיָמִ֗ן), matching 6:50's own construction; Judah, by contrast, is named as a territory rather than a tribe at oshb 6:40 (בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה); and Simeon is absent from decision 041's span outright -- a sweep of oshb 6:39-6:45 finds no occurrence of the name -- reached only through Ashan, oshb 6:44 (= web 6:59), which oshb 4:32 identifies as Simeonite territory (inside the register opened at oshb 4:24). The colophon stays attached to this row because nothing interrupts between 6:63's tally and 6:65's recap; 6:66 then reopens Kohath's case on unheaded, different terms, marking the true outer edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 64-65 as heading what follows rather than closing 61-63 is a real rival, since the cities v.65 calls 'named' are not this row's own, but 6:66 supplies no heading formula of any kind before it starts naming cities -- it is a bare, unheaded resumption -- so v.65's own recap of the already-named Judah/Simeon/Benjamin grant reads more naturally as looking back across the whole distribution than as introducing what 043 goes on to name.

boundary_rationale: Opens at 6:66 with an unheaded resumption of Kohath that decision 042 had already closed: “Some of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their borders out of the tribe of Ephraim” over וּמִֽמִּשְׁפְּח֖וֹת בְּנֵ֣י קְהָ֑ת וַיְהִי֙ עָרֵ֣י גְבוּלָ֔ם מִמַּטֵּ֖ה אֶפְרָֽיִם (oshb 6:51) -- and although Kohath also receives a second, differently-sourced grant later in this very row, from half-Manasseh at oshb 6:55 (= web 6:70, הַנּוֹתָרִֽים, 'the remaining,' the same designation that opens decision 042's own Kohath tally at oshb 6:46 and recurs again at oshb 6:62 and, outside this offset zone, at 24:20 -- a book sweep finds it nowhere else), a second tribal source cannot by itself be the tier-1 signal of a fresh pass, since this row's own single span already tolerates it internally. The tier-1 signal is instead the shift from decision 042's bare by-lot tallies (tribal source plus numeral, no city named) to this row's own named-city lists, disclosed further below. The pass reruns the same three clans (Kohath 66-70, Gershom 71-76, Merari 77-81), and the לבני X formula that opens Gershom's and Merari's re-entries here -- לִבְנֵי֮ (6:71 = oshb 6:56) and לִבְנֵ֣י מְרָרִי֮ (6:77 = oshb 6:62) -- is the identical construct-plural form decision 042 treats as row-constituting at 6:61-6:63; it does not reopen a fresh register here because each pass's own three clan-heads function as internal list-dividers within that pass, not as competing register-openings, once the whole is read as two sequential distribution rounds rather than one continuous list. Unlike decision 042's tallies, this pass supplies actual city names -- Gershom's 13 named cities here (oshb 6:56-6:61 = web 6:71-6:76) match decision 042's own stated Gershom tally of 13 exactly, while Kohath's 8 and Merari's 10 named cities diverge from 042's stated 10 and 12 for those clans, a discrepancy this campaign discloses rather than resolves. The pass runs to the chapter's final verse, 6:81, with no clan or region left to name after Gad's cities: “Heshbon with its pasture lands, and Jazer with its pasture lands” over וְאֶת חֶשְׁבּוֹן֙ וְאֶת מִגְרָשֶׁ֔יהָ וְאֶת יַעְזֵ֖יר וְאֶת מִגְרָשֶֽׁיהָ (oshb 6:66, weak samekh, single-witness) -- the last item in the last of the three lists, with the fresh “sons of Issachar” head that opens ch.7 confirming the close of the whole Levi complex.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this pass at each clan boundary (66-70/71-76/77-81), mirroring decisions 041-042, would over-fragment what is better read as one uniform second distribution round: each clan-head inside it is the same list-internal לבני X divider decision 042 uses within its own single row, and the Gershom/Merari city-name counts track decision 042's own numeral tallies closely enough to confirm this pass and that one are reporting one distribution process at two levels of detail, not two independent registers.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the register-head formula “וְלִבְנֵ֣י יִשָׂשכָ֗ר תּוֹלָ֧ע וּפוּאָ֛ה ישיב יָשׁ֥וּב וְשִׁמְר֖וֹן אַרְבָּעָֽה” ("Of the sons of Issachar"), which WEB renders as a fresh tribal heading naming four sons and immediately branching into Tola's clan (v2, its own count of 22,600) and Izrahiah's war-band (vv3-4, its own count of 36,000). It closes on a further, wider reckoning at v5: “וַאֲחֵיהֶ֗ם לְכֹל֙ מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשָׂשכָ֔ר גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י חֲיָלִ֑ים שְׁמוֹנִ֤ים וְשִׁבְעָה֙ אֶ֔לֶף הִתְיַחְשָׂ֖ם לַכֹּֽל” ("and their kinsmen, of all the families of Issachar, mighty men of valor, listed in all by genealogy, were eighty-seven thousand"), whose own scope -- "their kinsmen, of all the families of Issachar" -- names a broader population than Tola's chiefs and Izrahiah's band alone, so its total of 87,000 is an independent count supplied by its own reckoning formula, הִתְיַחְשָׂ֖ם לַכֹּֽל, not a sum of the 22,600 and 36,000 already given (which together total 58,600, well short of 87,000). A pe stands in the Masoretic tradition right at this same edge, trailing v5 (single-witness); being tier-3 it only seconds a close the arithmetic has already made. The next verse restarts cold with the bare tribe name “בִּנְיָמִ֗ן בֶּ֧לַע וָבֶ֛כֶר וִידִֽיעֲאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשָֽׁה”, WEB “The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.” -- a new three-item head count with no syntactic tie back to Issachar's total, so the seam at 7.5/7.6 is doubly marked (closure formula then fresh head).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 7:1-6 as one Issachar-Benjamin block because both open with a tribe name loses, because 7:6 restarts with its own independent head-count ("three") exactly mirroring 7:1's own head-count ("four"), marking a genuine new tribal register rather than a continuation.

boundary_rationale: Opens with “בִּנְיָמִ֗ן בֶּ֧לַע וָבֶ֛כֶר וִידִֽיעֲאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשָֽׁה” (WEB “The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.”) -- a bare name-plus-numeral line with no בני in the Hebrew at all; WEB's "The sons of" is the translator's supplied heading, not a feature of this verse, as decision 044's own description of this identical verse already establishes. The three members that line announces -- Bela, Becher, Jediael -- are then unpacked one by one, each closed by its own inclusio-style summary rather than by any competing register formula: Bela's clan (v7) ends with a census figure and no closing tag; Becher's (v8-9) closes “כָּל אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵי בָֽכֶר” ("all these are sons of Becher") plus its own census; Jediael's (v10-11) closes “כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י יְדִֽיעֲאֵל֙” ("all these are sons of Jediael") plus the war-muster total, “כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י יְדִֽיעֲאֵל֙ לְרָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֔וֹת גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י חֲיָלִ֑ים שִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֨לֶף֙ וּמָאתַ֔יִם יֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָ֖א לַמִּלְחָמָֽה” (seventeen thousand two hundred, "who were able to go out in the army for war", WEB v11). The samekh marks after v7 and v9 (single-witness, tier-3) land exactly at these clan sub-totals, weakly corroborating the internal three-clan structure without being asked to drive anything, since granularity is kept at the tribal register, not the clan. The unit closes at v11's war-muster total. What follows, “וְשֻׁפִּ֤ם וְחֻפִּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י עִ֔יר חֻשִׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י אַחֵֽר” (WEB “So were Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, and the sons of Aher.”), opens with a bare conjunction and no head formula of any kind, so it cannot be silently absorbed into this closed register.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting into three rows at each clan's census total (vv6-7 / 8-9 / 10-11) loses, because all three sub-lists unpack the exact three-member count ("three") that v6 itself announces, two of them, Becher's (v.8) and Jediael's (v.11), sealed by their own 'all these are sons of X' inclusio, while Bela's (v.7) closes on its census figure alone with no closing tag -- none carrying an independent tribal register formula -- there being no 'sons of Benjamin' head at v6 to compete with in the first place -- and the samekh marks after v7/v9 are tier-3 weak corroboration only, never a driver.

boundary_rationale: The whole verse “וְשֻׁפִּ֤ם וְחֻפִּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י עִ֔יר חֻשִׁ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י אַחֵֽר” (WEB “So were Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, and the sons of Aher.”) contains בני twice -- בְּנֵ֣י עִ֔יר and בְּנֵ֥י אַחֵֽר -- but never in clause-initial position, unlike the fronted בְּנֵ֣י נַפְתָּלִ֗י that opens v13 next door; v13 itself, though, closes on the identical predicate-position pattern (בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָֽה), so fronting rather than bare presence is the real criterion distinguishing a register head from a list-internal name. Contrast the war-muster closure just before v12, “כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י יְדִֽיעֲאֵל֙ לְרָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֔וֹת גִּבּוֹרֵ֖י חֲיָלִ֑ים שִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֨לֶף֙ וּמָאתַ֔יִם יֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָ֖א לַמִּלְחָמָֽה” (WEB v11's "...who were able to go out in the army for war"), which finishes the Benjamin unit's arithmetic, and the fresh fronted head just after it, “בְּנֵ֣י נַפְתָּלִ֗י יַחֲצִיאֵ֧ל וְגוּנִ֛י וְיֵ֥צֶר וְשַׁלּ֖וּם בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָֽה”, which opens a new tribe. Two recurrences bear on where v12's names belong, and neither settles it: v7 lists וְעִירִ֜י (Iri) among Bela's sons, one final yod from v12's עִ֔יר (Ir), the only עירי in the book; more decisively, v15 -- three verses later, inside decision 048's own Manasseh row -- names Huppim and Shuppim outright, verbatim, in a marriage notice -- Machir taking a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim, per the doubled prefix marking them as the parties for whom the wife was taken (the noun itself is singular, not plural) (וּמָכִ֞יר לָקַ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ לְחֻפִּ֣ים וּלְשֻׁפִּ֔ים וְשֵׁ֤ם אֲחֹתוֹ֙ מַעֲכָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖י צְלָפְחָ֑ד וַתִּהְיֶ֥נָה לִצְלָפְחָ֖ד בָּנֽוֹת), and a book-wide sweep confirms the Huppim consonants recur nowhere else in 1 Chronicles, but the Shuppim/Shapham consonants do: the same letters also name a Gadite chief at 5:12 (וְשָׁפָ֖ם, WEB 'Shapham') and a gatekeeper at 26:16 (לְשֻׁפִּ֤ים, WEB 'Shuppim'), both unrelated referents, which if anything weakens rather than strengthens the 'exact recurrence' framing offered for the Manasseh candidate. Neither the Iri/Ir near-miss nor the Huppim/Shuppim exact recurrence establishes a lineage tie the Hebrew itself states; a name recurring elsewhere is not by itself a lineage frame, and the WEB translators' own choice of "So were" (rather than "and the sons of") signals the same discontinuity in English. No mark corroborates either edge of this single verse, consistent with the rule that mark absence is never held as evidence either way. Given the unresolved tribal identity of Ir/Aher (a longstanding point of scholarly puzzlement this campaign has no corpus basis to adjudicate) and now two disclosed, unresolved near/exact recurrences rather than one, this row is held at low confidence rather than merged for convenience.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v12 into the Manasseh row that follows (048) is the genuinely strongest rival, not the earlier Benjamin-side framing: v15 there names Huppim and Shuppim verbatim, an exact recurrence closer and stronger than v7's Iri/Ir near-miss -- but a name recurring in an unrelated genealogical transaction three verses away does not by itself establish the lineage tie needed to relocate v12 into either neighbor's list.

boundary_rationale: "בְּנֵ֣י נַפְתָּלִ֗י יַחֲצִיאֵ֧ל וְגוּנִ֛י וְיֵ֥צֶר וְשַׁלּ֖וּם בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָֽה" (WEB "The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum, and the sons of Bilhah") opens with its own unambiguous register-head formula, unlike the fragment immediately preceding it in v12, and the pe mark falling after v13 (single-witness, tier-3) weakly corroborates a division exactly here. The unit closes because v14 opens a fresh tribal head, "בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה" (WEB "The sons of Manasseh"), with its own genealogical content that has nothing to do with Naphtali. Naphtali's entire tribal entry is compressed into this one verse with no clan sub-lists and no census total, unlike Issachar, Benjamin, or Asher elsewhere in this chapter; the text gives no explanation for the brevity, and none is invented here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating v12 and v13 as one leftover appendix unit loses, because v13 carries its own register-head formula ("sons of Naphtali") that v12 entirely lacks, so the two verses do not share a common frame.

boundary_rationale: Opens “בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אַשְׂרִיאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלָ֑דָה פִּֽילַגְשׁוֹ֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּיָּ֔ה יָלְדָ֕ה אֶת מָכִ֖יר אֲבִ֥י גִלְעָֽד” (WEB “The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bore. She bore Machir the father of Gilead.”) -- the Manasseh head running to Machir and Gilead; the first verb, יָלָ֑דָה ("she bore"), has no expressed subject of its own in the Hebrew (אֲשֶׁ֣ר is the relative particle introducing it), and it is only the following verb, bearing Machir, whose subject is explicitly given as "his Aramean concubine" -- WEB's reading, which extends her as mother of Asriel too, is the translator's construal, not a statement the witness itself makes, and the row's boundary argument does not depend on resolving it. Midway, v17 closes a sub-thread with its own "these are" formula, “וּבְנֵ֥י אוּלָ֖ם בְּדָ֑ן אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד בֶּן מָכִ֖יר בֶּן מְנַשֶּֽׁה” (WEB “The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.”), but this does not restart the register: vv18-19 continue describing the same Machir-Gilead family circle (his sister Hammolecheth's children, then Shemida's sons) without any competing tribal head, so the v17 formula is internal bookkeeping inside one Manasseh unit, not a seam between two units. The unit closes at “וַיִּהְי֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י שְׁמִידָ֑ע אַחְיָ֣ן וָשֶׁ֔כֶם וְלִקְחִ֖י וַאֲנִיעָֽם” (WEB “The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.”) -- a verbal continuation clause opening with the wayyiqtol וַיִּהְי֖וּ ("and there were"), not a fourth fronted register head of the kind found at 7:13, 7:14, and 7:20, which is exactly why v19 closes this unit rather than opening a new one. The Masoretic tradition places a pe immediately after v19 (single-witness) -- tier-3 weak support only, pointing to the same edge without driving it. What follows, “וּבְנֵ֥י אֶפְרַ֖יִם” (WEB "The sons of Ephraim:"), is an unrelated tribal head, marking the true outer boundary. This region's internal genealogical relationships (how the daughters of Zelophehad and Hammolecheth's children connect) are not fully recoverable from 1Chr's wording alone; that uncertainty is about content, not about where this row's edges fall.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v17's internal closure (14-17 / 18-19) loses, because vv18-19 keep describing the same Machir-Gilead-Manasseh family cluster with no new tribal head, so v17's formula closes a sub-thread, not the register.

boundary_rationale: Opens “וּבְנֵ֥י אֶפְרַ֖יִם שׁוּתָ֑לַח וּבֶ֤רֶד בְּנוֹ֙ וְתַ֣חַת בְּנ֔וֹ וְאֶלְעָדָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ וְתַ֥חַת בְּנֽוֹ” (WEB “The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,”), setting up a “his son” (בְּנוֹ) patrilineal refrain repeated through v21a. At v21b the syntax shifts to a new finite verbal clause, “וְזָבָ֥ד בְּנ֛וֹ וְשׁוּתֶ֥לַח בְּנ֖וֹ וְעֵ֣זֶר וְאֶלְעָ֑ד וַהֲרָג֗וּם אַנְשֵׁי גַת֙ הַנּוֹלָדִ֣ים בָּאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֣י יָרְד֔וּ לָקַ֖חַת אֶת מִקְנֵיהֶֽם” (WEB “Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath who were born in the land killed, because they came down to take away their livestock.”), introducing the new subject אַנְשֵׁי גַת֙ ("the men of Gath") where the preceding text ran a nominal X-plus-son sequence; וְעֵ֣זֶר וְאֶלְעָ֑ד ("Ezer, and Elead") are the two named sons and the object of the killing, per the row's own WEB quotation above -- the verb וַהֲרָג֗וּם itself is a waw-plus-suffix-conjugation form with a 3mp object suffix referring back to Ezer and Elead ('and they killed them'), not a wayyiqtol (it carries no prefix-conjugation preformative), so genuine wayyiqtol narration in this inset begins one clause later, with וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֛ל (v22); בְּנ֛וֹ ('his son'), by contrast, is simply the noun bearing a 3ms possessive suffix that continues the row's own patrilineal refrain from v.20-21a and carries no 3mp feature under any reading. The narrative continues through the mourning notice, “וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֛ל אֶפְרַ֥יִם אֲבִיהֶ֖ם יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶחָ֖יו לְנַחֲמֽוֹ” (WEB “Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.”), and the birth-naming, “וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶת שְׁמוֹ֙ בְּרִיעָ֔ה כִּ֥י בְרָעָ֖ה הָיְתָ֥ה בְּבֵיתֽוֹ” ("he called his name Beriah, because misfortune..." -- the naming itself plays on the sound of בְרָעָ֖ה against בְּרִיעָ֔ה, visible directly in the Hebrew text, not asserted from any footnote). The same family-notice frame continues at v24 rather than closing at v23's naming-etymology: “וּבִתּ֣וֹ שֶׁאֱרָ֔ה וַתִּ֧בֶן אֶת בֵּית חוֹר֛וֹן הַתַּחְתּ֖וֹן וְאֶת הָעֶלְי֑וֹן וְאֵ֖ת אֻזֵּ֥ן שֶׁאֱרָֽה” (WEB “His daughter was Sheerah, who built Beth Horon the lower and the upper, and Uzzen Sheerah.”) names Ephraim's daughter Sheerah and her city-building, extending the same household notice vv21b-23 already carry rather than opening a fresh device; v24 shares a place-naming interest with 7:28-29's later settlement formula, but that later formula is a differently-scoped, collective device ("their possessions and settlements," third-person plural, scoped to the whole tribe/Joseph at v29) rather than the individual family notice this inset carries, which is why v24 stays bound here rather than reading forward. The chain then resumes its own refrain verbatim at v25, “וְרֶ֣פַח בְּנ֗וֹ וְרֶ֧שֶׁף וְתֶ֛לַח בְּנ֖וֹ וְתַ֥חַן בְּנֽוֹ” (WEB “Rephah was his son, Resheph his son, Telah his son, Tahan his son,”), running to “נ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בְּנֽוֹ” (WEB “Nun his son, and Joshua his son.”) with no intervening tribal head. Per the inset rule, a narrative aside framed by and resumed within its host chain stays inside that host; here the same בְּנוֹ refrain frames both sides of the break, so vv20-27 form one register. The row closes because v28 pivots to a settlement formula, “וַאֲחֻזָּתָם֙ וּמֹ֣שְׁבוֹתָ֔ם בֵּֽית אֵ֖ל וּבְנֹתֶ֑יהָ וְלַמִּזְרָ֣ח נַעֲרָ֔ן וְלַֽמַּעֲרָ֗ב גֶּ֤זֶר וּבְנֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ וּשְׁכֶ֣ם וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ עַד עַיָּ֖ה וּבְנֹתֶֽיהָ” (WEB “Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer with its towns; Shechem also and its towns, to Azzah and its towns;”), a different device entirely.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two rivals compete here. Opening a new row at 7:21b where the narrative interrupts the chain is the weaker one, since the same 'his son' refrain that opens the unit at v20 resumes verbatim at v25 with no new tribal head in between. The sharper rival is the v23/v24 seam -- v23's naming-etymology closure could be read as capping the inset, with v24's daughter/city-building notice reading forward toward 7:28's settlement formula instead of staying bound to vv21b-23 -- but 7:28's device is a differently-scoped, collective settlement notice, not the individual family notice v24 continues, so the inset is framed by and returns to its host per the inset rule rather than splitting at either point.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:1Chr.7.29 (comparandum, collective settlement device contrasted with v24)

boundary_rationale: Opens on a settlement-formula pivot, "וַאֲחֻזָּתָם֙ וּמֹ֣שְׁבוֹתָ֔ם בֵּֽית אֵ֖ל וּבְנֹתֶ֑יהָ" (WEB "Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns..."), replacing the patrilineal "his son" chain that just closed the Ephraim unit in v27 with a geography-of-towns list. It closes on "בְּאֵ֨לֶּה֙ יָשְׁב֔וּ בְּנֵ֥י יוֹסֵ֖ף בֶּן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" (WEB "The children of Joseph the son of Israel lived in these"). A pe trails v29 in the Masoretic tradition (single-witness); tier-3 weak support, since the wording already carries the edge on its own. That closing line names "sons of Joseph" collectively — a scope wider than Ephraim alone, since Joseph's sons are Ephraim and Manasseh together — so this notice functions as a supra-tribal closure for both the Manasseh unit (7:14-19) and the Ephraim unit (7:20-27), not as an extension of Ephraim's own genealogy. The next verse restarts with a fresh tribal head, "בְּנֵ֣י אָשֵׁ֗ר" (WEB "The sons of Asher"), unrelated to Joseph.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 7:28-29 to the preceding Ephraim row loses, because v28 opens with a settlement formula rather than the patrilineal chain, and v29's closing names "sons of Joseph" collectively, a scope broader than the Ephraim line it would be appended to.

boundary_rationale: Opens "בְּנֵ֣י אָשֵׁ֗ר יִמְנָ֧ה וְיִשְׁוָ֛ה וְיִשְׁוִ֥י וּבְרִיעָ֖ה וְשֶׂ֥רַח אֲחוֹתָֽם" (WEB "The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Serah was their sister"), a fresh tribal head after Joseph's closing notice in v29. Beriah's branch (vv31-40) mixes construct-plural register sub-heads -- v31’s "וּבְנֵ֣י בְרִיעָ֔ה" (Beriah’s own sons), v33’s "וּבְנֵ֣י יַפְלֵ֔ט" (Japhlet’s), v34’s "וּבְנֵ֖י שָׁ֑מֶר" (Shemer’s), v36’s "בְּנֵ֖י צוֹפָ֑ח" (Zophah’s), v38’s "וּבְנֵ֖י יֶ֑תֶר" (Jether’s), and v39’s "וּבְנֵ֖י עֻלָּ֑א" (Ulla’s) -- with two clauses that are not "sons of X" heads at all: v32’s hif’il genitor clause "וְחֶ֨בֶר֙ הוֹלִ֣יד" ("and Heber fathered...") and v35’s singular construct "וּבֶן הֵ֖לֶם אָחִ֑יו" ("the son of Helem his brother"). None of these eight internal breaks carries an independent census figure attached to it, unlike Benjamin's three clans in 7:6-11. The whole tribe closes on one grand total, "כָּל אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵי אָ֠שֵׁר" ... "מִסְפָּרָ֣ם אֲנָשִׁ֔ים עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֖ה אָֽלֶף" (WEB "All these were the children of Asher... The number of them listed by genealogy for service in war was twenty-six thousand men"), structurally mirroring 7:5's tribal-total closure for Issachar (שְׁמוֹנִ֤ים וְשִׁבְעָה֙ אֶ֔לֶף הִתְיַחְשָׂ֖ם לַכֹּֽל, summing 'all the families of Issachar' as a whole tribe) more closely than 7:9's and 7:11's clan-level totals (עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וּמָאתָֽיִם for Becher's clan alone; שִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֨לֶף֙ וּמָאתַ֔יִם יֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָ֖א לַמִּלְחָמָֽה for Jediael's clan alone), both of the latter nested within the single Benjamin tribal register opened at 7:6, as this row's own earlier sentence on Benjamin's three clans already states. 7:9 and 7:11 accordingly stand as evidence that the census formula operates at more than one level, tribe and clan, not as parallel tribe closures matching 7:5. On its own that formula closes Asher alone: v40’s opening, "כָּל אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵי אָ֠שֵׁר", names only Asher, exactly paralleling 7:5’s tribe-specific "מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשָׂשכָ֔ר" for Issachar. The further observation that Asher, closing this way, is also the chapter’s last of the six tribes opened at 7:1 ("וְלִבְנֵ֣י יִשָׂשכָ֗ר", "now the sons of Issachar") is a positional inference from the chapter's tribe-by-tribe sequence, not a claim the closing formula itself makes. A samekh sits in the Masoretic tradition at the chapter's very last verse-end (single-witness); being tier-3 it can only second, never establish, a close the census arithmetic has already secured. The next verse opens 1Chr 8 with a new register entirely, "וּבִ֨נְיָמִ֔ן הוֹלִ֖יד" (WEB "Benjamin became the father of Bela his firstborn").
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Asher's register at each internal sub-head -- whether a construct-plural “sons of X” head (Beriah, Japhlet, Shemer, Zophah, Jether, Ulla) or a genitor/singular clause (Heber’s own line, Helem’s brother notice) -- loses, because none of those eight breaks carries its own census total the way the row's outer edges do; they are subordinate branches inside one register closed by a single grand total.

boundary_rationale: Opens "וּבִ֨נְיָמִ֔ן הוֹלִ֖יד אֶת בֶּ֣לַע בְּכֹר֑וֹ" (WEB "Benjamin became the father of Bela his firstborn"), a fresh chapter-level Benjamin register distinct from ch.7's military-muster treatment of the same tribe, running an ordinal firstborn-to-fifth-son chain (vv1-2) then Bela's own sons (vv3-5). It closes on an exile-notice formula, "וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י אֵח֑וּד אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֞ם רָאשֵׁ֤י אָבוֹת֙ לְי֣וֹשְׁבֵי גֶ֔בַע וַיַּגְל֖וּם אֶל מָנָֽחַת" (WEB "These are the sons of Ehud. These are the heads of fathers' households of the inhabitants of Geba, who were carried captive to Manahath"), continuing into v7's naming of the exilers, "וְנַעֲמָ֧ן וַאֲחִיָּ֛ה וְגֵרָ֖א ה֣וּא הֶגְלָ֑ם" (WEB "Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, who carried them captive"). The demonstrative-plus-construct-plural-plus-name shape opening v6, "וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י אֵח֑וּד" ("and these are the sons of Ehud"), is byte-identical in its first two words and their accents to MT 6:35’s "וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֑ן" ("and these are the sons of Aaron," = web:1Chr.6.50), which unambiguously introduces, rather than retitles, the descendants named in the rest of that verse -- a forward-pointing control for the identical opening. A genuinely anaphoric use of the same construction does exist at 4:18’s mid-verse "וְאֵ֗לֶּה בְּנֵי֙ בִּתְיָ֣ה" ("and these are the sons of Bithiah"), which does relabel the three sons just named in the verse's own opening clause, but that use sits mid-verse rather than verse-initial like 8:6's. 1Chr's own wording does not settle which pattern v6's opening clause follows, and that gap is held as insufficient_evidence rather than harmonized; the clause immediately following, "אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֞ם רָאשֵׁ֤י אָבוֹת֙ לְי֣וֹשְׁבֵי גֶ֔בַע" ("these are the heads of fathers[-households] of the inhabitants of Geba"), is a bare demonstrative-plus-pronoun summary that can carry the retroactive-summary work on its own regardless of how the first clause is read. The exile/return notice matches this book's settlement-closure device and ends the unit. What follows opens a wholly new genitor and setting, "וְשַׁחֲרַ֗יִם הוֹלִיד֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב" (WEB "Shaharaim became the father of children in the field of Moab").
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv1-5 (Bela's sons) as a row separate from vv6-7's exile notice loses either way: whether v6's opening clause is read anaphorically (as at 4:18, though its normal verse-initial use elsewhere is forward-pointing, cf. MT 6:35 = web:1Chr.6.50) or not, v6's own second clause, ‘these are the heads of fathers[-households]...,’ still summarizes the whole preceding list, binding 1-5 and 6-7 into one register that the exile notice then closes.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a new genitor and geography, "וְשַׁחֲרַ֗יִם הוֹלִיד֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב מִן שִׁלְח֖וֹ אֹתָ֑ם" (WEB "Shaharaim became the father of children in the field of Moab, after he had sent them away"), sharply distinct from the Bela-Ehud line just closed by exile in v6-7. The unit is internally segmented by wife and by descending generation rather than by a single formulaic refrain: Hodesh's sons open "וַיּ֖וֹלֶד מִן חֹ֣דֶשׁ אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ" (v9), Hushim's sons open "וּמֵחֻשִׁ֛ים הוֹלִ֥יד" (v11), and Elpaal's own descendants open "וּבְנֵ֣י אֶלְפַּ֔עַל" (v12) before the list runs on through Beriah's, Shimei's, Shashak's, and Jeroham's sons (vv13-27) without any of those sub-heads restarting a top-level Benjaminite register or attaching its own census total. Two internal demonstrative tags punctuate this stretch without closing it: v10’s "אֵ֥לֶּה בָנָ֖יו רָאשֵׁ֥י אָבֽוֹת" ("these were his sons, heads of fathers[-households],” gloss; WEB “These were his sons, heads of fathers’ households”) closes only the Hodesh sub-list before v11 opens a fresh genitor clause, "וּמֵחֻשִׁ֛ים הוֹלִ֥יד", for the Hushim line, and v13’s "הֵ֚מָּה רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֔וֹת לְיוֹשְׁבֵ֖י אַיָּל֑וֹן" ("they were heads of the fathers[-households] of the inhabitants of Aijalon,” WEB “who were heads of fathers’ households of the inhabitants of Aijalon”) echoes 8:6’s heads-of-fathers-plus-toponym formula "רָאשֵׁ֤י אָבוֹת֙ לְי֣וֹשְׁבֵי גֶ֔בַע" in wording only: unlike v6 it uses the plain pronoun הֵ֚מָּה rather than v6’s double-demonstrative frame, it carries no exile/return notice (v6 continues "וַיַּגְל֖וּם אֶל מָנָֽחַת"), and its own named group, Beriah and Shema, is still being tracked three verses later at v16’s closing tag "בְּנֵ֥י בְרִיעָֽה" and again at v18’s "בְּנֵ֥י אֶלְפָּֽעַל" -- so v13, like v10, is internal punctuation inside the still-running Elpaal complex, not a rival register-close. The whole complex closes only at "אֵ֣לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י אָב֛וֹת לְתֹלְדוֹתָ֖ם רָאשִׁ֑ים אֵ֖לֶּה יָשְׁב֥וּ בִירוּשָׁלִָֽם" (WEB "These were heads of fathers' households throughout their generations, chief men. These lived in Jerusalem"). A samekh in the Masoretic tradition sits right after v28 (single-witness) — tier-3 weak support pointing to the same seam, no more. Kept as one row rather than fragmented at every "sons of X" sub-head, per this book's register-dominant granularity: v10 and v13 are subordinate demonstrative tags that punctuate internally -- v10 closing the Hodesh sub-list, v13 tracking Beriah and Shema forward to v16 and v18 -- while v28 alone is the register-wide closing device. This is not formulaic repetition throughout: v12's building notice, "ה֚וּא בָּנָ֣ה אֶת אוֹנ֔וֹ וְאֶת לֹ֖ד וּבְנֹתֶֽיהָ" ("he built Ono and Lod and its villages," gloss), and v13's conflict clause, "הֵ֥מָּה הִבְרִ֖יחוּ אֶת י֥וֹשְׁבֵי גַֽת" ("they drove out the inhabitants of Gath," gloss), each supply distinct narrative content rather than a repeated formula. What follows opens with a settlement formula on new ground, "וּבְגִבְע֥וֹן יָשְׁב֖וּ" (WEB "The father of Gibeon... lived in Gibeon").
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v13's “heads of fathers[-households] of the inhabitants of Aijalon” -- the strongest internal rival, since its wording echoes 8:6's heads-of-fathers-plus-toponym formula -- loses because it lacks v6's double-demonstrative frame and exile notice, and its own named group (Beriah, Shema) is still being tracked at v16 and v18; splitting at v12's bare “sons of Elpaal” sub-head loses for the same reason as every other internal “sons of X” head in this run: no independent census closure anywhere before v28.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a settlement formula naming a new locale, "וּבְגִבְע֥וֹן יָשְׁב֖וּ אֲבִ֣י גִבְע֑וֹן וְשֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מַעֲכָֽה" (WEB "The father of Gibeon, whose wife's name was Maacah, lived in Gibeon"), the same "lived in" device already used to close 7:28-29. The unit opens as a settlement clause (v29) rather than a genitor clause, followed by an uninflected name list with no verb at all -- v30’s "וּבְנ֥וֹ הַבְּכ֖וֹר עַבְדּ֑וֹן וְצ֥וּר וְקִ֖ישׁ וּבַ֥עַל וְנָדָֽב" and v31’s "וּגְד֥וֹר וְאַחְי֖וֹ וָזָֽכֶר" -- before the first "X fathered Y" clause actually appears at v32, "וּמִקְל֖וֹת הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת שִׁמְאָ֑ה" ("and Mikloth fathered Shimeah"). From there the chain does run continuously through "וְנֵר֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת קִ֔ישׁ וְקִ֖ישׁ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת שָׁא֑וּל וְשָׁא֗וּל" (WEB "Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul") and on to Jonathan's and Merib-baal's descendants, lapsing again only at the close: v37 opens with its own genitor verb ("וּמוֹצָ֖א הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת בִּנְעָ֑א", "and Moza fathered Binea") but finishes on the patrilineal refrain "רָפָ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ אֶלְעָשָׂ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ אָצֵ֥ל בְּנֽוֹ" ("Raphah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son"), and v38 drops the verb again for a counted-sons construction, "וּלְאָצֵל֮ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה בָנִים֒" ("and Azel had six sons"). What actually crosses the v33 seam without a break is not a uniform verb pattern but the absence of any register-head formula there at all: no fresh settlement clause, no ‘sons of X’ construct head, and no demonstrative summary marks v33 itself off from Mikloth's genitor clause in v32. That absence is confined to the v33 seam, however: v35 does open with a genuine verse-initial construct ‘sons of X’ head, "וּבְנֵ֖י מִיכָ֑ה" ("and the sons of Micah," gloss) -- Micah being exactly the son v34 assigns to Merib-baal -- but this head is a list-internal break subordinated to v38's own "these are" close rather than a rival register opening: it falls inside the still-open Ner-Kish-Saul complex that v38 alone terminates, whereas v39's identically-shaped "וּבְנֵ֖י עֵ֣שֶׁק אָחִ֑יו" ("and the sons of Eshek his brother," gloss) falls after that close and so opens the next unit in fact, not merely in form. The criterion distinguishing v35 from v39 is therefore position relative to v38's closing tag, not construct-head shape, which the two share. Samekh marks fall after v32 (near "הֵ֗מָּה נֶ֧גֶד אֲחֵיהֶ֛ם יָשְׁב֥וּ בִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם עִם אֲחֵיהֶֽם", WEB "...in Jerusalem, near their relatives") and after v34 ("וּבֶן יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן מְרִ֣יב בָּ֑עַל וּמְרִ֥יב בַּ֖עַל הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת מִיכָֽה", the Merib-baal/Micah notice, sitting immediately before v35's own construct head) — both single-witness, tier-3; the v34 mark corroborates the list-internal break at v35 conceded above rather than evidencing an unbroken chain across it, and neither mark is treated as counterevidence to keeping this a single row. The unit closes on its own "these are" formula, "כָּל אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י אָצַֽל" (WEB "All these were the sons of Azel"), before v39 opens a new head naming a brother, "וּבְנֵ֖י עֵ֣שֶׁק אָחִ֑יו" (WEB "The sons of Eshek his brother"). This segment is the one place in this part where an in-book resumption is at all arguable — it recurs at 9:35-44 to relaunch the Saul narrative toward ch.10 — noted here only as background on the unit's function, not as evidence for where its own edges fall, which rest entirely on the settlement-formula opening and the "these are" closing already argued.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v33 where the family line narrows onto Ner-Kish-Saul loses, not because an unbroken genitor chain runs from the Gibeon settlement head at v29 (it does not: v29 is a settlement clause and vv30-31 are an uninflected name list), but because no register-head formula of any kind -- settlement, ‘sons of X’, or summary -- marks v33 off from the genitor chain already running since v32's Mikloth clause.

boundary_rationale: Opens "וּבְנֵ֖י עֵ֣שֶׁק אָחִ֑יו אוּלָ֣ם בְּכֹר֔וֹ יְעוּשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וֶֽאֱלִיפֶ֖לֶט הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁי" (WEB "The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third"), a fresh head naming Azel's brother rather than continuing Azel's own line just closed in v38. It closes on "כָּל אֵ֖לֶּה מִבְּנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִֽן" (WEB "All these were of the sons of Benjamin"). The chapter's final pe, trailing v40 (single-witness), lands on this same last line — tier-3 weak support that adds nothing the closing formula did not already establish. That closing formula names "sons of Benjamin" broadly, not just Eshek's or Azel's branch, so it functions as the closing bracket for the whole Benjamin-to-Saul register that began at 8:1 (and, at the tribal level, as far back as 7:6), not merely for this two-verse coda. There is no verse 8:41 to mark a further boundary; the span ends exactly at the chapter and part boundary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 8:39-40 into the Gibeon/Saul unit (8:29-38) loses, because v39 opens with a fresh head naming Azel's brother rather than continuing Azel's own line, and v40's closing formula names "sons of Benjamin" broadly, a scope wider than the Gibeon segment it would be appended to.

boundary_rationale: 9:1 closes the whole genealogical prologue with a finite-verb summary, 'וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הִתְיַחְשׂ֔וּ וְהִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל סֵ֖פֶר מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל' ('and all Israel were registered by genealogy, and behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel,' gloss), then pivots with 'וִיהוּדָ֛ה הָגְל֥וּ לְבָבֶ֖ל בְּמַעֲלָֽם' ('Judah was exiled to Babylon for their unfaithfulness,' gloss; WEB 'carried away captive to Babylon for their disobedience'), supplying the reason the land needed repopulating. Verse 2 opens with a differently-shaped clause, the participial settlement formula "וְהַיּוֹשְׁבִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים" ("the former inhabitants," WEB "the first inhabitants who lived"); its own partitive class-head shape does not match 9:10’s "וּמִן הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים" or 9:14’s "וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" -- that partitive construction first appears one verse later, at 9:3’s "וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יָשְׁב֔וּ מִן בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה" -- nor 9:17’s bare "וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִים֙"; v2’s own four-class tail, "יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים הַלְוִיִּ֖ם וְהַנְּתִינִֽים", previews rather than matches the heads that follow, aligning v2 at least as plausibly with v1 as a shared scope-setting summary as with the class-head series it was read against. The seam therefore rests on v1's own closural weight -- a finite-verb summary plus an exile notice -- consistent with, but not itself proof of, this book's broader category of exile/return notices as register closures (book_strategy_draft.md §2: '5:25-26; 6:15 (MT 5:41); 9:1b'), a single category rather than a repeated two-component formula: MT 5:41's exile notice, "וִיהוֹצָדָ֣ק הָלַ֔ךְ בְּהַגְל֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה אֶת יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בְּיַ֖ד נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּֽר" ("and Jehozadak went, when Yahweh exiled Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar," gloss), is itself a single integrated clause, with the preceding verse, 5:40's "וַעֲזַרְיָה֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת שְׂרָיָ֔ה וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת יְהוֹצָדָֽק" ("and Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak," gloss), a plain genitor clause rather than a paired summary member; and 5:25-26 pairs a trespass/apostasy notice, "וַיִּֽמְעֲל֔וּ בֵּאלֹהֵ֖י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּזְנ֗וּ אַחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י עַמֵּי הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁמִ֥יד אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם" ("and they trespassed against the God of their fathers, and played the harlot after the gods of the peoples of the land," gloss), with the exile notice at v26, not a registration summary parallel to 9:1a -- rather than on any formal echo between v2 and the later class heads. WLC also places a samekh right after v1 (single-witness) -- tier-3 and weak, but sitting exactly at this break. Even so, because v1's exile clause and the Jerusalem/tribal scope-setting that follows in vv. 2-3 share the same historical horizon, a reader could plausibly take vv. 1-3 as one continuous hinge complex rather than isolating v1; I hold the v1/v2 split with moderate confidence for that reason.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping vv. 1-3 as a single combined hinge (exile notice plus return/geographic setting) before the named entries begin at v4 is defensible but sets aside the closural pairing already argued for v1 -- summary clause plus exile notice, of the kind this book uses elsewhere to close a register (5:25-26; 6:15/MT 5:41) -- in favor of a three-verse span.

boundary_rationale: Verse 2 opens with the settlement-register formula "וְהַיּוֹשְׁבִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּאֲחֻזָּתָ֖ם בְּעָרֵיהֶ֑ם" ("the former inhabitants who lived in their possessions in their cities," gloss; WEB "the first inhabitants who lived in their possessions"), followed by a tail listing four groups, "יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים הַלְוִיִּ֖ם וְהַנְּתִינִֽים" (Israel-laity, priests, Levites, temple servants). That list is only a partial scope note for what follows: the priests and Levites do each get their own register (v10, v14), but the temple servants (וְהַנְּתִינִֽים) are a book-wide hapax -- this is their only appearance in 1 Chronicles -- and never receive a register of their own, while the gatekeepers (v17’s וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִים֙) do get one despite not being named in v2 at all. Verse 3, "וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יָשְׁב֔וּ מִן בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה" ("settled in Jerusalem, of the children of Judah," gloss), narrows to the laity and supplies the partitive מִן-plus-בְּנֵי shape before v4 opens the named entries with "עוּתַ֨י בֶּן" ("Uthai son of," gloss). That same partitive shape recurs, in two different sub-forms, inside this span: v5’s "וּמִן הַשִּׁ֣ילוֹנִ֔י" ("and of the Shilonite") is partitive-מִן plus a bare definite gentilic with no בְּנֵי, while only v6’s "וּמִן בְּנֵי זֶ֖רַח" ("and of the sons of Zerah") and v7’s "וּמִן בְּנֵ֖י בִּנְיָמִ֑ן" ("and of the sons of Benjamin") match the partitive-מִן-plus-בְּנֵי shape proper -- two recurrences, not three -- formally the same מִן/וּמִן head decision 058 reads as class-opening at v10 and v14, which likewise classifies v5 by its bare-noun shape rather than as a construct chain. What distinguishes vv5-7 from those later heads is that none of them gets its own closing tag the way the priests do (v13) or the way a fresh register would require: all four named entries from v4 through v8 -- Uthai's Judahite line, the Shiloni group, the Zerah group, and the Benjamin group -- are swept up together under the single summary that closes the whole span, "כָּל אֵ֣לֶּה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים רָאשֵׁ֥י אָב֖וֹת לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם" ("all these men were heads of fathers' households," WEB "heads of fathers' households by their fathers' houses"). I keep the header (2-3) and the named list (4-9) together rather than splitting at v3/v4 or at any of the internal partitive heads, since v9's summary explicitly covers the whole span as one group rather than resetting at each partitive; that close precedes the priests' own register-head at v10 (argued as its own unit below). This same class boundary happens to coincide with a WLC samekh after v9 (single-witness), for what little that tier-3 mark is worth. Because the fourfold list in v2 does less work than first stated -- it previews only three of the four registers ch. 9 actually runs, and the internal vv5-7 partitive heads needed their own argument rather than silent inclusion -- I hold this span at medium rather than high confidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at each of vv5-7's partitive heads -- the strongest internal rival, since they share v10's and v14's מִן/וּמִן class-opening shape -- loses because none of them earns its own closing tag the way the priests do at v13; all of vv4-8 fall under the single summary at v9, which is the stronger, span-wide signal.

boundary_rationale: The priestly class listed in v2’s scope note gets its own register at v10: "וּמִן הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים יְדַֽעְיָ֥ה וִיהוֹיָרִ֖יב וְיָכִֽין" ("and of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin," gloss), a head-formula matching the מִן/וּמִן shape that first appears in this chapter at v3’s "מִן בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה" ("of the children of Judah"), not v2 itself, which has no partitive particle. That shape is not by itself diagnostic of a class head, since it recurs seven times across ch. 9 -- v5, v6, v7, v10, v14, v30, and v32 -- and only two of those, v10 and v14, open a fresh named register. What actually sorts the seven is whether מִן/וּמִן governs a bare definite class noun directly or interposes a בְּנֵי construct before a lineage or gentilic: v10’s "וּמִן הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים" and v14’s "וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" take the bare noun directly, and v5’s "וּמִן הַשִּׁ֣ילוֹנִ֔י" ("and of the Shilonite," gloss) has the same direct-object shape, so 'construct chain' misdescribes it; v6’s "וּמִן בְּנֵי זֶ֖רַח", v7’s "וּמִן בְּנֵ֖י בִּנְיָמִ֑ן", v30’s "וּמִן בְּנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים", and v32’s "וּמִן בְּנֵ֧י הַקְּהָתִ֛י" all interpose בְּנֵי -- v30 even shares its governed noun (הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים, 'the priests') with v10, showing the object noun alone cannot sort them, only the בְּנֵי interposition does. None of the seven is followed by a demonstrative-summary close of its own except the priestly register this row argues, which gets one at v13 below. Named lineages (Azariah, Adaiah, Maasai) run through to v13’s close, "גִּבּ֣וֹרֵי חֵ֔יל מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִֽים" ("able men for the work of the service of God's house," WEB "very able men for the work of the service of God's house"), a summary whose opening actually echoes v9’s closing tag rather than merely paralleling its function: v13’s "וַאֲחֵיהֶ֗ם רָאשִׁים֙ לְבֵ֣ית אֲבוֹתָ֔ם" ("and their brothers, chiefs of the house of their fathers," gloss) shares the brothers-noun (אֲחֵיהֶם), the ר-א-שׁ chiefs construct, and the "house of their fathers" phrase with v9’s "וַאֲחֵיהֶם֙ לְתֹ֣לְדוֹתָ֔ם"..."רָאשֵׁ֥י אָב֖וֹת לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם", making v9 and v13 a matched pair of register-closing tags rather than two differently-worded devices. V14’s fresh head, "וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" ("and of the Levites"), opens the third named class -- itself a bare class noun on the model of v10, not a construct-plus-lineage chain like v6/v7/v30/v32 (v5 shares v10's and v14's direct-object shape instead) -- giving priests a self-contained head-to-summary bracket.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging priests and Levites into one clergy bloc (9:10-16) overlooks that each class gets its own bare-class-noun ‘וּמִן’ head (v10, v14), distinguished from the construct-plus-lineage ‘וּמִן’ phrases at v6, v7, v30, and v32 (v5 shares the bare-noun shape with v10 and v14 rather than the construct-chain group) by whether the partitive governs its noun directly or through an interposed בְּנֵי construct -- not, as v30's shared governed noun with v10 shows, by the identity of the object noun itself.

boundary_rationale: The third class from v2's list opens at v14 with 'וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם שְׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה' ('and of the Levites: Shemaiah,' gloss), matching the 'וּמִן' head pattern of v10. Unlike the priests' and laity's registers, this short list has no closing summary tag; it simply runs out at v16 with a settlement note on Berechiah, 'הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחַצְרֵ֥י נְטוֹפָתִֽי' ('who lived in the villages of the Netophathites,' gloss), before v17's fresh named head 'וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִים֙' ('and the gatekeepers') opens a register with its own historical anecdote (vv. 19-21) absent from the plain Levite list. Because v14's head is the only tier-1 signal doing real work here (the close is by contrast rather than by formula), and because v26 predicates Levite status specifically of the four chief gatekeepers rather than the class as a whole, "אַרְבַּ֨עַת֙ גִּבֹּרֵ֣י הַשֹּׁעֲרִ֔ים הֵ֖ם הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" ("the four chief gatekeepers, they are the Levites," gloss; WEB "the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites"), narrower than a blanket claim -- v18's "הֵ֚מָּה הַשֹּׁ֣עֲרִ֔ים לְמַחֲנ֖וֹת בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי" ("they were the gatekeepers for the camps of the sons of Levi," gloss), the chapter's only other candidate, states a service relation rather than membership, and no verse extends the Levite identification to the gatekeeper class as a whole -- this three-verse class register is nonetheless held with somewhat less certainty than its neighbors.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing 9:14-16 into the gatekeepers' register (9:14-27) as one 'Levites broadly' unit is tempting since v26 calls the gatekeepers Levites, but it erases v17's own head-formula switch -- from the partitive-plus-class-noun "וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" that opens this row to the waw-plus-definite-plural "וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִים֙" that opens the next -- and the origin anecdote at vv19-21 that has no counterpart in vv15-16; v2's own class list does not help this argument, since it never names the gatekeepers at all.

boundary_rationale: V17 opens a fourth named class, 'וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִים֙ שַׁלּ֣וּם וְעַקּ֔וּב' ('and the gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub,' gloss), and the unit stays on this office through a genealogical note on Shallum/Korah, 'וְשַׁלּ֣וּם בֶּן ק֠וֹרֵא בֶּן אֶבְיָסָ֨ף בֶּן קֹ֜רַח וְֽאֶחָ֧יו לְבֵית אָבִ֣יו הַקָּרְחִ֗ים' ('and Shallum son of Kore son of Ebiasaph son of Korah, and his brothers of his father's house, the Korahites,' gloss, v19), a founding-era anecdote naming past overseers, 'וּפִֽינְחָ֣ס בֶּן אֶלְעָזָ֗ר נָגִ֨יד הָיָ֧ה עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם לְפָנִ֖ים' ('Phinehas son of Eleazar was ruler over them in time past,' gloss, v20) and 'זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּ֣ן מְשֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֔ה' ('Zechariah son of Meshelemiah,' gloss, v21), the appointment notice, 'יִסַּ֥ד דָּוִ֛יד וּשְׁמוּאֵ֥ל' ('David and Samuel ordained,' gloss, v22), and general watch-duty statements using collective subjects through v26's 'וְהָיוּ֙ עַל הַלְּשָׁכ֔וֹת וְעַ֥ל הָאֹצְר֖וֹת' ('and were over the rooms and the treasuries,' gloss), closing 'וְלַבֹּ֥קֶר לַבֹּֽקֶר' ('and morning by morning,' WEB '...their duty to open it morning by morning'). V28 shifts register from collective duty-statements to individually itemized custody: "וּמֵהֶ֖ם עַל כְּלֵ֣י הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה" ("and some of them were over the vessels of service," gloss) is the first of a run of partitive clauses -- "וּמֵהֶ֗ם" (v29), "וּמִן בְּנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים" (v30), "וּמַתִּתְיָה֙ מִן הַלְוִיִּ֔ם" (v31, naming an individual), "וּמִן בְּנֵ֧י הַקְּהָתִ֛י" (v32) -- each assigning a specific object (vessels, furniture and spices, the mixing of spices, baked offerings, showbread) to a named or partitive-scoped custodian; only the first two, v28 and v29, share the same consonants and vowels of וּמֵהֶ֖ם while differing in accent -- v28's tipeha "וּמֵהֶ֖ם" against v29's revia "וּמֵהֶ֗ם" (codepoint-confirmed) -- but v30-32 continue the same object-by-custodian pattern with מִן/וּמִן instead. This differs in kind, not merely in vocabulary, from 22-27's collective duty-statements, where the subject is 'they' or 'all of them' acting together on a location or a schedule -- v22's "כֻּלָּ֤ם הַבְּרוּרִים֙" ("all of them who were chosen"), v26's collective "הֵ֗מָּה" over rooms and treasuries, v27's "וְהֵ֥ם עַל הַמַּפְתֵּ֖חַ" ("and they had charge of the key") -- rather than any single verse assigning one object to one custodian. Verses 19-21 are the concentration's exception rather than its rule: v19 places Shallum and his brothers עַ֚ל מְלֶ֣אכֶת הָעֲבוֹדָ֔ה ("over the work of the service," gloss), the same construction v28 later uses for the itemized custodians, עַל כְּלֵ֣י הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה ("over the vessels of the service"); v20's נָגִ֨יד clause assigns Phinehas an individual's office, and v21 assigns Zechariah, זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּ֣ן מְשֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֔ה שֹׁעֵ֥ר פֶּ֖תַח לְאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד ("Zechariah son of Meshelemiah, gatekeeper of the entrance to the tent of meeting," gloss), one named man to one specific post. The real contrast is therefore one of concentration rather than an always-collective-versus-itemized split: vv19-21 read as named-individual, founding-era precedent notices; vv22-27 shift to collective subjects; and vv28-32 return to named or partitive-scoped custodians uniformly, object by object. I hold the split at v27/28 with moderate confidence, since the collective-versus-itemized-custody line, while real throughout 28-32, is a difference of emphasis built up across several verses rather than a single sharp formal marker at the seam itself. Span and confidence are unaffected by this recharacterization.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 9:17-34 together as one undifferentiated gatekeeper unit is a live option, since v26's rooms-and-treasuries duty already anticipates v28's itemized vessel-custody language; but the shift from collective 'they' subjects assigned to locations and schedules (17-27) to individually itemized objects assigned to named or partitive-scoped custodians (28-32) still gives 28-34 its own internal coherence, even though the shared form covers only v28 (tipeha וּמֵהֶ֖ם) and v29 (revia וּמֵהֶ֗ם, differing in accent) before the pattern continues with plain מִן/וּמִן.

boundary_rationale: This unit is built entirely from partitive distribution clauses -- 'וּמֵהֶ֖ם עַל כְּלֵ֣י הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה' (v28, 'and some of them'), 'וּמֵהֶ֗ם מְמֻנִּים֙' (v29, 'and some of them'), 'וּמִן בְּנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים' (v30, 'and of the sons of the priests'), 'וּמַתִּתְיָה֙ מִן הַלְוִיִּ֔ם' (v31, 'and Mattithiah, of the Levites'), and 'וּמִן בְּנֵ֧י הַקְּהָתִ֛י' (v32, 'and of the sons of the Kohathites') -- assigning vessels, furniture, spices, baked offerings, and showbread to named custodians. V33 then opens with its own demonstrative head, "וְאֵ֣לֶּה הַ֠מְשֹׁרְרִים רָאשֵׁ֨י אָב֧וֹת לַלְוִיִּ֛ם" ("and these are the singers, heads of fathers[-households] of the Levites," gloss) -- formally capable of opening a fresh register, per this book's own device matrix, rather than merely continuing the partitive run. But v33's own content is not itemized custody like vv28-32; it gives the singers’ exempt status ("בַּלְּשָׁכֹ֖ת פטירים פְּטוּרִ֑ים", "in the chambers, free [from other duties]") and a general day-and-night duty statement, and it supplies no distinct closing tag of its own before v34's double summary follows immediately -- Read together, vv33-34 form a two-verse closing bracket for the whole 28-32 custody run: v33 names the last group (the singers) inside the same 'heads of fathers[-households] of the Levites' vocabulary that v34 then generalizes into the complex's summary, rather than v33 standing as an independent register head with its own separate unit. This closing pattern reproduces 8:28's "אֵ֣לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י אָב֛וֹת לְתֹלְדוֹתָ֖ם רָאשִׁ֑ים אֵ֖לֶּה יָשְׁב֥וּ בִירוּשָׁלִָֽם" almost word for word, which in ch. 8 likewise precedes a Gibeon/Saul segment starting "וּבְגִבְע֥וֹן יָשְׁב֖וּ" ("and in Gibeon lived," 8:29). The shared verb יָשְׁב֥וּ at this row's own 9:34/9:35 seam is byte-identical -- root, form, and merkha accent alike, confirmed on both 9:34's closing "יָשְׁב֥וּ" and 9:35's opening "יָשְׁב֥וּ" -- the catchword pivot marking a register-closing demonstrative-summary frame passing into a settlement-head prepositional-phrase-plus-perfect, not evidence that the two units continue one another. The parallel 8:28/8:29 seam shares the same root and form but not the same accent: 8:28's closing יָשְׁב֥וּ carries merkha while 8:29's opening יָשְׁב֖וּ carries tipeha (codepoint-confirmed); the catchword-pivot argument does not depend on accentual identity there either, since it turns on the shift from closing demonstrative-plus-verb to opening preposition-plus-verb, not on the accent. This same seam is exactly where WLC places a pe (single-witness) -- tier-3 support, but right on target. A samekh also marks 9:32 (single-witness), tier-3 support for the rival 9:28-32 seam that this row's head-and-catchword form argument outweighs; it is disclosed rather than treated as counterevidence, matching the annotation already given the agreeing 9:34 pe.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 9:28-34 as background notes folded into the Saul-line unit that follows (9:28-44) ignores the difference in form at the seam, not a difference in vocabulary: v34 closes with a demonstrative-summary frame, "אֵ֖לֶּה יָשְׁב֥וּ בִירוּשָׁלִָֽם" ("these lived in Jerusalem"), the same register-closing device that ends 8:28, while v35 opens with a locative prepositional phrase plus a perfect verb, "וּבְגִבְע֛וֹן יָשְׁב֥וּ" ("and in Gibeon lived"), the same settlement-head device that opens 8:29. The two clauses do share the verb יָשְׁב֥וּ -- byte-identical root, form, and accent at this row's own 9:34/9:35 seam -- but that repetition is the catchword pivot marking the seam, not evidence that the two units continue one another: a closing demonstrative-plus-verb and an opening preposition-plus-verb are different constructions built on the same root, which is precisely how the parallel 8:28/8:29 seam also works, there sharing root and form while differing in accent (merkha at 8:28, tipeha at 8:29).

boundary_rationale: V35 opens with 'וּבְגִבְע֛וֹן יָשְׁב֥וּ אֲבִֽי גִבְע֖וֹן יעואל יְעִיאֵ֑ל וְשֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מַעֲכָֽה' ('and in Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon...and his wife's name was Maacah,' gloss), reproducing 8:29's 'וּבְגִבְע֥וֹן יָשְׁב֖וּ אֲבִ֣י גִבְע֑וֹן וְשֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מַעֲכָֽה' clause for clause, differing only in adding a name for 'the father of Gibeon' (יעואל יְעִיאֵ֑ל, Kethiv-Qere, cf. Jeiel) that 8:29 lacks. The Saul line then re-runs fourteen named individuals across thirteen links -- Ner, Kish, Saul, Jonathan, Merib-baal, Micah, Ahaz, Jarah, Zimri, Moza, Binea, Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel -- the thirteen links mixing הוליד-verb steps with nominal joins such as v40's "וּבֶן יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן מְרִ֣יב בָּ֑עַל" ("and the son of Jonathan, Merib-baal," gloss) and v43's threefold בְנ֛וֹ chain ("וּרְפָיָ֥ה בְנ֛וֹ אֶלְעָשָׂ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ אָצֵ֥ל בְּנֽוֹ", "Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son," gloss), distinct from the nine הוליד tokens actually printed across 9:35-44 (own token sweep), of which the ninth, at v38's "וּמִקְל֖וֹת הוֹלִ֣יד", belongs to the Mikloth side-branch outside this line, leaving eight on the Saul line proper -- down to v44's close, matching 8:38's close 'כָּל אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י אָצַֽל' (WEB there: 'all these were the sons of Azel'; here: 'these were the sons of Azel') -- the two witnesses differ slightly in wording (8:38 adds a 'all,' 9:44 omits it), and several descendant names carry variant spellings between the two lists, e.g. 8:31's 'וָזָֽכֶר' (Zecher) against 9:37's 'וּזְכַרְיָ֖ה' (Zechariah), and 8:36's 'אֶת יְהוֹעַדָּ֔ה' (Jehoaddah) against 9:42's 'אֶת יַעְרָ֔ה' (Jarah) -- hygiene: not harmonized here. A further divergence bears on the line itself rather than mere spelling, and is witness-scoped rather than a plain hygiene variant: 8:35 lists Ahaz among Micah's sons, "וּבְנֵ֖י מִיכָ֑ה פִּית֥וֹן וָמֶ֖לֶךְ וְתַאְרֵ֥עַ וְאָחָֽז", while MT 9:41's parallel list carries only three names and omits him, "וּבְנֵ֖י מִיכָ֑ה פִּית֥וֹן וָמֶ֖לֶךְ וְתַחְרֵֽעַ" (WEB 9:41, by contrast, already supplies him: "The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz."), yet 9:42 opens "וְאָחָז֙ הוֹלִ֣יד" ("and Ahaz fathered") as though he had just been named -- the ch. 9 chain presupposes a son MT 9:41's own wording does not supply, an MT-only gap that WEB's fuller witness closes, disclosed here rather than harmonized. This near-verbatim resumption relaunches Saul's household immediately before ch. 10's death narrative, which opens with a waw-plus-fronted-subject-plus-niphal-perfect setting clause sharing no genealogical vocabulary, "וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים נִלְחֲמ֣וּ" ("and the Philistines fought," not itself a wayyiqtol; the chapter's first wayyiqtol is the next clause's "וַיָּ֑נָס", "and [they] fled"). WLC's own mark inventory shows a pe right after v44 (single-witness), sitting exactly at this register-to-narrative hinge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 9:35-44 as the narrative's own opening (starting the Saul story at 9:35 rather than 10:1) loses the register form (toledot-style begetting chain, closing 'these are the sons of' tag) that 9:35-44 shares with 8:29-38 and not with ch. 10's finite-verb battle report.

boundary_rationale: Ch. 10 opens with a backgrounding setting clause sharing no vocabulary with the genealogy just closed: waw-conjunctive plus fronted subject plus niphal perfect, "וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים נִלְחֲמ֣וּ בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל" ("and the Philistines fought against Israel," gloss) -- not itself a wayyiqtol, though the chapter's own first wayyiqtol follows immediately in the same verse, "וַיָּ֑נָס אִֽישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙" ("and the men of Israel fled," gloss). A fronted-subject perfect opening a scene is, if anything, a stronger discourse-initial signal than a bare wayyiqtol continuation would have been, since it explicitly introduces a new grammatical subject (the Philistines) rather than simply carrying forward the previous clause's subject -- sharpening rather than softening the seam this row argues for. The unit tracks one continuous action -- pursuit, wounding, Saul's suicide by sword (vv. 1-5), the summary 'וַיָּ֤מָת שָׁאוּל֙ וּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָ֔יו וְכָל בֵּית֖וֹ יַחְדָּ֥ו מֵֽתוּ' (v6, 'so Saul died with his three sons, and all his house died together,' gloss) -- and closes with the towns' abandonment forming an inclusio with the opening flight: 'וַיַּעַזְב֤וּ עָרֵיהֶם֙ וַיָּנֻ֔סוּ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בָּהֶֽם' (v7, 'they abandoned their cities and fled, and the Philistines came and lived in them,' WEB similar). V8's 'וַיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת' ('the next day came,' gloss) is a classic day-shift formula introducing a new scene at the corpses, marking the next unit's edge rather than this one's. Consistent with that, WLC's samekh count includes one immediately following v7 (single-witness). Two further samekh marks fall at 10:4 and 10:5 (both single-witness), interior to this row's own 10:1-7 span; both track combat-scene beats finer than the row -- Saul's request to his armor-bearer (v4) and the armor-bearer's refusal (v5) -- and, being tier-3, leave the 10:1-7 boundary intact, matching the treatment rows 070 and 071 give their own interior marks.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through v8 on the theory that the corpse-stripping is simply the battle's aftermath loses the explicit 'next day' time-jump that separates same-day combat (1-7) from the following day's looting (8-12).

boundary_rationale: V8's day-shift, 'וַיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְפַשֵּׁ֖ט אֶת הַֽחֲלָלִ֑ים' ('and it happened, the next day, the Philistines came to strip the slain,' gloss), opens a new scene at the battlefield, distinct from the same-day combat scene argued for the preceding unit. The Philistines' trophy display, 'וַיַּ֨פְשִׁיטֻ֔הוּ' (v9, 'and they stripped him,' gloss) through 'וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ֙ אֶת כֵּלָ֔יו' (v10, 'and they put his armor,' gloss), is answered once Jabesh-Gilead hears of it, 'וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ כֹּ֖ל יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד' (v11, 'and all Jabesh Gilead heard,' gloss), running through the honor burial and closing notice 'וַיָּצ֖וּמוּ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים' (v12, 'and they fasted seven days,' gloss). V13 opens with the same wayyiqtol death-notice verb already used at v6 -- "וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁא֗וּל" here against v6's "וַיָּ֤מָת שָׁאוּל֙" -- and the wayyiqtol chain does not in fact break at this seam: v14 supplies two further consecutives, "וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ" ("and he killed him") and "וַיַּסֵּב֙" ("and he turned over"). What actually marks v13 off as a distinct commentary unit rather than a continuation of the burial notice is the retrospective, causal material riding on that resumed wayyiqtol: the beth-of-cause clause "בְּמַֽעֲלוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָעַ֣ל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה" ("for his trespass which he committed against Yahweh"), the relative clause "עַל דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא שָׁמָ֑ר" ("because of Yahweh's word, which he did not keep"), and the necromancy notice "וְגַם לִשְׁא֥וֹל בָּא֖וֹב לִדְרֽוֹשׁ" ("and also to ask of a medium, to inquire," gloss; WEB keeps both infinitives, "and also because he asked counsel of one who had a familiar spirit, to inquire") -- none of which has any counterpart in vv8-12's battlefield-and-burial report, which never pauses to explain why Saul died, only what was done to and for his body. The second infinitive's root recurs at 10:14 in דָרַ֥שׁ ("וְלֹֽא דָרַ֥שׁ", "and he did not inquire," gloss), binding 13-14 to each other by root repetition and away from 10:8-12, which sharpens rather than weakens this row's far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the burial account together with the closing verdict as a single 'aftermath and evaluation' block obscures that v13 restates rather than advances the story: it resumes v6's own death-notice verb only to wrap it in causal and relative clauses that explain the death rather than report new events, a function distinct from vv8-12's battlefield-and-burial action even though both stretches share the wayyiqtol chain.

boundary_rationale: The claim that a wayyiqtol chain drops out here does not survive a check of the verbs themselves: v13 ("וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁא֗וּל") and v6 ("וַיָּ֤מָת שָׁאוּל֙") share the identical qal wayyiqtol form, and v14 continues on with two more of its own, "וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ" and "וַיַּסֵּב֙". What genuinely distinguishes this two-verse unit is not a broken chain but a resumed one: v13 picks the v6 death-report back up only to encase it in causal subordination, converting bare event-narration into the Chronicler's own retrospective verdict: "וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁא֗וּל בְּמַֽעֲלוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָעַ֣ל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה" (v13, "so Saul died for his trespass which he committed against Yahweh," gloss), citing 'עַל דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא שָׁמָ֑ר' ('because of Yahweh's word, which he did not keep,' gloss), and his consultation of a medium, 'וְגַם לִשְׁא֥וֹל בָּא֖וֹב לִדְרֽוֹשׁ' ('and also to ask of a medium, to inquire,' gloss; WEB keeps both infinitives, 'asked counsel of one who had a familiar spirit, to inquire'), then closing v14 with the theological point of the whole unit, 'וְלֹֽא דָרַ֥שׁ בַּֽיהוָ֖ה וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וַיַּסֵּב֙ אֶת הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה לְדָוִ֖יד בֶּן יִשָֽׁי' ('he did not inquire of Yahweh, so he killed him and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse,' gloss). The second infinitive of v13b, לִדְרֽוֹשׁ, and v14a's דָרַ֥שׁ share the same root ד-ר-שׁ, a tier-1 cohesion signal binding the two verses that the row's own quotations already place side by side without naming it. This is the passage's evaluative close: the resumed wayyiqtol circles back to the plain fact reported in full already at v6 ('וַיָּ֤מָת שָׁאוּל֙ וּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָ֔יו וְכָל בֵּית֖וֹ יַחְדָּ֥ו מֵֽתוּ'), not to add plot but, framed by the causal and relative clauses wrapped around it, to render verdict and pivot the kingdom to David, priming the David narrative that follows. The chapter's -- and this whole part's -- final WLC mark is a pe placed right after v14 (single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating these two verses as the final beats of the preceding burial narrative misses that, although the wayyiqtol chain itself runs straight through the seam, these verses re-narrate the death already reported at v6 wrapped in causal and relative commentary rather than advancing the action -- a distinct evaluative function the surrounding narrative units lack.

boundary_rationale: The chapter opens with a wayyiqtol gathering formula, וַיִּקָּבְצ֧וּ כָֽל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל (gloss: 'and all Israel gathered'), matching the device matrix's scene-shift pattern and launching the tribal address to David quoted at WEB 11:1-2 ('we are your bone and your flesh' ... 'you shall be shepherd of my people Israel'). The scene is a single covenant-and-anointing event at Hebron: elders arrive (v3a), David 'made a covenant with them ... before Yahweh' (WEB 11:3), and the unit is sealed by a source-citation closure, כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד שְׁמוּאֵֽל (gloss: 'according to the word of Yahweh by the hand of Samuel'), answering the tribal speech's appeal in v2 to what 'Yahweh your God said to you.' The WLC places a samekh after v3 (single-witness) -- a tier-3 nod toward the same pause, offered only as background agreement, never as the reason for it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 11:1-9 as one undivided 'David becomes king' scene loses the tier-1 seam at the wayyelek relocation to Jerusalem in v4, which shifts the unit from covenant-speech to conquest-report.
