boundary_rationale: David's relocation carries its own wayyiqtol verb, וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ דָּוִ֧יד וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם (gloss: 'and David and all Israel went to Jerusalem'), replacing Hebron with Jebus as the scene's location (WEB 11:4) and opening a self-contained conquest report: the Jebusites' taunt and Zion's capture (5-6), David's residence in the stronghold and Joab's repair of the rest of the city (7-8). The unit closes on an editorial growth-notice rather than a register formula -- David 'grew greater and greater,' וַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עִמּֽוֹ (gloss: 'and Yahweh of Armies was with him', WEB 11:9b) -- a favor-summary clause with no counterpart running into v10, where the register-superscription vocabulary takes over instead. That same paragraph break earns a pe after v9 in the WLC (single-witness), tracking -- but not supplying -- what the wayyelek relocation at v4 already established.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv4-9 into the Hebron scene as 11:1-9 in one row erases the wayyelek relocation seam and mismatches two different rhetorical modes, covenant speech versus conquest report.

boundary_rationale: Verse 10 carries superscription vocabulary distinct from what follows: וְאֵ֨לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֤י הַגִּבּוֹרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֔יד (gloss: 'and these are the heads of the mighty men whom David had'), a general encomium tying the whole catalogue's legitimacy to kingship ('together with all Israel, to make him king') and closing with its own citation formula, כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (gloss: 'according to the word of Yahweh concerning Israel', WEB 11:10b). This same citation-template, כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה [X] ("according to the word of Yahweh..."), also closes v3's anointing notice, "כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד שְׁמוּאֵֽל" ("according to Yahweh's word by the hand of Samuel"), seven verses earlier; a book-wide sweep finds the exact consonantal bigram כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה at three loci -- 11:3, 11:10, and 15:15 -- but only two of them share the same accentuation: 11:3's כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה (merkha, tipeha) and 11:10's כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה (merkha, tipeha) are accent-exact matches, while 15:15's כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (munah, etnahta) is a consonantal but not accent-exact match (codepoint-confirmed). The bracket argument rests on the accent-exact pair, 11:3 and 11:10, so the two occurrences bracketing 11:3-10 are not incidental. Read this way, v10 is a Janus-faced verse: its closing formula looks backward, bracketing the whole accession-and-covenant narrative from v3’s anointing, while its own opening ("וְאֵ֨לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֤י הַגִּבּוֹרִים֙") and v11’s forward launch into the named roster carry it forward into the mighty-men catalogue. I hold it as its own row on the forward-facing strength of its own heading vocabulary and v11’s list-specific launch, disclosing the backward echo as a live competing reading rather than treating v10 as a purely forward-facing superscription. Verse 11 reopens with a narrower, list-specific heading ('these are the number of the mighty men') that launches the named roster with Jashobeam -- a different headword (number, rather than heads) and a different rhetorical register. A samekh trails v10 in the WLC (single-witness), consistent with but not the basis for the pause posited here between the two headings. A pe also marks 11:9 (single-witness), this row's own near edge; it is tier-3 support against the backward-closure rival that would fold this verse into the accession-and-covenant narrative, disclosed here without letting it drive the boundary or lift confidence above medium. Confidence is capped at medium because reading both 'these are' clauses as one compound superscription spanning 11:10-47 is a genuinely live alternative.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v10 as the shared opening clause of one long 11:10-47 heading, rather than its own row, is defensible but effaces the vocabulary shift this row isolates. A second rival, reading v10 primarily as a backward-facing closure of the 11:3-10 accession-and-covenant narrative (its citation formula brackets v3's own כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה notice), is disclosed above rather than adopted, since v10's own heading vocabulary and v11's forward launch still carry more weight for where the mighty-men catalogue itself begins.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:1Chr.15.15 (codepoint comparison; book-wide sweep confirms no other consonantal hits)

boundary_rationale: The list-specific heading וְאֵ֛לֶּה מִסְפַּ֥ר הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד (gloss: 'and these are the number of the mighty men whom David had', WEB 11:11a) introduces the mighty men generally (הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים), not 'the Three' as such; the rank title that immediately follows Jashobeam's name carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere split, an unpointed 'השלושים' ("the thirty") under the pointed 'הַשָּׁ֣לִישִׁ֔ים' ("the officers"/"the third-rank men") -- neither reading names 'the three,' and the split is disclosed here rather than run together. The unit's first mention of a three-group comes one verse later, at v12's 'ה֖וּא בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים' ("he was among the three mighty men"); the numeral בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה is absolute -- no article, no dagesh in the shin -- codepoint-identical in shape to the anarthrous שְֽׁלוֹשָׁה֩ at v15, which this row calls anarthrous and partitive three sentences later. 'Definite' is reserved below for v18's articular הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֜ה and v19's true construct שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַגִּבּוֹרִֽים. Continuing directly into Eleazar's Pas-dammim battle (12-14) and the water-libation episode: 'three of the thirty' -- וַיֵּרְד֡וּ שְֽׁלוֹשָׁה֩ מִן הַשְּׁלוֹשִׁ֨ים (gloss: 'and three of the thirty went down', WEB 11:15) -- is anarthrous and partitive, three men drawn out of a larger Thirty, not yet the definite collective; that definite anchor arrives three verses later at v18's 'וַיִּבְקְע֨וּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֜ה' ("and the three broke through"), and the episode's climax pours the water 'to Yahweh': וְלֹֽא אָבָ֤ה דָוִיד֙ לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֔ם וַיְנַסֵּ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖ם לַיהוָֽה (gloss: 'but David would not drink them, and poured them out to Yahweh', WEB 11:18b). Per the inset rule, this narrative episode stays inside its host entry because it is syntactically resumed by the unit's own closing formula, אֵ֣לֶּה עָשׂ֔וּ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַגִּבּוֹרִֽים (gloss: 'these things did the three mighty men', WEB 11:19b) -- the same "these did X" template that closes Benaiah's separate entry at v24, 'אֵ֣לֶּה עָשָׂ֔ה בְּנָיָ֖הוּ בֶּן יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע' ("these things did Benaiah son of Jehoiada") -- which loops back to and completes the roster entry opened in v11 rather than opening anything new. Verse 20 begins a fresh named figure outside 'the three' proper, giving the unit's far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating the water-drawing episode (15-19) as its own narrative decision would sever the closing 'these did the three mighty men' from the entry it summarizes, contrary to the inset-stays-inside default.

boundary_rationale: Abishai's entry opens with a fresh named subject, וְאַבְשַׁ֣י אֲחִֽי יוֹאָ֗ב (gloss: 'and Abishai, brother of Joab', WEB 11:20a), outside the closed 'Three' unit, and closes with וְלוֹ שֵׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁלוֹשָֽׁה (v20b, 'and he had a name among the three,' gloss; the witness prints this against an immediately preceding unpointed ketiv, 'ולא,' a negation -- 'and he had NO name among the three' -- so the possessive reading followed here is the qere, disclosed rather than run together with the consonantal text) and וְעַד הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֖ה לֹֽא בָֽא (v21b, 'but to the three he did not come', gloss). Benaiah's entry, introduced separately below in this row's span, answers both members of that pair rather than only one: v24 closes his parallel feats with the matching positive clause, וְלוֹ שֵׁ֖ם בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים (gloss: 'and he had a name among the three mighty men', WEB 11:24b), and v25a supplies the matching negative clause, וְאֶל הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֖ה לֹא בָ֑א (gloss: 'but he did not attain to the three'), immediately before the unit's final verdict, וַיְשִׂימֵ֥הוּ דָוִ֖יד עַל מִשְׁמַעְתּֽוֹ (gloss: 'and David set him over his guard', WEB 11:25b). The refrain is therefore a four-member ABAB alternation across the two entries -- 'had a name among the three' at 20b and 24b, 'did not attain to the three' at 21b and 25a -- not a chiasm, and reading it correctly paired binds the two heroes into one runner-up pairing more tightly than a single repeated clause would, distinct from both the closed Three (11-19) and the paratactic roster beginning at v26, which opens its own construct-plural rubric, "וְגִבּוֹרֵ֖י הַחֲיָלִ֑ים" ("and the mighty men of the forces," gloss), closed by etnahta before the first name, עֲשָׂה (Asahel), begins -- so that register is not headless at its own outer edge, even though it then runs paratactically with no further heading. A samekh falls after v21 in the WLC (single-witness) -- a list-internal mark that could support splitting Abishai from Benaiah, but it is tier-3 corroboration only and does not override the four-member refrain this row treats as decisive; a second samekh, after v25, sits right where this row ends. Correcting the refrain from a single mispaired clause to the four-member alternation strengthens rather than weakens the case for holding vv20-25 together, which is reflected in a modest rise in confidence from medium_low to medium.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Abishai (20-21) and Benaiah (22-25) into separate rows is the strongest rival reading, supported by the intervening samekh, but it breaks apart the two entries' four-member ABAB refrain -- 'had a name among the three' (20b, 24b) answered by 'did not attain to the three' (21b, 25a) -- that binds them into one pairing rather than two independent entries.

boundary_rationale: The register shifts form at v26 from individuated hero-narratives to a flat patronymic-and-gentilic list: וְגִבּוֹרֵ֖י הַחֲיָלִ֑ים עֲשָׂה אֵל֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב (gloss: 'and the mighty men of the forces: Asahel, brother of...', WEB 11:26a) opens with its own construct-plural rubric before the names begin, so the register is not headless at its own outer edge -- what it lacks is any fresh heading formula recurring inside vv26-47 to re-open a new register. The word בְּנֵ֗י ('sons of') does recur four times in this stretch (token sweep of 11:26-47), not three: verse-initially at v34 (בְּנֵ֗י הָשֵׁם֙ הַגִּ֣זוֹנִ֔י, 'the sons of Hashem the Gizonite'), inside a toponym at v31 (מִגִּבְעַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן, 'from Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin' -- the clearest non-head of the four), and mid-verse at v44 (בְּנֵ֖י חוֹתָ֥ם הָעֲרֹעֵרִֽי, 'the sons of Hotham the Aroerite') and v46 (בְּנֵ֣י אֶלְנָ֑עַם, 'the sons of Elnaam') -- but in each case it functions as an appositional patronymic (or, at v31, a place-name element) identifying one soldier's own family or hometown within a single name-entry, not as a construct-plural head re-launching the register the way 7:1's or 8:1's 'sons of X' openers do; none of the four is followed by its own sub-list or its own closing tag. The catalogue continues paratactically, name after name, through the Reubenite and Ammonite entries to the chapter's final trio, אֱלִיאֵ֣ל וְעוֹבֵ֔ד וְיַעֲשִׂיאֵ֖ל הַמְּצֹבָיָֽה (gloss: 'Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite', WEB 11:47), where the list simply stops rather than closing with a formula; the chapter boundary itself supplies the far edge, and the WLC's own pe after v47 (single-witness) happens to land on the identical spot. The WLC marks this stretch densely with samekh at nearly every name-cluster, including doubled samekh at both 11:32 and 11:44 (single-witness); per the marker policy this dense field tracks list-item granularity finer than the row and does not drive a split -- the register, not the name, is the unit here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the roster at every samekh, or at the two doubled-samekh verses specifically, would multiply rows without any tier-1 seam: the four internal 'sons of X' patronymics at vv31, 34, 44, and 46 identify individual soldiers, hometowns, or lineages rather than re-heading the register, and no other new heading, subject, or verb-form recurs between 26 and 47; the participial epithet at 11:39, נֹשֵׂ֕א כְּלֵ֖י יוֹאָ֥ב ("armor-bearer of Joab"), and the rank-and-retinue notice at 11:42, רֹ֛אשׁ לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֖י וְעָלָ֥יו שְׁלוֹשִֽׁים ("chief of the Reubenites, and over him thirty"), are the two candidates closest to a heading in the stretch, and neither re-heads the register.

boundary_rationale: A fresh 'these are' register head opens the chapter at a new locale, וְאֵ֗לֶּה הַבָּאִ֤ים אֶל דָּוִיד֙ לְצִ֣יקְלַ֔ג (gloss: 'and these are those coming to David at Ziklag', WEB 12:1a; identical numbering here, no dual-cite required), replacing the previous roster's flat parataxis with a dated fugitive-period frame ('while he was a fugitive from Saul the son of Kish') around a named Benjaminite kinship group. This row runs into the offset zone at WEB 12:4, where the combined MT 12:4+12:5 supplies Ishmaiah and the four names after him (web:1Chr.12.4 = oshb:1Chr.12.4 (MT) + oshb:1Chr.12.5 (MT)), and continues through the dual-cited interior verses web:1Chr.12.5 = oshb:1Chr.12.6 (MT), אֶלְעוּזַ֤י וִירִימוֹת֙ וּבְעַלְיָ֣ה וּשְׁמַרְיָ֔הוּ וּשְׁפַטְיָ֖הוּ החריפי הַחֲרוּפִֽי (gloss: 'Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite'), and web:1Chr.12.6 = oshb:1Chr.12.7 (MT), אֶלְקָנָ֡ה וְ֠יִשִּׁיָּהוּ וַעֲזַרְאֵ֧ל וְיוֹעֶ֛זֶר וְיָשָׁבְעָ֖ם הַקָּרְחִֽים (gloss: 'Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites'); the sub-list then closes without any new formula on its final two names, web:1Chr.12.7 = oshb:1Chr.12.8 (MT), וְיוֹעֵאלָ֧ה וּזְבַדְיָ֛ה בְּנֵ֥י יְרֹחָ֖ם מִן הַגְּדֽוֹר (gloss: 'and Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham, from Gedor'). The following verse pivots to a different tribe with a partitive מִן phrase governing a niphal perfect, web:1Chr.12.8 = oshb:1Chr.12.9 (MT), 'וּמִן הַגָּדִ֡י נִבְדְּל֣וּ' ('and from the Gadite(s), they separated,' gloss -- a gentilic singular collective, not the bare tribal name), giving this row's far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the Gadites to WEB 12:15 would merge two tribally distinct sub-registers that the text itself separates with a fresh partitive-plus-niphal-perfect opening at web:1Chr.12.8 = oshb:1Chr.12.9 (MT).

boundary_rationale: A new subject-marking construct opens this row, web:1Chr.12.8 = oshb:1Chr.12.9 (MT), וּמִן הַגָּדִ֡י נִבְדְּל֣וּ אֶל דָּוִיד֩ (gloss: 'and from the Gad they separated to David'), pivoting from the Benjaminite archers to a Gadite contingent 'in the stronghold in the wilderness' with its own ordinal-ranked captain list running chief through eleventh. The group then receives a double 'these' closure rather than a single one: a rank-summary, web:1Chr.12.14 = oshb:1Chr.12.15 (MT), אֵ֥לֶּה מִבְּנֵי גָ֖ד רָאשֵׁ֣י הַצָּבָ֑א (gloss: 'these were of the sons of Gad, heads of the army'), immediately followed by a narrative coda about the same men's Jordan-crossing feat, web:1Chr.12.15 = oshb:1Chr.12.16 (MT), אֵ֣לֶּה הֵ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבְר֤וּ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ (gloss: 'these are they who crossed the Jordan'). Per the inset rule, the second 'these' does not open a new subject and stays inside the Gad entry as an appended feat-report. The WLC's samekh after web:1Chr.12.15 = oshb:1Chr.12.16 (MT) (single-witness) sits at this same spot, background agreement rather than a reason, just before Benjamin-and-Judah's arrival opens the next scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the rank-summary (v14) and the Jordan-crossing coda (v15) as two separate decisions would split one group's profile at a non-subject-changing internal 'these', against the inset-stays-inside default.

boundary_rationale: The arrival of a mixed Benjamin-Judah band is announced with a bare wayyiqtol rather than any 'these are' formula, web:1Chr.12.16 = oshb:1Chr.12.17 (MT), וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ מִן בְּנֵ֤י בִנְיָמִן֙ וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה (gloss: 'and they came, from the sons of Benjamin and Judah'), shifting the passage from list to scene: David tests their loyalty with direct speech (WEB 12:17), and the Spirit 'clothes' Amasai for an oracular reply, web:1Chr.12.18 = oshb:1Chr.12.19 (MT), וְר֣וּחַ לָבְשָׁ֗ה אֶת עֲמָשַׂי֮ (gloss: 'and the Spirit clothed Amasai'). The scene resolves within that same verse: David 'received them, and made them captains of the band', web:1Chr.12.18 = oshb:1Chr.12.19 (MT), וַיְקַבְּלֵ֣ם דָּוִ֔יד וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּרָאשֵׁ֥י הַגְּדֽוּד. A pe in the WLC (single-witness) marks this identical seam after web:1Chr.12.18 = oshb:1Chr.12.19 (MT), noted only as background agreement ahead of the Manasseh notices that follow.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping this dialogue scene with the surrounding Gad or Manasseh list-notices would collapse a distinct speech-and-response form into flanking rosters that carry no comparable direct discourse.

boundary_rationale: A retrospective Manasseh notice opens with its own transition, web:1Chr.12.19 = oshb:1Chr.12.20 (MT), וּמִֽמְּנַשֶּׁ֞ה נָפְל֣וּ עַל דָּוִ֗יד (gloss: 'and from Manasseh they fell to David'), recalling the earlier Philistine-campaign episode where Manasseh could not help him. A second, near-identical opening immediately follows for a separate, later group of Ziklag-period defectors, web:1Chr.12.20 = oshb:1Chr.12.21 (MT), בְּלֶכְתּ֣וֹ אֶל צִֽיקְלַ֗ג נָפְל֣וּ עָלָ֣יו מִֽמְּנַשֶּׁ֡ה (gloss: 'as he went to Ziklag, some from Manasseh fell to him'), named individually and credited with helping 'against the band of raiders' (WEB 12:21). The pointed form נָפְל֣וּ that opens both notices is rare: a book-wide sweep finds it in only one other place, 5:22's pausal נָפָ֔לוּ (a different accentual form of the same root), so the exact shared form binding vv19-20 to each other is essentially unique to this pair, and that scarcity -- not the closing verse below -- is what individuates the two Manasseh notices as one row rather than the closing verse's reach, which is broader than this pair alone. That closing verse, web:1Chr.12.22 = oshb:1Chr.12.23 (MT), כִּ֚י לְעֶת י֣וֹם בְּי֔וֹם יָבֹ֥אוּ עַל דָּוִ֖יד לְעָזְר֑וֹ עַד לְמַחֲנֶ֥ה גָד֖וֹל כְּמַחֲנֵ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים (gloss: 'for at the time, day by day, they came to David to help him, until a great army, like the camp of God'), does generalize beyond Manasseh -- it is a summary bracket for the whole 12:1-22 accession section, shared equally by the Benjaminite archers and the Gadites earlier in the chapter, not a warrant exclusive to this pair -- so it is read here only as a description of what that verse does for the section as a whole, not as the ground for binding vv19-22 specifically. The עַל דָּוִ֗יד phrase (revia on the name) inside v19/MT 12:20 shares its consonants, but not its accent, with two later attestations: MT 12:23's עַל דָּוִ֖יד (tipeha), sitting mid-verse at words 6-7 of the verse's thirteen, not at its close (the close is כְּמַחֲנֵ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים); and MT 12:24's עַל דָּוִ֖יד (tipeha), at words 6-8 of בָּ֥אוּ עַל דָּוִ֖יד ("they came to David," gloss), following that verse's own register head, וְ֠אֵלֶּה מִסְפְּרֵ֞י רָאשֵׁ֤י הֶֽחָלוּץ֙ לַצָּבָ֔א ("and these are the numbers of the heads of the armed for war," gloss), rather than opening it. Both later attestations are governed by a different verb (arrival, not 'fell to' or 'came to help'), so consonantal recurrence alongside נָפְל֣וּ's scarcity is loose corroboration rather than a clean two-point inclusio on its own. The WLC's pe after web:1Chr.12.22 = oshb:1Chr.12.23 (MT) (single-witness) lands on this same seam, tier-3 background agreement ahead of the census's own 'these are the numbers' heading.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the two Manasseh notices (19 vs. 20-22) into separate rows is defensible given their distinct historical referents, but both open with the same rare pointed form נָפְל֣וּ -- attested elsewhere in the book only in the different, pausal form at 5:22 -- favoring a single row over the section-wide closing verse, which binds Manasseh no more tightly than it binds the chapter's other accession groups.

boundary_rationale: The Hebron muster opens with a generic 'these are' register head, web:1Chr.12.23 = oshb:1Chr.12.24 (MT), וְ֠אֵלֶּה מִסְפְּרֵ֞י רָאשֵׁ֤י הֶֽחָלוּץ֙ (gloss: 'and these are the numbers of the heads of the armed for war'), sharing the generic waw-plus-demonstrative ('these are...') opener with both 11:10 and 12:1. Its own distinctive element, מִסְפְּרֵ֞י ('the numbers of'), matches not 11:10's רָאשֵׁ֤י ('the heads of') but 11:11's מִסְפַּ֥ר ('the number of', וְאֵ֛לֶּה מִסְפַּ֥ר הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים) -- and 11:11 itself sits one verse inside the mighty-men register without opening a unit there, so the shared ס-פ-ר consonantal root alone is not sufficient boundary evidence; what actually marks this verse as a fresh register head is its content, the arrival goal 'בָּ֥אוּ עַל דָּוִ֖יד חֶבְר֑וֹנָה' ('they came to David, to Hebron') and the kingdom-transfer purpose 'לְהָסֵ֞ב מַלְכ֥וּת שָׁא֛וּל אֵלָ֖יו' ('to turn Saul's kingdom over to him'), neither of which has any counterpart in the Ziklag-period notices just closed. The tally that follows is not perfectly uniform: its first entry is asyndetic and non-partitive, web:1Chr.12.24 = oshb:1Chr.12.25 (MT), 'בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה' ('the children of Judah'), and three further entries take the partitive without a conjunctive waw -- Simeon (web:1Chr.12.25 = oshb:1Chr.12.26 (MT), 'מִן בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֗וֹן'), Levi (web:1Chr.12.26 = oshb:1Chr.12.27 (MT), 'מִן בְּנֵי֙ הַלֵּוִ֔י'), and Zebulun (web:1Chr.12.33 = oshb:1Chr.12.34 (MT), 'מִזְּבֻל֞וּן') -- while the remaining eight of the twelve entries do carry the fuller waw-plus-partitive shape. An asyndetic, non-partitive first entry is itself consistent with a governing register head just introduced, reinforcing rather than undermining the near edge, even though it means the tally's internal form is not the single invariant pattern first claimed. One internal elaboration stays inside the same row: the Levite figure is expanded by two named leaders rather than a bare number, web:1Chr.12.27 = oshb:1Chr.12.28 (MT), וִיהוֹיָדָ֖ע הַנָּגִ֣יד לְאַהֲרֹ֑ן (gloss: 'and Jehoiada was leader for Aaron'), and web:1Chr.12.28 = oshb:1Chr.12.29 (MT), וְצָד֥וֹק נַ֖עַר גִּבּ֣וֹר חָ֑יִל (gloss: 'and Zadok, a young man mighty of valor') -- an inset naming priestly figures within the tally's own format, with no new heading marking it off, so it does not divide the row. The WLC's samekh field runs the full length of MT 12:24-12:37 (single-witness, confirmed on all fourteen verses including the priestly inset at MT 12:28 and 12:29), weak, non-driving list-item texture that this register unit declines to follow; no mark stands at MT 12:38, where the WLC's own final section of the chapter runs across this row's far edge. The last tribal figure, web:1Chr.12.37 = oshb:1Chr.12.38 (MT), מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָֽלֶף (gloss: 'a hundred and twenty thousand'), closes the numeric series; the next verse drops all numbers for qualitative celebration language, giving this row's far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carving out the Jehoiada/Zadok elaboration (27-28) as its own decision would split a priestly aside from its host tally without any tier-1 frame marking it as a separate unit. A further live rival at the far edge: MT 12:39's בָּ֣אוּ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה ("they came, to Hebron," gloss) answers this row's own head at MT 12:24's בָּ֥אוּ עַל דָּוִ֖יד חֶבְר֑וֹנָה ("they came to David, to Hebron," gloss; confirmed shared בא/חברונה lexemes) -- the identical inclusio M8-1Chr-077 discloses as a 'genuinely live rival' while grading itself medium.

boundary_rationale: The summary formula, web:1Chr.12.38 = oshb:1Chr.12.39 (MT), כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה אַנְשֵׁ֣י מִלְחָמָה֮ עֹדְרֵ֣י מַעֲרָכָה֒ בְּלֵבָ֤ב שָׁלֵם֙ בָּ֣אוּ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת דָּוִ֖יד עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (gloss: 'all these, men of war...came with a whole heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel'), closes the Hebron muster by a tier-1 lexical inclusio rather than by reaching across the whole chapter: its predicate בָּ֣אוּ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה answers the census's own head at web:1Chr.12.23 = oshb:1Chr.12.24 (MT), בָּ֥אוּ עַל דָּוִ֖יד חֶבְר֑וֹנָה (gloss: 'came to David at Hebron'), and directional חברונה is otherwise confined in the book to David's own accession, at oshb:1Chr.11.1 and oshb:1Chr.11.3. Each earlier notice in MT 12:1-22 is anchored to its own place instead — לְצִ֣יקְלַ֔ג at web:1Chr.12.1 = oshb:1Chr.12.1 (MT), לַמְצַ֨ד מִדְבָּ֜רָה at web:1Chr.12.8 = oshb:1Chr.12.9 (MT), עַד לַמְצָ֖ד at web:1Chr.12.16 = oshb:1Chr.12.17 (MT), אֶל צִֽיקְלַ֗ג at web:1Chr.12.20 = oshb:1Chr.12.21 (MT) — so the summary's predicate cannot sweep them in; its own widening clause, וְ֠גַם כָּל שֵׁרִ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל (gloss: 'and also all the rest of Israel'), reaches outward to Israel's remainder, not backward over those earlier bands. What genuinely closes here is the numbered tally itself: no further count follows web:1Chr.12.37 = oshb:1Chr.12.38 (MT), and the unit ends the chapter on the joy-formula, web:1Chr.12.40 = oshb:1Chr.12.41 (MT), כִּ֥י שִׂמְחָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל (gloss: 'for there was joy in Israel'), leaving nothing to compete for a further split. A pe also marks MT 12:41 (single-witness), exactly this row's own far edge; it is weak, non-driving corroboration, matching the disclosure practice this cluster otherwise observes at M8-1Chr-075/080/084.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v38/39(MT) as the census's own closing line rather than as this row's opening is a genuinely live rival, since directional חברונה clusters exactly at the census head (12:24 MT) and this summary (12:39 MT); it is defeated only by the disappearance of numeric content after web:1Chr.12.37 = oshb:1Chr.12.38 (MT) -- MT 12:37 itself still carries numeric content, Asher's אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אָֽלֶף ("forty thousand"), so the tally's actual final figure is MT 12:38's magnitude -- and the pivot to feast-narrative content, not by any chapter-wide reach the summary's own predicate does not supply.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a fresh deliberative verb with no antecedent in the celebratory Hebron-feast close that ends ch12: וַיִּוָּעַ֣ץ דָּוִ֗יד עִם שָׂרֵ֧י הָאֲלָפִ֛ים וְהַמֵּא֖וֹת ("David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds") — WEB: "David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, even with every leader." This introduces a wholly new topic (the ark) and a two-stage audience (officers, then the assembly). The unit stays one continuous speech-act through the proposal (13:2-3) and the people's reply, closing on the decision-idiom כִּֽי יָשַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י כָל הָעָֽם ("for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people") — WEB: "for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people" — immediately before 13:5 restarts with a different mustering verb, וַיַּקְהֵ֤ל דָּוִיד֙ אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ("David assembled all Israel"), that moves the action from words to a journey.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 13:1-8 together as one 'proposal-to-procession' unit loses because it erases the mode-shift from reported speech to narrated travel that the fresh gathering verb at 13:5 marks.

boundary_rationale: The mustering notice, oshb:1Chr.13.5, וַיַּקְהֵ֤ל דָּוִיד֙ אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (WEB: “So David assembled all Israel together, from the Shihor River of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath”), continues rather than swaps the root governing the deliberation just closed: its verb is hiphil of the same קהל that supplies קְהַ֣ל at oshb:1Chr.13.2, לְכֹ֣ל קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל, and הַקָּהָ֖ל at oshb:1Chr.13.4, וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֖ל; the root actually dropped at this seam is קבץ, David's own וְיִקָּבְצ֖וּ אֵלֵֽינוּ ('let them gather to us') at 13:2. The seam is instead a mode shift: 13:1-4 is reported deliberation closing on an evaluative formula, כִּֽי יָשַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י כָל הָעָֽם ('the thing was right in the eyes of all the people'), while 13:5 continues the wayyiqtol chain already running from 13:1's וַיִּוָּעַ֣ץ through 13:4's וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ -- 13:5's own וַיַּקְהֵ֤ל is likewise wayyiqtol, not a formal reset -- now reporting that same gathering as executed, running the geographic sweep and the retrieval at Kiriath Jearim through to the joyful cadence closing 13:8, מְשַׂחֲקִ֛ים לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּכָל עֹ֑ז וּבְשִׁירִ֤ים וּבְכִנֹּרוֹת֙ וּבִנְבָלִ֣ים וּבְתֻפִּ֔ים וּבִמְצִלְתַּ֖יִם וּבַחֲצֹצְרֽוֹת (WEB: 'played before God with all their might... and with trumpets'). That celebratory description ends abruptly at the temporal/locative pivot opening 13:9, וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד גֹּ֣רֶן כִּידֹ֑ן ('they came to Chidon's threshing floor'), so the music-and-motion unit does not bleed into the disaster that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing 13:5-8 into 13:1-4 as one proposal-through-execution arc is strengthened, not weakened, by the shared קהל root spanning both movements, a cohesion signal the row must disclose rather than deny; it still loses because the deliberative-speech-to-narrated-execution mode shift marks a real seam that root continuity alone does not erase; no wayyiqtol co-factor is needed or claimed, since the chain itself does not break at 13:5 -- 13:1's וַיִּוָּעַ֣ץ, 13:4's וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ, and 13:5's וַיַּקְהֵ֤ל are all wayyiqtol.

boundary_rationale: A location pivot breaks the procession's momentum: וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד גֹּ֣רֶן כִּידֹ֑ן ('they came to Chidon's threshing floor') — WEB: “When they came to Chidon’s threshing floor, Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark, for the oxen stumbled.” Uzza's death, וַיִּֽחַר אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּעֻזָּ֔א וַיַּכֵּ֕הוּ ('Yahweh's anger burned against Uzza, and he struck him'), and the etiological naming at 13:11, וַיִּקְרָ֞א לַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ פֶּ֣רֶץ עֻזָּ֔א עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה ('he called that place Perez Uzza, to this day'), might invite a split before David's fear, but 13:12's full clause, וַיִּירָ֤א דָוִיד֙ אֶת הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא (WEB: 'David was afraid of God that day'), anchors its own 'that day', בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא, a story-time anaphora, to the very death and naming just narrated — a deliberately different deictic than 13:11's own close, עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה ('to this day'), the etiological formula pointing to the narrator's present. Book-wide, the accent-exact form בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא (merkha+tipeha) is otherwise confined to oshb:1Chr.29.22, where the identical accents recur (בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא); 16:7 carries the same consonants under a different accent, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (munah+revia), a differently-accented consonantal attestation rather than an exact match. Likewise the accent-exact form עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה (tipeha+merkha) is confined to oshb:1Chr.4.43 (עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה) and oshb:1Chr.5.26 (עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה); 4:41's עַד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה and 17:5's עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה both carry different accents (4:41's עד is unaccented and its יום is munah, not merkha; 17:5's יום is likewise munah, and its close, הזה, ends on etnahta rather than the silluq of the exact-match set) -- two non-overlapping accent-exact sets whose contrast is the real cohesion signal, not a shared deixis. 13:12 drives, with no fresh scene verb, straight into the diversion and the closing blessing formula, וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת בֵּ֥ית עֹבֵֽד אֱדֹ֖ם וְאֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לֽוֹ ('Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom's house and all that he had') — WEB: “Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom’s house and all that he had.” A weak single-witness pe follows (oshb:1Chr.13.14), corroborating a break there before 14:1 introduces a wholly unrelated foreign embassy.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 13:12 into a death-and-etiology row (9-11) and a fear-and-relocation row (12-14) is a defensible finer cut, but it is rejected because the fear notice's own ביום ההוא points back into the same story-time as the death, in deliberate contrast to 13:11's narrator's-present formula, and no fresh wayyiqtol scene-verb of the assembly/gathering type intervenes.

boundary_rationale: A wholly new participant and topic open the unit; skipping past the witness's own internal doublet of the king's name (left as the source has it, not harmonized), the unambiguous continuation reads מֶֽלֶךְ צֹ֥ר מַלְאָכִים֮ אֶל דָּוִיד֒ ("king of Tyre ... messengers to David") — WEB: "Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house." This diplomatic-gift notice is structurally unlike anything in ch13. It closes at 14:2 with a recognition formula, כִּֽי הֱכִינ֧וֹ יְהוָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ("that Yahweh had established him king over Israel") — WEB: "David perceived that Yahweh had established him king over Israel" — corroborated by a weak single-witness pe (oshb:1Chr.14.2), immediately before 14:3 pivots to David's household.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 14:1-2 with the family list 14:3-7 as a single 'fruits of establishment' unit loses because the list has its own formal register-head at 14:4 and a pe mark corroborates a break precisely at 14:2.

boundary_rationale: The topic turns from diplomacy to household with וַיִּקַּ֨ח דָּוִ֥יד ע֛וֹד נָשִׁ֖ים בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם ("David took more wives in Jerusalem") — WEB: "David took more wives in Jerusalem, and David became the father of more sons and daughters" — then formalizes into a register with the 'these are' list-head at 14:4, וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ שְׁמ֣וֹת הַיְלוּדִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיוּ ל֖וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם ("these are the names of the children who were born to him in Jerusalem") — WEB: "These are the names of the children whom he had in Jerusalem." The list closes on its final triad, וֶאֱלִישָׁמָ֥ע וּבְעֶלְיָדָ֖ע וֶאֱלִיפָֽלֶט ("Elishama, and Beeliada, and Eliphelet") — WEB: "Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet" — immediately before an entirely different subject and verb reopen the narrative in military mode at 14:8.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 14:1-7 as one continuous 'David's rise' unit spanning embassy-then-family loses because two independent signals — the pe break after 14:2 and the formal namelist head at 14:4 — both point to the same seam rather than none.

boundary_rationale: A fresh subject and hearing-verb reopen military narrative after the namelist: וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים כִּי נִמְשַׁ֨ח דָּוִ֤יד ('the Philistines heard that David was anointed') — WEB: "When the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over all Israel ... David heard of it, and went out against them." The unit is organized around the oracular-inquiry formula at 14:10, וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤יד בֵּאלֹהִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֶֽעֱלֶה֙ ('David inquired of God, saying, Shall I go up'). It does not close at 14:11 despite that verse's own closure-shaped etiological naming formula, עַל כֵּ֗ן קָֽרְא֛וּ שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בַּ֥עַל פְּרָצִֽים ('therefore they called the name of that place Baal Perazim'): 14:12 opens with a locative anaphor, וַיַּעַזְבוּ שָׁ֖ם ('they left there'), binding the gods-disposal notice back to the very battlefield 14:11 just named, so the naming formula functions as an internal beat rather than the unit's own close. The unit closes instead at 14:12 on the disposal of the captured gods, וַיַּעַזְבוּ שָׁ֖ם אֶת אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד וַיִּשָּׂרְפ֖וּ בָּאֵֽשׁ — WEB: "They left their gods there; and David gave a command, and they were burned with fire." The verse also closes under a pe mark — weak, single-witness corroboration only — immediately before 14:13 opens a second, explicitly repeated campaign.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 14:8-17 into one 'two Philistine victories' super-unit is rejected not chiefly on 14:13's iteration marker — that marker word (עוֹד) recurs at 14:14 too, and so ties the panels together as much as it parts them — but on the reversed divine instruction the two inquiries receive: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֤וֹ יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵ֔ה at 14:10 against לֹ֥א תַֽעֲלֶ֖ה אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם at 14:14, a different tactic under a different command that a single merged unit cannot absorb as readily as a repeated formula.

boundary_rationale: The explicit iteration marker, oshb:1Chr.14.13, וַיֹּסִ֤יפוּ עוֹד֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֖וּ בָּעֵֽמֶק (WEB: “The Philistines made another raid in the valley”), opens a formally parallel but tactically different campaign — a reversed divine instruction, the mulberry-tree ambush — after the pe (single-witness) closing 14:12. It runs, via the wayyiqtol chain that includes 14:16, וַיַּ֣עַשׂ דָּוִ֔יד כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים ('David did as God commanded him'), to a closing summary at 14:17 whose own subject switches to the abstract NP שֵׁם דָּוִ֖יד ('the name/fame of David') rather than the David who acts in v16, and whose second clause, וַֽיהוָ֛ה נָתַ֥ן אֶת פַּחְדּ֖וֹ עַל כָּל הַגּוֹיִֽם ('and Yahweh brought the fear of him on all nations'), is waw-plus-subject-plus-qatal — a disjunctive summarizing construction, not a further wayyiqtol beat of the campaign narrative. That subject switch and cadence, not any claimed break in wayyiqtol form, is what closes the interlude here: 14:17 reports the campaign's outcome and stages no scene of its own. The forward edge is a shift of topic, participant, and setting rather than a break in verb form: 15:1, web:1Chr.15.1, וַיַּֽעַשׂ ל֥וֹ בָתִּ֖ים בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד (WEB: “David made himself houses in David’s city; and he prepared a place for God’s ark, and pitched a tent for it”), is itself a wayyiqtol — book_strategy_draft.md's own device matrix (§2) lists 15:1 alongside 11:1, 13:1, and 28:1 as exactly this class of wayyiqtol scene-opener — and its clause carries no expressed subject at all, since דָּוִ֑יד there is the nomen rectum of the place-name 'David's city,' not a stated actor. What actually marks the seam is the wholesale change of location and topic — houses, a prepared place, a tent for the ark — with no continuation of the battle scene, not any break in wayyiqtol form or any supplied subject the Hebrew itself withholds.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 14:16-17 as its own closing notice apart from the battle is rejected on function, not on a false syntactic reset: 14:17's subject switches to 'David's fame' and its second clause is a disjunctive waw-x-qatal, so the verse summarizes the campaign's outcome rather than continuing it, and it stages no independent scene of its own to stand alone as a row.

boundary_rationale: Opens the whole ark-transfer complex with a fresh notice, “וַיַּֽעַשׂ ל֥וֹ בָתִּ֖ים בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד” (“David made himself houses in David’s city”), paired with the tent clause “וַיֶּט ל֖וֹ אֹֽהֶל” (“and pitched a tent for it”) — a scene wholly new after chapter 14's Philistine battles, and with its own preparation verb, וַיָּ֤כֶן מָקוֹם֙ ('he prepared a place'). Verse 2's Levite-only principle (“no one ought to carry God’s ark but the Levites… Yahweh has chosen them”) supplies the theological grounds for everything through v24. The unit does not split at v3 despite v3's own gathering-verb-plus-royal-subject shape, וַיַּקְהֵ֥ל דָּוִ֛יד אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (matching v4's construction class), because v3's purpose clause, לְהַעֲלוֹת֙ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה אֶל מְקוֹמ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁר הֵכִ֥ין לֽוֹ ('to bring up Yahweh's ark to its place, which he had prepared for it'), re-uses the same root and noun as v1's וַיָּ֤כֶן מָקוֹם֙ ('he prepared a place'), forming a preparation inclusio that binds vv1-3 as one notice widening the stage to the whole nation before the priestly-Levitical muster narrows it again. A WLC samekh stands at oshb:1Chr.15.2 (single-witness); it is disclosed here as weak, non-driving texture and corroborates nothing beyond a possible internal pause the row declines to split on. The unit closes here because v4 pivots to a bounded named group under its own head verb, “וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף דָּוִ֛יד אֶת בְּנֵ֥י אַֽהֲרֹ֖ן וְאֶת הַלְוִיִּֽם” (“David gathered together the sons of Aaron and the Levites”), the scope-narrowing that opens the register proper.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 15:3, where the gathering verb matches v4's own construction class, is the row's real rival — not isolating v1 alone; it is rejected because v3's purpose clause completes the preparation inclusio opened at v1 (root and noun כון...מָקוֹם shared across both verses), keeping vv1-3 one preparatory notice before the register proper opens at v4.

boundary_rationale: The register head “וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף דָּוִ֛יד אֶת בְּנֵ֥י אַֽהֲרֹ֖ן וְאֶת הַלְוִיִּֽם” announces both priests and Levites -- אֶת בְּנֵ֥י אַֽהֲרֹ֖ן ("the sons of Aaron," the priestly party) and וְאֶת הַלְוִיִּֽם ("and the Levites") -- but the six לבני items that follow in strict parallel enumerate the Levitical side only (confirmed: אַֽהֲרֹ֖ן/הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֑ים never appear inside 15:5-10, own chapter-wide sweep), and the priests are first named individually at 15:11, Zadok and Abiathar. Then six items follow in strict parallel, each opening the same construct incipit “of the sons of X”: “לִבְנֵ֖י קְהָ֑ת” (Kohath), “לִבְנֵ֖י מְרָרִ֑י” (Merari), “לִבְנֵ֖י גֵּרְשׁ֑וֹם” (Gershom), “לִבְנֵ֖י אֱלִֽיצָפָ֑ן” (Elizaphan), “לִבְנֵ֖י חֶבְר֑וֹן” (Hebron), “לִבְנֵ֖י עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל” (Uzziel) — WEB mirrors this with “of the sons of Kohath… of the sons of Merari… of the sons of Gershom…”, each item naming a chief and a brother-count. The list never states a summary closure (“these are…”); its own six-fold incipit is the organizing device, and it ends the moment that pattern breaks — v11 abandons the “of the sons of X” template and reports David *calling* the same six chiefs by personal name in a new clause, “וַיִּקְרָ֣א דָוִ֔יד לְצָד֥וֹק וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֑ים”, shifting from list-form to direct address. A WLC samekh follows every one of vv5-10 without exception (oshb:1Chr.15.5 through oshb:1Chr.15.10, all single-witness), so the mark cannot selectively corroborate the terminal item's boundary over the five it never divides on; it is item-level, tracking each list entry rather than the row's own seam, and contributes nothing differential at v10 beyond what the six-fold incipit break at v11 already establishes on its own.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv4-10 into the v1-3 preparation notice as one span would bury the register-head/six-item-list device under the preceding narrative frame. Adding 15:4-11 as a combined register-plus-summons span is a further alternative, and it loses because v11 opens a fresh wayyiqtol, וַיִּקְרָ֣א ("and he called"), on a different root from the six-fold בְּנֵ֥י incipit, turning list-form into direct summons and keeping the priestly complement as M8-1Chr-087's own unit. NOTE FOR BOSS: this implies a live boundary question (whether v11 belongs with 086 or 087); flagged only, no span/confidence change ordered here.

boundary_rationale: V11's full clause, וַיִּקְרָ֣א דָוִ֔יד לְצָד֥וֹק וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֑ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֗ם לְאֽוּרִיאֵ֤ל עֲשָׂיָה֙ וְיוֹאֵ֣ל שְׁמַֽעְיָ֔ה וֶאֱלִיאֵ֖ל וְעַמִּינָדָֽב (“David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites: for Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab”), names the six chiefs just registered in vv5-10 in its own continuation and adds Zadok and Abiathar, new by name at this verse, the priestly party having been announced in the head at 15:4 (אֶת בְּנֵ֥י אַֽהֲרֹ֖ן), though not yet the individual names; their pairing with the Levites is confirmed downstream by the compliance report at 15:14, וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם ('the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves'). This eight-party address opens a speech that runs through v13. Its imperative core, “הִֽתְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ אַתֶּ֣ם וַאֲחֵיכֶ֔ם” (“Sanctify yourselves, both you and your brothers”), is second-person plural address, a mode absent from the preceding list, and v13 grounds the command by recalling the earlier failure (“because you didn’t carry it at first, Yahweh our God broke out in anger against us”), the causal appeal a charge needs before it can close. The speech ends where direct address ends: v14 drops back into third-person narration reporting compliance, “וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם” (“the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves”), echoing v12's imperative root but in the completed voice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 15:11-15 into one charge-and-compliance row is defensible by content, but it erases the cleaner grammatical seam between commanded second-person speech and narrated third-person fulfillment.

boundary_rationale: “וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם” answers v12's imperative in the completed third person, and v15 supplies the concrete enactment — the Levites bearing the ark on their shoulders with its poles, anchored to a legal warrant, “כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה” (WEB: 'as Moses commanded according to Yahweh’s word'). That citation answers the manner of carrying specifically — the second-person failure v13 named, לֹ֣א אַתֶּ֑ם ('not you') — and is distinct from the separate, first-person-plural failure to seek God 'according to the ordinance,' כִּי לֹ֥א דְרַשְׁנֻ֖הוּ כַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט, that closes the same verse; the speech keeps the two failures apart, and v15's warrant corrects only the carrying half. The pair closes because v16 opens an unrelated commission — David addressing the Levitical chiefs about singers, not ark-bearers — with its own new clause, “וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִיד֮ לְשָׂרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּם֒ לְהַֽעֲמִ֗יד אֶת אֲחֵיהֶם֙ הַמְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים”, naming a different office; the command verb itself is not the discriminator -- וַיֹּ֣אמֶר (v12) and וַיֹּ֣אמֶר (v16) are byte-identical wayyiqtol, and 15:14/15:15 carry no command at all, so וַיֹּ֣אמֶר occurs only twice in chapter 15, at v12 and v16 (chapter-wide sweep: 2 hits). What actually distinguishes v16 is its explicit subject, דָּוִיד֮ ("David," named where v12 leaves the subject unstated), and its infinitive complement, לְהַֽעֲמִ֗יד ("to appoint"), against v12's imperative הִֽתְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ ("sanctify yourselves") and וְהַֽעֲלִיתֶ֗ם ("and you shall bring up"). A pe stands after 15:15 in the WLC (single-witness); it does not itself mark the direct-speech-to-report boundary, which actually falls at 15:13/15:14, where David's charge ends and third-person narration resumes (וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם) — the 15:15/16 seam instead runs narration into a new speech frame (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִיד֮ לְשָׂרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּם֒). pmarks_1Chr.json also keys a pe to 1Chr.15.16 (single-witness), so the mark does not single this seam out from its neighbor; both are disclosed here as weak, non-differential texture rather than a driver.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching vv14-15 to the following singer-appointment span (16-24) as one long Levitical-action block would conflate the ark-bearing correction with a separate musical commission that both concern Levites but share no head verb.

boundary_rationale: V16 opens a second, distinct commission, “וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִיד֮ לְשָׂרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּם֒ לְהַֽעֲמִ֗יד אֶת אֲחֵיהֶם֙ הַמְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים” (“David spoke to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brothers as singers”), naming David explicitly as the subject of a wayyiqtol וַיֹּ֣אמֶר, a pattern unique in chapter 15 to this verse: v12's own וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם ('he said to them') carries no explicit subject noun, and 15:2's אָמַ֣ר דָּוִ֔יד ('David said') is qatal, not wayyiqtol -- own ויאמר sweep of chapter 15 -- so that uniqueness, not the v12 echo, carries the head claim here; the v12 echo may remain as a formula note but cannot itself ground the seam, since v12 sits mid-span inside M8-1Chr-087's own 15:11-13 unit rather than heading anything there. V16 also differs from v11's call-formula, וַיִּקְרָ֣א ('he called') — a different root — and names a musical office rather than ark-bearing; this is the register's controlling head. What follows through v24 is one continuous distribution of roles under that head — chief singers and instruments (17-19), second-rank singers on strings (20-21), the supervising Chenaniah (22), and finally doorkeepers and priest-trumpeters (23-24), closing on “וְעֹבֵ֤ד אֱדֹם֙ וִֽיחִיָּ֔ה שֹׁעֲרִ֖ים לָאָרֽוֹן” (“Obed-Edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark”). The head is formally resumed and executed, not merely left uninterrupted: v17's own wayyiqtol, וַיַּעֲמִ֣ידוּ הַלְוִיִּ֗ם ('the Levites appointed'), realizes v16's infinitive לְהַֽעֲמִ֗יד under a new, explicit subject, so the roster is one commissioned sequence carried out by the same עמד-hiphil root rather than a series interrupted by a rival head. The span closes because v25 abandons roster form for a fresh scene, “וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛יד וְזִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֑ים”, naming a different subject set in motion from Obed-Edom's house toward David's city -- v25's מִן בֵּ֥ית עֹבֵֽד אֱדֹ֖ם ("from the house of Obed-Edom," gloss; WEB "up out of the house of Obed-Edom") marks the procession leaving that house, reaching עַד עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד ("to the city of David") at 15:29.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this into an instruments sub-unit (16-22) and a doorkeepers sub-unit (23-24) is plausible since v23 shifts topic, but the resumption of the same head by וַיַּעֲמִ֣ידוּ at v17, rather than by a rival command, and the strategy's own disclosed row-vs-inset uncertainty here argue for holding it as one roster row.

boundary_rationale: “וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛יד וְזִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֑ים” (“David, the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands went to bring the ark of Yahweh’s covenant up out of the house of Obed-Edom with joy”) opens the scene as its own main predication, naming the procession's participants; sacrifice (26), vestments (27), and instrumented shouting (28) all continue the same journey without any new head-verb breaking the sequence. A pe follows 15:29 in the WLC (single-witness), and oshb:1Chr.15.25 itself carries a samekh (single-witness), a division immediately after the span's own first verse; both are disclosed here as equally non-driving texture, consistent with but not the source of a boundary the subject-and-verb change at 16:1 already carries. Two further ויהי clauses inside the span are not rival scene-openers but subordinate protases, each closed by its own apodosis within the same verse: v26's וַֽיְהִי֙ בֶּעְזֹ֣ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים ('and it happened, as God helped...') is answered by the sacrifice clause that follows it, and v29's וַיְהִ֗י אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה בָּ֖א עַד עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד ('the ark of Yahweh's covenant came to David's city') is answered, in the same verse, by Michal's reaction — וּמִיכַ֨ל בַּת שָׁא֜וּל נִשְׁקְפָ֣ה...וַתִּ֥בֶז ל֖וֹ בְּלִבָּֽהּ ('Michal, Saul's daughter, looked out...and she despised him in her heart'), welded to the arrival clause not by a wayyiqtol chain but by its actual shape, waw plus fronted subject plus qatal -- the opening clause itself, not a wayyiqtol; the wayyiqtols וַתֵּ֨רֶא ("and she saw") and וַתִּ֥בֶז ("and she despised") continue only after this clause -- which is the regular answering form after a temporal protasis, not the 'plain consecutive chain' a rival reading would need; WEB's own rendering, 'As the ark of Yahweh’s covenant came to David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window,' corroborates the subordination reading from the second witness. This aligns the rationale with the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative paragraph, which already identifies v29 as a temporal protasis. The span ends because 16:1 switches subject and verb entirely, “וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּצִּ֣יגוּ אֹת֔וֹ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאֹ֔הֶל” (“they brought in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent”), moving the action from street to shrine.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Peeling v29 off into its own row as an isolated Michal notice is not defeated by denying that v29 opens a clause-initial scene — it demonstrably does, the identical ויהי-plus-subject frame that opens v25 recurs there. Recounted precisely, the span's ויהי clauses are two subject-bearing clauses (15:25, 15:29) and one infinitival temporal clause: v26's וַֽיְהִי֙ בֶּעְזֹ֣ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים ("and it happened, as God helped...") has no fronted-subject-plus-participle frame like v25 or v29, only a bare infinitive construct, so frame-identity does not in fact extend to a third instance. The real ground is subordination: v25's ויהי clause is itself the scene's main predication, while both v26 and v29 are temporal protases whose own apodoses follow in the same verse, so Michal's reaction is subordinate to, not a rival scene alongside, the arrival just narrated, and the procession stays whole through its own resolution.

boundary_rationale: “וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּצִּ֣יגוּ אֹת֔וֹ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאֹ֔הֶל” begins the installation with a new subject and location distinct from the street procession just closed; WEB's “They brought in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent” reads as the destination-arrival counterpart to 15:25's departure. The unit runs through the blessing (v2) to the food distribution, closing on a concrete, bounded gift-list, “לְאִישׁ֙ כִּכַּר לֶ֔חֶם וְאֶשְׁפָּ֖ר וַאֲשִׁישָֽׁה” (“to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins”). Verses 1-4 run as one unbroken wayyiqtol chain — וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙, וַיַּצִּ֣יגוּ, וַיַּקְרִ֛יבוּ (v1), וַיְכַ֣ל, וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ (v2), וַיְחַלֵּק֙ (v3), וַיִּתֵּ֞ן (v4), with no intervening nominal clause — so no verb-form break isolates v3/v4 specifically, and the row does not rest on one; the one participant shift in the stretch is v1's unnamed plural actors yielding to David from v2 on (וַיְכַ֣ל דָּוִ֔יד), which lands at v1/v2, not at the drawn seam. What actually divides v3 from v4 is content: v1-3 narrates a single, completed event — installation, blessing, a bounded one-time distribution to 'everyone' — while v4 opens a lasting institution, "וַיִּתֵּ֞ן לִפְנֵ֨י אֲר֧וֹן יְהוָ֛ה ..." ("He appointed some of the Levites to minister before Yahweh's ark"), with its own durative purpose clause, וּלְהַזְכִּיר֙ וּלְהוֹד֣וֹת וּלְהַלֵּ֔ל ('to commemorate, to thank, and to praise'), moving from a one-time offering-and-meal notice to a standing liturgical office. This new institution is nonetheless tied to the installation just narrated, in both place and date: v4's לִפְנֵ֨י אֲר֧וֹן יְהוָ֛ה ("before the ark of Yahweh") places the appointed ministers at the very ark installed in the tent at v1, and v7's בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא ("on that day") dates the ordinance to that same installation day. The seam therefore rests on the shift in aspect -- from a bounded, completed distribution to a durative, standing office -- not on any unrelatedness between the two; this is itself consistent with the row's existing medium confidence, and no confidence change is ordered here. A pe marks v4 and a samekh marks 15:25 (both single-witness, confirmed in pmarks_1Chr.json); neither settles the boundary, and both are disclosed here as standing, non-driving texture rather than evidence for or against the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this span through v4 is a live rival now that the syntactic discriminators are withdrawn; it is rejected only on content — a completed one-time gift distribution giving way to an ongoing ministerial appointment with its own durative purpose clause — not on any verb-form or subject break at the v3/v4 join itself, which the text does not supply.

boundary_rationale: “וַיִּתֵּ֞ן לִפְנֵ֨י אֲר֧וֹן יְהוָ֛ה מִן הַלְוִיִּ֖ם מְשָׁרְתִ֑ים” opens a register-style institution notice whose purpose clause, “וּלְהַזְכִּיר֙ וּלְהוֹד֣וֹת וּלְהַלֵּ֔ל” (“to commemorate, to thank, and to praise”), sets the terms for everything through v7; vv5-6 name the roster under that purpose, led by “אָסָ֥ף הָרֹ֖אשׁ” (“Asaph the chief”), then the priest-trumpeters. V7 closes the notice with a dated colophon, “בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא אָ֣ז נָתַ֤ן דָּוִיד֙ בָּרֹ֔אשׁ לְהֹד֖וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה בְּיַד אָסָ֖ף וְאֶחָֽיו” (“Then on that day David first ordained giving of thanks to Yahweh by the hand of Asaph and his brothers”): the near-edge warrant binding v7 to vv5-6 is a catchword bracket, not the date: v5's אָסָ֥ף הָרֹ֖אשׁ ("Asaph the chief") is answered by v7's own בָּרֹ֔אשׁ and בְּיַד אָסָ֖ף וְאֶחָֽיו ("by the hand of Asaph and his brothers"), the sole אסף/ראש co-occurrence in 16:1-22 (book-wide sweep). The demonstrative "that day" cannot itself supply that warrant: it points backward to the ark's installation at v1, outside this row's own 16:4-16:7 span, so the dated formula is read here as dating the whole complex and disclosed as reaching back into 16:1-3, not as itself binding v7 within this row's boundaries. The clause is nonetheless third-person narrative report, the same register as vv4-6. The span ends exactly where that mode breaks: v8 opens with a bare plural imperative, “הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ בִשְׁמ֔וֹ” (“Oh give thanks to Yahweh. Call on his name.”), direct liturgical address with no narrator's voice at all — the sharpest register shift in the complex. pmarks_1Chr.json keys pe to both oshb:1Chr.16.4 and oshb:1Chr.16.7 (each single-witness); the earlier mark falls after the span's own opening verse and cuts v4 from the vv5-7 material the row binds to it, so both are disclosed here together rather than citing only the agreeing 16:7 mark, and neither is treated as capable of settling the v7-vs-v8 question by itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v7 as the medley's own frame rather than the appointment's colophon has real support, since its infinitive 'to give thanks' is echoed by v8's imperative 'give thanks', but v7's backward-pointing 'that day' and unbroken third-person grammar tie it more tightly to vv4-6.

boundary_rationale: The movement opens on the bare imperative cluster “הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ בִשְׁמ֔וֹ”, immediately reinforced by v9's own pair, “שִׁ֤ירוּ לוֹ֙” (“Sing to him”), addressed to the “offspring of Israel his servant” (v13); the content moves through covenant-historical recital — the Abrahamic covenant and the oath to Isaac (16), the wandering “few men in number” (19), kings reproved (21) — and closes on a quoted divine warning, “אַֽל תִּגְּעוּ֙ בִּמְשִׁיחָ֔י וּבִנְבִיאַ֖י אַל תָּרֵֽעוּ” (“Don’t touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!”), addressed within that embedded quotation to the מְלָכִֽים ("kings") of v21 -- לֹא הִנִּ֤יחַ לְאִישׁ֙ לְעָשְׁקָ֔ם וַיּ֥וֹכַח עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מְלָכִֽים ("he allowed no man to wrong them, and he reproved kings for their sakes," gloss) -- not to the זֶ֚רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדּ֔וֹ בְּנֵ֥י יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּחִירָֽיו ("offspring of Israel his servant, sons of Jacob his chosen," gloss) of v13; since it is quoted speech within the recital, the recital's own audience remains unbroken through v22, whereas v23 re-addresses the poem itself to כָּל הָאָ֔רֶץ ("all the earth"). Repetition alone is not what marks the far boundary: the same movement repeats “זִכְר֗וּ” ('remember') at v12 and again at v15, נִפְלְאֹתָיו֙ / לְעוֹלָם֙ בְּרִית֔וֹ, without dividing anything there. What marks the boundary with what follows is instead a resumption re-addressed: the movement's own opening imperative is הוֹד֤וּ (v8), which recurs only once more, at v34; v23 does not repeat that word, but instead resumes v9's own שִׁ֤ירוּ ("sing") alone -- book-wide, שירו surfaces only at v9 and v23 -- while v9's own לוֹ֙ ("to him") gives way at v23 to לַֽיהוָה֙ כָּל הָאָ֔רֶץ ("to Yahweh, all the earth"), re-addressing the imperative rather than merely continuing it, marking a deliberate new movement. The WLC also carries a pe after 16:22 (single-witness); it neither drives nor is needed for the call, since the resumed-and-re-addressed imperative is sufficient on its own.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 16:8-36 as one undivided quotation because it is nominally 'one poem' would erase the audience-shift the text marks by resuming and re-addressing v9's שירו, the clearest available seam.

boundary_rationale: “שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ כָּל הָאָ֔רֶץ” (“Sing to Yahweh, all the earth!”) reprises v9's imperative but universalizes its addressee from Israel to “all the earth,” a phrase repeated verbatim at v30, “חִ֤ילוּ מִלְּפָנָיו֙ כָּל הָאָ֔רֶץ” (“Tremble before him, all the earth”) — a genuine two-point verbatim bracket, v23 and v30, not a third repetition inside this span: a consonantal sweep of כל הארץ across the whole chapter returns exactly three hits, v14, v23, and v30, and the third sits outside this span, in the preceding movement's “בְּכָל הָאָ֖רֶץ” (v14, 'in all the earth', adverbial, describing Yahweh's own judgments rather than addressing an audience) — so the phrase is not exclusive to 23-33 and does not itself recur a third time inside it. V33's own close, “כִּי בָ֖א לִשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ” ('for he comes to judge the earth'), reads אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ, a definite object with no כָּל — a distinct closing gesture, not the bracketing phrase repeated — and a further bare “הָאָ֔רֶץ” at v31 (וְתָגֵ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ, 'let the earth rejoice') likewise stands outside the two-point bracket. The movement runs from the summons (23-24) through Yahweh's incomparability among “the gods of the peoples” (25-27) to the peoples' own summons to worship (28-29) and finally creation's acclamation — heavens, earth, sea, field, and trees — closing, at v33, in a shift of addressee from nations to inanimate creation entirely, “אָ֥ז יְרַנְּנ֖וּ עֲצֵ֣י הַיָּ֑עַר מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כִּי בָ֖א לִשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ” (“then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth”). V34 breaks the pattern by dropping 'the earth' language altogether and instead reprising the medley's own opening consonantal skeleton -- the same two-word skeleton opens both v8, “הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙” ('Give thanks to Yahweh'), and v34, “הוֹד֤וּ לַיהוָה֙” ('Give thanks to Yahweh'); a consonantal sweep of the whole book confirms these are its only two loci (16:8, 16:34). The repetition is not byte-identical: v8's divine name carries a meteg mark that v34's lacks. Only v34 continues into the following clause, “כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם” ('for he is good, for his lovingkindness endures forever'), which does not belong to v8's own opening.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending this movement at v30, splitting the divine-versus-idols argument from the creation-acclamation, remains a live rival now that the bracket is corrected to two points rather than three; it is rejected because the v33/34 edge is independently defensible on its own terms — v34 drops 'the earth' language and restarts the medley's own opening words instead — not because a three-fold inclusio spans 23-33, which the text does not supply.

boundary_rationale: “הוֹד֤וּ לַיהוָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב” (“Oh give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good”) opens with the same two-word formula that opened v8’s “הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ בִשְׁמ֔וֹ”, a deliberate inclusio signaling the composition folds back to its start rather than continuing the prior creation-acclamation. The prayer that follows, “וְאִמְר֕וּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֨נוּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֔נוּ וְקַבְּצֵ֥נוּ וְהַצִּילֵ֖נוּ מִן הַגּוֹיִ֑ם” (“Say, ‘Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us together and deliver us from the nations…’”, the quoted speech continuing to a plea for praise), and the doxology close the performed unit, and the narrative resumes explicitly at “וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ כָל הָעָם֙ אָמֵ֔ן וְהַלֵּ֖ל לַֽיהוָֽה” (“all the people said, ‘Amen,’ and praised Yahweh”) — a third-person report of the congregation’s response ending the direct-address poetry begun at v8. That shift from quoted liturgy back to narrated crowd-response is the clearest close available, and it is exactly where v37 picks up an unrelated standing-arrangements notice. Fittingly, the WLC also marks a break with a pe right at 16:36 (single-witness parashah division); the inclusio and the Amen-report have already secured the close on their own, so this only echoes what the wording had settled.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv34-36 into the preceding universal-turn movement would lose the inclusio the text builds by echoing its own opening line, and would understate the formal weight of the congregation's spoken Amen as its own closing device.

boundary_rationale: V37 opens with a new subject and verb, “וַיַּֽעֲזָב שָׁ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית יְהוָ֔ה לְאָסָ֖ף וּלְאֶחָ֑יו” (“So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, to minister before the ark continually”), returning to third-person narration about David once the congregation’s Amen has closed the quoted psalm. From there the register lists parallel standing assignments introduced by repeated conjunctive clauses rather than new scene-verbs: Obed-Edom and Hosah as doorkeepers (38), then Zadok’s priestly line at Gibeon, “וְאֵ֣ת צָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאֶחָיו֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה בַּבָּמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן” (“Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests, before Yahweh’s tabernacle in the high place that was at Gibeon”), with its own burnt-offering duty (40), and finally Heman and Jeduthun’s musicians, closing on “וּבְנֵ֥י יְדוּת֖וּן לַשָּֽׁעַר” (“the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate”). No new head-verb interrupts this parallel structure, so it reads as one two-site staffing register. It closes because v43 abandons list form for a wholly different closing verb naming the whole assembly’s departure.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this into a Jerusalem-ark sub-unit (37-38) and a Gibeon-tabernacle sub-unit (39-42) tracks the real change of location, but neither half carries its own commissioning verb, so holding the register whole better matches its grammar than a location-based split would.

boundary_rationale: “וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ כָל הָעָ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ לְבֵית֑וֹ וַיִּסֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֖יד לְבָרֵ֥ךְ אֶת בֵּיתֽוֹ” (“All the people departed, each man to his house; and David returned to bless his house”) supplies a fresh subject, “all the people,” breaking the two-site personnel register of vv37-42, which never named a general dismissal for the assembly as a whole. The verse pairs a general dispersal with David's own return and private household blessing, a two-part closing formula. What actually discriminates the far edge is not campaign tiling but 17:1's own frame-setting clause, oshb:1Chr.17.1, וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָשַׁ֥ב דָּוִ֖יד בְּבֵית֑וֹ ('Now it happened, when David lived in his house...'), web:1Chr.17.1: “When David was living in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet” — a new temporal frame handing the floor to a wholly different scene, the dynastic oracle, and a new participant, Nathan; nothing in 16:43 continues into it. The verse is the natural terminus of the entire ark-transfer-and-worship complex begun at 15:1. A pe closes 16:43 itself in the WLC (single-witness) — a weak corroboration for treating this verse as a unit-final beat, though the subject-and-formula shift and the 17:1 frame contrast already carry the argument without it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Appending v43 to the preceding standing-arrangements register as its final item would treat 'departed to his house' as one more staffing note, but its wholly different subject and dismissal-formula shape mark it as the complex's own closing beat.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a fresh temporal/spatial notice, "כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָשַׁ֥ב דָּוִ֖יד בְּבֵית֑וֹ" (WEB "When David was living in his house"), that introduces Nathan the prophet by name and title for the first time in Chronicles (earlier Nathans at 1Chr.2.36, 1Chr.3.5, 1Chr.11.38, 1Chr.14.4 are a different genealogical figure, a son of David, and a mighty man's kinsman) - a new-participant notice that opens a scene rather than continuing one. The unit is David's cedar-house remark and Nathan's daytime reply, "כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֑ה" (WEB "Do all that is in your heart"). It closes there because v.3 resets the clock with its own temporal marker, "וַֽיְהִ֖י בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא" (WEB "That same night"), swapping human counsel for a night-time word-event; the daytime conversation and the night oracle are marked as two successive time-frames, not one continuous speech. A samekh follows v.2 in WLC (single-witness), weakly corroborating the seam before the night formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 1-2 into the oracle report as its narrative frame (one span through v.15) loses because the night-time reset at v.3 is itself a tier-1 temporal marker separating counsel from revelation.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the classic word-event formula "וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶל נָתָ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר" (WEB "the word of God came to Nathan, saying"), then a commission-plus-messenger-formula pair at v.4 introduces the first divine word: לֵ֤ךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֙ אֶל דָּוִ֣יד עַבְדִּ֔י כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה ('go and tell my servant David, thus says Yahweh') — a house is not needed now, God has walked tent to tent. That word closes on its own rhetorical question, "לָ֛מָּה לֹא בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים" (WEB "Why have you not built me a house of cedar?"), before v.7 opens a second commission-plus-formula pair built the same way as v.4's own: וְ֠עַתָּה כֹּֽה תֹאמַ֞ר לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְדָוִ֗יד ('now therefore, thus you shall say to my servant David') is a second-person commissioning yiqtol, completed by the messenger formula proper, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת ('thus says Yahweh of Armies') — the identical two-part shape already standing at v.4. This recurring commission-plus-formula shape, together with the logical pivot ועתה ('and now') and the expanded divine title, marks v.7 as a restart rather than mid-oracle continuation. A samekh also stands after v.2 itself (oshb:1Chr.17.2, samekh, single-witness), weak corroboration of this span's own opening edge (the 17:2/17:3 seam), disclosed here alongside the mark already noted at v.7. Within the book itself, the identical consonantal skeleton, כה אמר, recurs only twice more, at 21:10 and 21:11 — a two-stage relay, Yahweh's commission to Gad and then Gad's own delivery to David — not a further in-book precedent for a single speaker pivoting mid-oracle to a new topic, so the argument for treating vv.3-6 as the deferral-word proper, distinct from the promise-word that follows, rests on the in-chapter repetition and pivot alone rather than on any wider book usage.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 17:3-15 as one unbroken divine speech (the single-envelope view favored by the coarser register-reading) is a live rival, since both words share Nathan as intermediary. A WLC samekh does stand at oshb:1Chr.17.7 (single-witness), one verse past the drawn boundary, noted here only as weak texture that neither confirms nor rules out this seam. The rival loses because the repeated commission-plus-messenger-formula pattern at v.4/v.7, reinforced by the עתה pivot, is itself a recognized restart shape within this very speech, not mere continuation.

boundary_rationale: The second commission-and-messenger-formula pairing at v.7 pivots the content from deferral to promise: "אֲנִ֤י לְקַחְתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן הַנָּוֶ֔ה מִֽן אַחֲרֵ֖י הַצֹּ֑אן" (WEB "I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep") runs through the dynastic core, "וּבַ֖יִת יִֽבְנֶה לְּךָ֥ יְהוָֽה" (v.10, WEB "Yahweh will build you a house") and "ה֥וּא יִבְנֶה לִּ֖י בָּ֑יִת וְכֹנַנְתִּ֥י אֶת כִּסְא֖וֹ עַד עוֹלָֽם" (v.12, WEB "He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever"). This span's own left edge carries the same seam risk disclosed at the sibling 17:3-6 row: both rest on the same v.6/7 messenger-formula pivot, and if that seam were resolved the other way, this row and its neighbor would collapse into one; see M8-1Chr-099 for the corrected in-chapter argument that seam still carries. Internally the promise runs through a hinge the rationale argues rather than steps past: v.11 opens a protasis, וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי מָלְא֤וּ יָמֶ֨יךָ֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת עִם אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ ('when your days are fulfilled that you must go to be with your fathers'), whose apodosis follows in weqatal, וַהֲקִֽימוֹתִ֤י אֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֙ אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ ('I will set up your seed after you'), pivoting the grant from the addressee's own history (vv.7-10) to the offspring who will build the house (vv.11-14). The two halves stay inside one row because both sit within a single, uninterrupted divine speech with no narrative frame intervening between v.10 and v.12 — the protasis-apodosis pair is the transition the speech itself uses to move from David to his heir, not a break in the speech act. It closes on the narrator's summary tag, "כְּכֹל֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וּכְכֹ֖ל הֶחָז֣וֹן הַזֶּ֑ה כֵּ֛ן דִּבֶּ֥ר נָתָ֖ן אֶל דָּוִֽיד" (v.15, WEB "According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David"), a compiler-voice closure that answers the word-event opener of v.3 and stands outside the direct speech. A pe follows v.15 in WLC (single-witness), corroborating the pause before v.16's scene change, "וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔יד וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה" (WEB "David the king went in and sat before Yahweh"), which reassigns David the royal title he lacked in vv.1-15 and moves him bodily before Yahweh to pray.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is not v.15 peeling off as its own one-verse closural row but full 17:3-15 unification, which book_strategy_draft.md §6 (non-authorizing planning artifact) itself treats as a single oracle unit. It is rejected on grounds internal to this row's own span: the second commission-and-messenger-formula pairing at v.7 itself, וְ֠עַתָּה כֹּֽה תֹאמַ֞ר לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְדָוִ֗יד, together with the expanded title, יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת, is the restart-marking device this row opens on, independently argued at the sibling row bounding 17:3-6. v.15's retrospective 'all these words ... this vision' answering v.3's opening word-event formula is conceded to the unification rival rather than pressed against it: that inclusio in fact spans the whole 3-15 stretch, which would, if anything, argue for holding vv.3-15 together, not for peeling v.7-15 off alone.

boundary_rationale: David's move to a new posture and place, "וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִֽי אֲנִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה" (v.16, WEB "and he said, Who am I, Yahweh"), opens a first-person prayer answering the oracle just delivered. Internally the prayer turns three times on the particle עתה/'and now', but not in one uniform printed form: וְעַתָּ֣ה (munah accent) opens v.23; the same form, וְעַתָּ֣ה (munah), opens v.26; and וְעַתָּ֗ה (revia accent) opens v.27 — but the three turns are not parallel petitions: only v.23 petitions, with a jussive followed by an imperative, יֵאָמֵ֖ן עַד עוֹלָ֑ם וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ ('let it be established forever, and do as you have said'); v.26 is a verbless declarative, אַתָּה ה֖וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים ('you are God'); and v.27 opens with a Hiphil qatal of acknowledgment, הוֹאַ֨לְתָּ֙ לְבָרֵךְ֙ ('you have been pleased to bless'), reporting what Yahweh has already granted rather than asking for anything. The particle marks a mood arc — request moving to declaration — rather than a threefold petition refrain, and that arc argues for keeping vv.16-27 together at least as strongly as three parallel petitions would: it is a single, unbroken movement, not a scene change, so these stay inside one row rather than becoming three. The prayer closes on its own doxological cadence, "כִּֽי אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בֵּרַ֔כְתָּ וּמְבֹרָ֖ךְ לְעוֹלָֽם" (v.27, WEB "for you, Yahweh, have blessed, and it is blessed forever"), immediately before 18:1 resets the discourse with the campaign-report opener "וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן" (WEB "After this"), moving from temple-house oracle to battlefield notices entirely.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the prayer at each 'now, Yahweh' turn into three petition-rows loses because all three share one uninterrupted first-person address to Yahweh with no intervening narrative frame; the particle marks progression along one mood arc — request moving to declaration — rather than restarting the speech at each turn.

boundary_rationale: The campaign-report opener "וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים" (v.1, WEB "After this, David defeated the Philistines") launches a run of victory notices against Moab, Zobah, Damascus, and Edom that the text itself binds together with a repeated refrain: וַיּ֤וֹשַׁע יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֔יד בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽךְ closes the Zobah/Damascus notice (v.6, WEB: 'Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went') and a near-identical clause closes the Edom notice, וַיּ֤וֹשַׁע יְהוָה֙ אֶת דָּוִ֔יד בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽךְ (v.13, WEB: 'Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went') — the two verses are identical but for the government of David, prepositional ל at v.6 against the object marker את at v.13, an alternation worth disclosing given how much weight the refrain carries. Book-wide, this Hiphil-wayyiqtol of ישע occurs only three times total — here at v.6 and v.13, and once more at oshb:1Chr.11.14, וַיּ֥וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֖ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה ('Yahweh saved with a great victory') — which takes a cognate accusative rather than a personal object at all. The refrain's first occurrence, v.6, does not itself terminate a panel: the Hadadezer thread it closes runs on through the spoil notices of vv.7-8 (the bronze and gold Solomon later used) and into the Tou-of-Hamath embassy, vv.9-11, whose opening clause, וַיִּשְׁמַ֕ע תֹּ֖עוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֲמָ֑ת כִּ֚י הִכָּ֣ה דָוִ֔יד אֶת כָּל חֵ֖יל הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר (WEB: 'Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer'), ties it explicitly back to that same Zobah victory — the כִּ֚י here is the object complementizer completing the verb of hearing, וַיִּשְׁמַ֕ע, not a causal connector, the same construction correctly labeled at 19:6's parallel כִּ֥י (M8-1Chr-104). Only v.13's occurrence is followed by nothing further of its own campaign before the register-head pivot at v.14, which is what makes it, and not v.6, the catalogue's true terminus. WLC keys a pe to v.8 (single-witness), marking a sub-pause before the Tou notice, consistent with, not the source of, the seam argued above. The unit closes before v.14's register-head pivot, "וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ דָּוִ֖יד עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל" (WEB "David reigned over all Israel"), which trades victory notices for an administrative summary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading vv.1-6 and vv.7-13 as two refrain-closed panels rather than one bracketed catalogue is the stronger rival the row must close off, not a Tou-embassy peel-off: it loses because v.6's occurrence of the refrain is non-terminal — the Hadadezer thread it closes runs on through the spoil notices and the causally-linked Tou embassy — while v.13's is followed immediately by the v.14 register-head pivot to an unrelated administrative summary, so only one of the refrain's two occurrences actually functions as a catalogue-ending seam.

boundary_rationale: The regnal summary וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ דָּוִ֖יד עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֗י עֹשֶׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה לְכָל עַמּֽוֹ (v.14, WEB “David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness for all his people.”) is wayyiqtol on both its verbs (וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ, וַיְהִ֗י עֹשֶׂ֛ה), so the pivot at this seam is not a shift out of wayyiqtol; it is the periphrastic וַיְהִ֗י עֹשֶׂ֛ה (a היה-plus-participle construction) reading as durative and characterising, against the punctual הכה-chain of vv.1-13 headed by וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד (18:1, and again at 18:3 as וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד) and וַיַּ֖ךְ (18:2), together with the domain shift from foreign-nation conquest to the domestic pair מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה.
