The verbless title-clauses proper begin only at v.15, וְיוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֖ה עַל הַצָּבָ֑א (WEB “Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army”), and run as a polysyndetic, waw-coordinated register of office-holders — וְיוֹאָ֥ב/וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט (v.15), וְצָד֧וֹק/וַאֲבִימֶ֥לֶךְ (v.16), וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ֙/וּבְנֵי (v.17) — rather than an asyndetic list, closing on וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע עַל הַכְּרֵתִ֖י וְהַפְּלֵתִ֑י וּבְנֵי דָוִ֥יד הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים לְיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (v.17, WEB “and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief officials serving the king.”). A pe follows v.17 in WLC (single-witness), corroborating the close before 19:1 resets again with וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן (WEB “After this, ... died”), the same campaign-report opener reused for the Ammon/Aram war.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 18:14-17 as the capstone of the preceding victory catalogue (one span, 18:1-17) loses because v.15's verbless, polysyndetic title-clauses (וְיוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֖ה עַל הַצָּבָ֑א, no finite verb) replace the punctual הכה-chain of vv.1-13 outright, and the domain shifts from conquest to office, the register-head shift the device matrix treats as boundary-bearing.

boundary_rationale: The report opens with the same campaign-report device used at 18:1, וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיָּ֕מָת נָחָ֖שׁ (v.1, WEB “After this, Nahash the king of the children of Ammon died”), and runs a single self-contained episode: comfort mission, the princes' suspicion, וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י בְנֵי עַמּ֜וֹן לְחָנ֗וּן הַֽמְכַבֵּ֨ד דָּוִ֤יד אֶת אָבִ֨יךָ֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי שָׁלַ֥ח לְךָ֖ מְנַחֲמִ֑ים הֲלֹ֡א בַּ֠עֲבוּר לַחְקֹ֨ר וְלַהֲפֹ֤ךְ וּלְרַגֵּל֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ בָּ֥אוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו אֵלֶֽיךָ (v.3, WEB “But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven’t his servants come to you to search, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?””), the mutilation, and David's resolving directive, וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ וַיַּגִּ֨ידוּ לְדָוִ֤יד עַל הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח לִקְרָאתָ֔ם כִּי הָי֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים נִכְלָמִ֣ים מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ שְׁב֣וּ בִֽירֵח֔וֹ עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר יְצַמַּ֥ח זְקַנְכֶ֖ם וְשַׁבְתֶּֽם (v.5, WEB “Then some people went and told David how the men were treated. He sent to meet them; for the men were greatly humiliated. The king said, “Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.””), which closes the incident with a settled outcome. The wayyiqtol chain itself runs unbroken from v.1 through v.7: no fronted constituent, temporal notice, or new participant marks v.6 as a fresh discourse unit, and Hanun and the Ammonite princes remain the actors on both sides of the seam. The seam is instead argued on content: v.5's directive resolves the embassy incident, and v.6's clause, וַיִּרְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֥י הִֽתְבָּאֲשׁ֖וּ עִם דָּוִ֑יד (WEB “When the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David,”), where כִּ֥י is the object complementizer completing the verb of seeing rather than a discourse-level causal connector, reconfigures Ammon's role from host of a rebuffed embassy to hirer of Aramean mercenaries — a genuine participant-role shift even though no grammatical break accompanies it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this unit through v.9 (Ammon's muster) as one Ammon-response block is a live alternative, since the wayyiqtol chain never breaks between v.5 and v.9 and the same participants persist throughout; the case for stopping at v.5 rests entirely on content (the directive's resolution, the shift from host to hirer) rather than on any grammatical seam, which is why confidence is lowered here from high to medium. A pe stands after v.3 as well (oshb:1Chr.19.3, pe, single-witness), weak tier-3 texture against this row's own internal unity (vv.1-5); it is disclosed here alongside the pe after v.7 (oshb:1Chr.19.7, pe, single-witness), weak tier-3 texture against carrying the unit through v.9 -- neither mark is decisive, both are on the record.

boundary_rationale: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֥י הִֽתְבָּאֲשׁ֖וּ עִם דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח חָ֠נוּן וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן אֶ֣לֶף כִּכַּר כֶּ֗סֶף לִשְׂכֹּ֣ר לָ֠הֶם מִן אֲרַ֨ם נַהֲרַ֜יִם וּמִן אֲרַ֤ם מַעֲכָה֙ וּמִצּוֹבָ֔ה רֶ֖כֶב וּפָרָשִֽׁים (v.6, WEB “When the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David,”) opens the hiring of Aramean chariots, וַיִּשְׂכְּר֣וּ לָהֶ֡ם שְׁנַיִם֩ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף רֶ֗כֶב וְאֶת מֶ֤לֶךְ מַעֲכָה֙ וְאֶת עַמּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י מֵידְבָ֑א וּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן נֶאֶסְפוּ֙ מֵעָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (v.7, WEB “So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah with his people, who came and encamped near Medeba. The children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle.”), then Joab's tactical read, וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹאָ֗ב כִּֽי הָיְתָ֧ה פְנֵי הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו פָּנִ֣ים וְאָח֑וֹר וַיִּבְחַ֗ר מִכָּל בָּחוּר֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ לִקְרַ֥את אֲרָֽם (v.10, WEB “Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose some of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians.”), and his charge to Abishai, חֲזַ֤ק וְנִֽתְחַזְּקָה֙ בְּעַד עַמֵּ֔נוּ וּבְעַ֖ד עָרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָ֔ה הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה (v.13, WEB “Be courageous, and let’s be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. May Yahweh do that which seems good to him.””). This ראה+כי construction recurs five times within 19:6-19 itself (vv.6, 10, 15, 16, 19) and eight times book-wide across 10:5-28:10 at a three-word proximity window (10:5, 19:6, 19:10, 19:15, 19:16, 19:19, 21:28, 28:10), so it cannot by itself discriminate v.16 as a fresh round; what does discriminate v.15 as this unit's close is its form: וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֤וֹן רָאוּ֙ כִּי נָ֣ס אֲרָ֔ם (WEB “When the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled,”) fronts the subject before a qatal verb, a backgrounded, summarizing notice, against the wayyiqtol-initial forms that open the two fresh rounds at v.6 and v.16 (v.10 is Joab's own tactical read rather than a round-opener, and v.19 functions in the following row, M8-1Chr-106, as that unit's own closing verse rather than an opening one). The unit closes on Joab's arrival at Jerusalem, וַיָּבֹ֥א יוֹאָ֖ב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (v.15, WEB “Then Joab came to Jerusalem.”) — an arrival notice (וַיָּבֹ֥א), not the book's genuine return formula (שוב); that return verb occurs just once, at 20:3's וַיָּ֧שָׁב דָּוִ֛יד וְכָל הָעָ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם. The arrival-verb clause recurs on its own, unit-internally, at 21:4, וַיָּבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם ('and he came to Jerusalem') -- its accent there differs from this verse's own accent on the same verb, so the two are not one repeated form -- so neither verb alone carries this unit's own close. What does close the unit is the combination of v.15's backgrounded syntax with the change of acting party at v.16, וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֗ם כִּ֣י (WEB “When the Syrians saw that they were defeated by Israel,”) — the same wayyiqtol-initial hinge as v.6, but now Aram itself is the acting subject rather than Ammon's hired help, marking a fresh round rather than a continuation. A pe stands after v.7 (oshb:1Chr.19.7, pe, single-witness), span-internal; a samekh also stands span-internally after v.12 (oshb:1Chr.19.12, samekh, single-witness) -- both disclosed here rather than passed over. A further pe stands after v.15 itself (oshb:1Chr.19.15, pe, single-witness); since this row's own span runs 19:6-19:15, that mark sits on the span's own closing edge -- the 19:15/19:16 seam with the following row, M8-1Chr-106 -- not span-internally, and is weak single-witness corroboration of that close, never a driver.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 19:6-19 as one undivided war episode is a live alternative, since the ראה+כי hinge recurs five times through the stretch and cannot alone divide it; the case for closing at v.15 instead rests on its backgrounded waw-subject-qatal form (against the wayyiqtol-initial forms opening the two fresh rounds at v.6 and v.16) together with v.16's change of acting party from Ammon's hired proxies to Aram itself.

boundary_rationale: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֗ם כִּ֣י נִגְּפוּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיּוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֶת אֲרָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשׁוֹפַ֛ךְ שַׂר צְבָ֥א הֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר לִפְנֵיהֶֽם (v.16, WEB “When the Syrians saw that they were defeated by Israel,”) opens the second, escalated round, in which David himself rather than Joab takes the field: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗יד וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם וַיַּעֲרֹ֨ךְ דָּוִ֜יד לִקְרַ֤את אֲרָם֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ (v.17, WEB “David was told that, so he gathered all Israel together, passed over the Jordan, came to them, and set the battle in array against them. So when David had put the battle in array against the Syrians, they fought with him.”). The unit closes on an inclusio: v.19's own כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל echoes v.16's opening כִּ֣י נִגְּפוּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒, framing the whole engagement, and the verse's close, וְלֹא אָבָ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת בְּנֵי עַמּ֖וֹן עֽוֹד (WEB “The Syrians would not help the children of Ammon any more.”), settles Aram's part in the war rather than the Ammonite campaign as a whole, which continues past this verse at 20:1's וַיַּשְׁחֵ֣ת אֶת אֶ֣רֶץ בְּנֵֽי עַמּ֗וֹן and 20:3's לְכֹ֖ל עָרֵ֣י בְנֵי עַמּ֑וֹן. The seam is instead argued from the fresh temporal frame that opens 20:1, וַיְהִ֡י לְעֵת֩ תְּשׁוּבַ֨ת הַשָּׁנָ֜ה לְעֵ֣ת צֵ֣את הַמְּלָכִ֗ים (WEB “At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out,”), which marks time by the annual campaigning season rather than by 'after this,' together with the v.16/v.19 inclusio that brackets this unit as Aram's own engagement, now closed, distinct from the Ammon siege that resumes under Joab alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with 20:1-3 as one continuous Ammon campaign is a live alternative on participant-tracking grounds alone, since 19:19b's withdrawal of Aram is continuity evidence for the war, not separation evidence; the case for a seam rests instead on the v.16/v.19 כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל inclusio closing Aram's own engagement and on 20:1's fresh campaigning-season frame, not on Aram's disappearance from the following verses.

boundary_rationale: This unit is marked off by its own opener, distinct from the "after this" formula used around it: "וַיְהִ֡י לְעֵת֩ תְּשׁוּבַ֨ת הַשָּׁנָ֜ה לְעֵ֣ת צֵ֣את הַמְּלָכִ֗ים" (v.1, WEB "At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out"), an annual-campaign frame that stages Joab's siege, "וַיַּ֥ךְ יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת רַבָּ֖ה וַיֶּֽהֶרְסֶֽהָ" (v.1, WEB "Joab struck Rabbah, and overthrew it"), while David stays behind in Jerusalem. It closes on the return-home notice, "וַיָּ֧שָׁב דָּוִ֛יד וְכָל הָעָ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם" (v.3, WEB "David and all the people returned to Jerusalem"), a pe following in WLC (single-witness) corroborating the pause before v.4 resumes the "after this" device for an unrelated theater, "וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַתַּעֲמֹ֧ד מִלְחָמָ֛ה בְּגֶ֖זֶר" (WEB "After this, war arose at Gezer"), against the Philistines rather than Ammon.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 20:1-8 as one Philistine-and-Ammon war summary loses because 20:4's "after this" plus its shift to Gezer/Gath and to individual champion duels is the same device the book uses elsewhere to open a fresh report, not to continue one.

boundary_rationale: וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַתַּעֲמֹ֧ד מִלְחָמָ֛ה בְּגֶ֖זֶר עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים אָ֣ז הִכָּ֞ה סִבְּכַ֣י הַחֻֽשָׁתִ֗י אֶת סִפַּ֛י מִילִדֵ֥י הָרְפָאִ֖ים וַיִּכָּנֵֽעוּ (v.4, WEB “After this, war arose at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, of the sons of the giant; and they were subdued.”) opens a third Philistine theater. A pe stands after 20:3 itself (oshb:1Chr.20.3, pe, single-witness), on this row's own opening edge (the 20:3/20:4 seam argued here), weak non-driving corroboration only. The three champion-notices are bound not by a shared refrain but by a נכה-chain: v.4's אָ֣ז הִכָּ֞ה סִבְּכַ֣י הַחֻֽשָׁתִ֗י (WEB “Sibbecai the Hushathite killed”), v.5's וַיַּ֞ךְ אֶלְחָנָ֣ן (WEB “Elhanan ... killed”), and v.7's וַיַּכֵּ֨הוּ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן (WEB “Jonathan ... killed him”) — the same binding device (though not the same formula) that ch.18's own נכה-chain uses, וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים, וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת, וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛יד אֶת הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר; ch.18 nowhere uses וַתְּהִי ע֥וֹד מִלְחָמָ֖ה, so that phrase is not the shared comparandum. Within the catalogue, וַתְּהִי ע֥וֹד מִלְחָמָ֖ה does bind the second and third notices as a secondary link, וַתְּהִי ע֥וֹד מִלְחָמָ֖ה (v.5) and וַתְּהִי ע֥וֹד מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּגַ֑ת (v.6), but v.4 does not carry it, opening instead on וַתַּעֲמֹ֧ד with no ע֥וֹד. The unit closes on the tally, אֵ֛ל נוּלְּד֥וּ לְהָרָפָ֖א בְּגַ֑ת וַיִּפְּל֥וּ בְיַד דָּוִ֖יד וּבְיַד עֲבָדָֽיו (v.8, WEB “These were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.”); the summary head is the anomalous short demonstrative אֵ֛ל — the only verse-initial אל in the book used demonstratively (the sole other instance, 16:22, is the negative particle) — rather than the אלה that opens verse-initially thirteen times elsewhere in the book (a consonantal sweep confirms the count exactly) -- of which roughly five function as closural summaries (4:38, 8:28, 9:34, 24:19, 26:19; e.g. 9:34's אֵלֶּה֩ רָאשֵׁ֨י הָאָב֧וֹת) and several others as register heads introducing what follows rather than closing it (1:29, 2:1, 2:50, 5:14, 23:24) -- with a further seventeen ואלה openings noted separately as a related but distinct device -- so the closure rests on the collective tally clause וַיִּפְּל֥וּ בְיַד itself rather than on an assumed אלה head. A pe follows v.8 in WLC (single-witness), weakly corroborating that close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting each champion-notice (v.4, v.5, vv.6-7) into its own row is a live alternative, since only vv.5-6 share the וַתְּהִי ע֥וֹד מִלְחָמָ֖ה refrain and v.4 stands apart from it; what actually binds all three into one catalogue is the נכה-chain running v.4/v.5/v.7, closed by the collective tally in v.8, which is the real ground for keeping the notices as one row.

boundary_rationale: A wholly new grammatical subject opens this unit: וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֥ד שָׂטָ֖ן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל, rendered by WEB as ‘Satan stood up against Israel,’ (v.1), introduces an agent with no antecedent anywhere in this passage (a book-wide hapax) and launches a self-contained cause-and-effect chain: incitement (1), royal command to Joab (2), Joab's protest (3), the command's prevailing and its province-wide execution (4-5), and a scope-limiting exception. That exception is the unit's true close: וְלֵוִי֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן לֹ֥א פָקַ֖ד בְּתוֹכָ֑ם (WEB ‘he didn’t count Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.’) is a fronted-topic, negated-qatal clause (פָקַ֖ד, a finite Qal qatal 3ms 'he did not count,' negated and preceded by the fronted subject וְלֵוִי֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן) that interrupts the wayyiqtol chain rather than continuing it, tidying off Joab's report before the narrative moves on; its second clause, כִּֽי נִתְעַ֥ב דְּבַר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת יוֹאָֽב, carries its own finite verb, a Niphal qatal נִתְעַ֥ב. The next verse breaks the human-administrative frame: its opening clause, וַיֵּ֨רַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה (WEB ‘God was displeased’), is an evaluative impersonal clause — הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים is the nomen rectum of the construct בְּעֵינֵ֣י, not the verb's grammatical subject — and the actual shift to a divine agent occurs in the clause that follows it, וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (WEB ‘therefore he struck Israel.’), an unexpressed-subject wayyiqtol whose referent is God; together the two clauses move the story from bureaucratic execution to divine evaluation and action, which is where this unit properly yields to the next.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 21:7 as this unit's direct consequence and folding it in would erase the shift from Joab's human report to God's evaluation-and-strike that the Chronicler uses to open the judgment sequence, even though the subject change proper falls in v.7's second clause (וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) rather than its first.

boundary_rationale: This short unit opens exactly where the census report closed: the new subject of וַיֵּ֨רַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיַּ֖ךְ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (‘it was evil in the eyes of God concerning this thing... and he struck Israel’) answers 21:6’s Levi/Benjamin aside (וְלֵוִי֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן לֹ֥א פָקַ֖ד בְּתוֹכָ֑ם) with a verdict on the whole census. David’s reply follows without any change of scene or addressee, חָטָ֣אתִֽי מְאֹ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה (‘I have sinned greatly, in that I have done this thing,’ WEB), so judgment and confession form one tight beat. The single-witness WLC places a petuchah after v.7 itself (oshb:1Chr.21.7, pe, single-witness), which could suggest an even finer cut between judgment and confession, but that division is not allowed to drive here: the confession is David’s immediate answer to the very verdict just announced, with no new speaker introduced to whom it is addressed. A second petuchah follows this row's own closing verse, v.8, itself (oshb:1Chr.21.8, pe, single-witness) -- distinguishing the two petuchot in this short span: one internal, after v.7, which this row declines to follow as a divider; one on the closing edge, after v.8, weak single-witness corroboration of the seam into v.9's fresh word-event frame. The unit ends where a formal word-event frame opens fresh business: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל גָּ֔ד חֹזֵ֥ה דָוִ֖יד לֵאמֹֽר (‘Yahweh spoke to Gad, David’s seer, saying’) brings in a new addressee and a new communication channel that v.8 has no part in.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v.7 from v.8 at the WLC petuchah would sever an immediate verdict from the confession it provokes, with no change of speaker or addressee to justify treating them as separate scenes.

boundary_rationale: The commissioning formula וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל גָּ֔ד חֹזֵ֥ה דָוִ֖יד לֵאמֹֽר opens a distinct communication event — Yahweh addressing a named intermediary rather than continuing the direct David-and-God exchange of v.8 — a message-and-delivery pattern (commission to the seer, seer's journey, seer's delivery) this passage does not use anywhere else in vv.1-8. The messenger formula כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר occurs twice, but only once as an actual relay: v.10's לֵךְ֩ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֶל דָּוִ֜יד לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר is a 2ms imperative-plus-weqatal addressed to Gad — Yahweh instructing Gad what to say, not Gad relaying anything yet — and Gad's actual delivery begins only at v.11, וַיָּ֥בֹא גָ֖ד אֶל דָּוִ֑יד וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֛וֹ כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה קַבֶּל לָֽךְ (WEB ‘So Gad came to David and said to him, “Yahweh says, ‘Take your choice:’). The three-item list of v.12 sits inside that delivered speech rather than opening a new scene. The unit closes on David's decisive answer to Gad, וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛יד אֶל גָּ֖ד צַר לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד (WEB ‘David said to Gad, “I am in distress.’), resolving the choice the oracle posed. A pe stands at the opening edge itself, after 21:8 (oshb:1Chr.21.8, pe, single-witness), weakly corroborating the seam at v.8/v.9; internally, the single-witness WLC opens a second petuchah right after v.12 (oshb:1Chr.21.12, pe, single-witness), dividing the offer from the reply, but that cut falls inside one continuous exchange and does not rise to a row boundary here. The next verse, וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה דֶּ֖בֶר (14, WEB ‘So Yahweh sent a pestilence’), executes the chosen punishment and opens a new movement.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at the pe after v.12 to isolate David's one-verse reply would break a single question-and-answer exchange between Gad and David into two fragments neither of which stands as its own scene.

boundary_rationale: David's choice from the previous unit is carried out at once: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה דֶּ֖בֶר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּפֹּל֙ (14, WEB ‘So Yahweh sent a pestilence on Israel,’) switches from deliberation to enactment and opens this scene. Within it, the site that will matter for the rest of the arc is named for the first time: וּמַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֔ד עִם גֹּ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֥ן הַיְבוּסִֽי (15, WEB ‘Yahweh’s angel was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.’) fixes the location before David has even seen the angel (16) or Ornan has appeared as a character. A samekh stands after v.15 itself (oshb:1Chr.21.15, samekh, single-witness), inside this span; it is disclosed here rather than left to stand unremarked, and does not drive the boundary. The unit closes on the terminal clause of David's prayer over the vision, not its atnach-marked first half, וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ (17, ‘but these sheep, what have they done?’), but the petition that follows it to the verse's end, יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֗י תְּהִ֨י נָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ בִּ֚י וּבְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֔י וּֽבְעַמְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א לְמַגֵּפָֽה (WEB ‘Please let your hand, O Yahweh my God, be against me and against my father’s house; but not against your people, that they should be plagued.”’). That closing term, לְמַגֵּפָֽה, recurs at 21:22's וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם (WEB 'that the plague may be stopped from afflicting the people.') -- but 21:22 sits five verses inside the following row's own span (M8-1Chr-113: 21:18-21:27), so the shared vocabulary is a cross-boundary cohesion tie this row must absorb, not closural evidence for a division at 21:17/18; the close rests instead on what is internal to v.17 itself: the petition as the prayer's own terminal clause and the change of speaker and mode that follows at v.18. The single-witness WLC sets a setumah right after v.17 (oshb:1Chr.21.17, samekh, single-witness), corroborating the break: the next clause changes speaker and mode entirely, וּמַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֶל גָּ֖ד לֵאמֹ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד (18, WEB ‘Then Yahweh’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to Yahweh on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.’), moving from David's prayer to a fresh instruction relayed through Gad.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through v.18's instruction would blur David's completed prayer into the start of an action he has not yet taken, when the angel's command to Gad plainly opens new business.

boundary_rationale: This unit's core bracket is lexical, not a full command-to-completion inclusio: the phrase מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה recurs byte-identically (accents included) in the opening instruction, וּמַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֶל גָּ֖ד לֵאמֹ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד כִּ֣י יַעֲלֶ֣ה דָוִ֗יד לְהָקִ֤ים מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה בְּגֹ֖רֶן אָרְנָ֥ן הַיְבֻסִֽי (18, WEB ‘Then Yahweh’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to Yahweh on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.’), and in its completion, וַיִּבֶן֩ שָׁ֨ם דָּוִ֤יד מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה (26, WEB ‘David built an altar to Yahweh there,’), so the command-to-completion bracket proper closes at v.26, not v.27, where the grammatical subject shifts to Yahweh, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ (27, WEB ‘Then Yahweh commanded the angel,’); the bracket phrase itself does not recur there, but word-level comparison shows the shared vocabulary against v.18 does not shrink to the divine name alone -- both verses also share the particle לֵאמֹ֣ר, the מלאך root (וּמַלְאַ֧ךְ / לַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ), and the אמר root (אָמַ֥ר / וַיֹּ֤אמֶר) -- strengthening rather than weakening the case for holding v.27 in the span on the angel-and-sword frame. Everything between v.18 and v.26 serves the altar arc: David's compliance (19), Ornan's noticing the angel and the arrival at his threshing floor (20-21), the purchase request מְק֣וֹם הַגֹּ֔רֶן וְאֶבְנֶה בּ֥וֹ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַיהוָ֑ה (22), Ornan's counter-offer (23), David's refusal to take it free, כִּֽי קָנֹ֥ה אֶקְנֶ֖ה בְּכֶ֣סֶף מָלֵ֑א (24), the payment (25), and the theophany that answers the purchased altar, וַיַּ֥עַל עֹל֖וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָא֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּֽעֲנֵ֤הוּ בָאֵשׁ֙ מִן הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם עַ֖ל מִזְבַּ֥ח הָעֹלָֽה (26, WEB ‘and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on Yahweh; and he answered him from the sky by fire on the altar of burnt offering.’). v.27 belongs with this arc on a different ground: it answers not the altar bracket but the drawn-sword threat David saw at v.16, וְחַרְבּ֤וֹ שְׁלוּפָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ נְטוּיָ֖ה עַל יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (WEB ‘having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem.’); v.27's וַיָּ֥שֶׁב חַרְבּ֖וֹ אֶל נְדָנָֽהּ (WEB ‘and he put his sword back into its sheath.’) is that threat's resolution, so the whole span from the first sight of the drawn sword through its sheathing forms the arc's true frame, with the fire-answered altar as its centerpiece. Ornan's entry at v.20 shifts the camera to a new character but not to a new task, so it reads as a viewpoint change within one job rather than a fresh row. The WLC tradition opens a petuchah between vv.26 and 27 (oshb:1Chr.21.26, pe, single-witness); that would separate the altar-building from the sword's sheathing, but the division cuts across the single cause (the fire answer) and its single effect (the sword-threat ends), so it is disclosed rather than followed. On the opening edge, v.18 itself supplies a discourse-initial signal: וּמַלְאַ֧ךְ יְהוָ֛ה אָמַ֥ר fronts its subject rather than continuing a wayyiqtol chain out of v.17's prayer, marking a clean break from David's petition, וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַצֹּ֖אן מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ...לֹ֥א לְמַגֵּפָֽה, with a samekh standing after v.17 itself (oshb:1Chr.21.17, samekh, single-witness) weakly corroborating that seam. The next verse turns from action to explanation — בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא — and belongs to a different kind of unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at Ornan's introduction (v.20) or at the pe after v.26 would carve one purchase-and-theophany action into pieces that share the same command, the same site, and the same resolution; the pe after v.26 in particular divides the fire-answered altar from the sword's sheathing that the fire directly causes, even though the מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה inclusio proper closes there and not at v.27.

boundary_rationale: This is the arc's most contested seam, and it deserves its own accounting. The unit opens on a resumptive temporal frame not used anywhere earlier in the chapter, בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא בִּרְא֤וֹת (‘at that time, when David saw,’ 28), which steps back from the just-completed action (27's sword-sheathing) to explain it, and the same phrase recurs almost immediately, בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא (29, ‘at that time’), this time locating the standing tabernacle ‘in the high place at Gibeon,’ בַּבָּמָ֖ה בְּגִבְעֽוֹן. The repetition ties 28-29 together as one rationale, completed by v.30's negative clause, וְלֹא יָכֹ֥ל דָּוִ֛יד לָלֶ֥כֶת לְפָנָ֖יו לִדְרֹ֣שׁ אֱלֹהִ֑ים (‘David couldn't go before it to inquire of God’): the Chronicler is explaining why the Ornan site, not Gibeon, became the place of sacrifice. David's declaration in 22:1, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד זֶ֣ה ה֔וּא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְזֶה מִּזְבֵּ֥חַ לְעֹלָ֖ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל (‘This is the house of Yahweh God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel’), is read here as the payoff of that rationale rather than as the start of new material: its demonstratives זֶ֣ה/וְזֶה have no referent of their own and can only point back to the site the previous three verses have just been justifying. Against this, the strongest case for treating 22:1 as the head of the temple-preparation material instead is lexical: בֵּ֖ית is absent from 28-30's own cultic vocabulary, which speaks only of וּמִשְׁכַּ֣ן and וּמִזְבַּ֥ח, and its temple-building sense debuts only in 22:1, then immediately again in 22:2's לִבְנ֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים. The lexeme itself is not new to this arc — v.17's petition already used it once, in a different sense, וּבְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֔י (‘and against my father's house,’ 21:17), naming David's own household rather than Yahweh's — but that occurrence does not anticipate the temple usage, so the rival reading is not dismissed outright and is treated as the genuine one it is. The WLC single witness places a samekh after both v.30 and 22:1 (oshb:1Chr.21.30, samekh, single-witness; oshb:1Chr.22.1, samekh, single-witness), bracketing 22:1 on both sides; that pattern is compatible with either reading and is not used to settle it, but it is disclosed because it is the clearest sign in the manuscript tradition that this verse was felt to be transitional. On balance the backward-pointing deixis is treated as the deciding tier-1 signal, so the unit is read as closing the census-plague-altar arc rather than opening ch.22's material register, and 22:2's fresh administrative action (with no deictic tie back to ‘this’) is where the next unit truly starts.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 22:1 as the opening verse of the temple-preparation unit is a live alternative on lexical grounds (בֵּ֖ית's temple-building sense debuts there, absent from 21:28-30's own cultic vocabulary), but it strands 22:1's demonstratives without the antecedent that only 21:28-30 supplies.

boundary_rationale: 1Chr.22.1 and 1Chr.22.2 open with the same nineteen-character formula (nineteen Unicode code points, including the interior space), וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד, and it recurs a third time at v.5, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗יד; the difference that determines this row's opening edge is not the formula itself but what follows it. A samekh follows 22:1 itself (oshb:1Chr.22.1, samekh, single-witness), tier-3 corroboration of this row's own opening edge, matching the same reference's disclosure in decision 114. v.1's וַיֹּ֣אמֶר introduces a direct declarative quotation, זֶ֣ה ה֔וּא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (WEB ‘said, “This is the house of Yahweh God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”’), the site-declaration this arc already closed on in decision 114; v.2's וַיֹּ֣אמֶר instead governs an infinitival directive, לִכְנוֹס֙ אֶת הַגֵּרִ֔ים (WEB ‘gave orders to gather together the foreigners’), naming its own objects rather than pointing back to v.1's ‘this’ by any demonstrative of its own. After the site is named, the narrative pivots to hardware, continuing with iron, וּבַרְזֶ֣ל לָ֠רֹב (3, WEB ‘David prepared iron in abundance’), and cedar, וַעֲצֵ֥י אֲרָזִ֖ים לְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר (4, WEB ‘and cedar trees without number,’). Between vv.4 and 5 the single-witness WLC likewise opens a petuchah (oshb:1Chr.22.4, pe, single-witness), separating the materials list from David's closing reflection in v.5 — which recurs the same וַיֹּ֣אמֶר-plus-direct-quotation pattern as v.1, שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִי֮ נַ֣עַר וָרָךְ֒ (WEB ‘“Solomon my son is young and tender,’) — but that reflection gives the reason for the very gathering just narrated and ends by restating it, וַיָּ֧כֶן דָּוִ֛יד לָרֹ֖ב לִפְנֵ֥י מוֹתֽוֹ (WEB ‘So David prepared abundantly before his death.’), so it reads as this unit's summarizing close rather than a fresh beat: its direct-speech form echoes v.1 formally, but its content closes v.2's own gathering action rather than opening a new declaration, and the pe is disclosed without being treated as a row divider. This is a content-level argument, not the form-level test that opened this row's own left edge at v.2 (where an infinitival directive, rather than a further direct declaration, marked the restart): the two edges are governed by different discriminators because v.1's and v.2's forms differ while v.1's and v.5's forms are the same. The next verse changes both mode and addressee: וַיִּקְרָ֖א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה (‘he called for Solomon his son’) moves from third-person preparation to a face-to-face summons that opens direct instruction.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v.5 off at the pe after v.4 would separate David's stated reason for gathering materials from the materials themselves, when v.5 functions as the passage's own rationale and summary for vv.2-4.

boundary_rationale: The summons וַיִּקְרָ֖א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֑וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֨הוּ֙ לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (6, WEB ‘Then he called for Solomon his son, and commanded him to build a house for Yahweh, the God of Israel.’) opens a single continuous address from David to Solomon whose outer frame — speaker David, addressee Solomon — never changes hands all the way to v.16's closing imperative, ק֣וּם וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה וִיהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ (‘Arise and be doing, and may Yahweh be with you’). At the embedded level the speech does shift: a לֵאמֹ֔ר-framed quotation at v.8, וַיְהִ֨י עָלַ֤י דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר (WEB ‘Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,’), opens a first-person divine speaker addressing David in the second person — שָׁפַ֔כְתָּ, לֹֽא תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֨יִת֙ לִשְׁמִ֔י (8), עָשִׂ֑יתָ — through v.10's הֽוּא יִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֨יִת֙ לִשְׁמִ֔י, before עַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֔י (11, ‘now, my son’) restores the David-to-Solomon axis. This embedded oracle stays inside David's host speech not because of the לֵאמֹ֔ר-frame itself -- that frame word also closes the oracle-relay of 21:9, לֵאמֹֽר (differing from 22:8's לֵאמֹ֔ר only in cantillation and metheg), and v.6's summons carries no such frame at all -- but because of what stands inside the frame: v.8's word is embedded in David's own first-person recollection, 'God said TO ME,' עָלַ֤י דְּבַר יְהוָה֙, whereas 21:9's is a narrator-level wayyiqtol addressed outward to Gad. The לֵאמֹ֔ר-frame is an accompanying feature of both, not the reason the two are structurally different. After the embedded oracle, David's address later shifts again into an inventory of what he has stockpiled, וְהִנֵּ֨ה בְעָנְיִ֜י הֲכִינ֣וֹתִי לְבֵית יְהוָ֗ה (14, ‘now, behold, in my affliction I have prepared for Yahweh's house’); this too stays within the unbroken outer address. A samekh stands after v.6 in its entirety — following the summons, Solomon's name, and the charge to build already given within that verse — immediately before v.7's direct discourse opens (oshb:1Chr.22.6, samekh, single-witness); the summons and the speech it introduces are too tightly bound to divide there. The unit ends because the next verse changes both addressee and occasion: וַיְצַ֤ו דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעְזֹ֖ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֽוֹ (‘David commanded all the princes of Israel,’ 17) turns from the private charge to Solomon to a public charge to the officials.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Elevating the embedded oracle at v.8-10 (or its resumption at v.11) to a row seam would mistake a לֵאמֹ֔ר-framed quotation within David's own speech for a new communication event; the outer frame's speaker and addressee never change across vv.7-16, unlike the genuinely new events at 21:9 and v.6 itself.

boundary_rationale: The addressee change that closed the previous unit opens this one: וַיְצַ֤ו דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעְזֹ֖ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֽוֹ (17, WEB ‘David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,’) moves the charge from a private father-son address to a public command to the nation's officials. (WEB's closing 'saying,' here is a translator supply: the MT clause itself ends on לִשְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֽוֹ, oshb:1Chr.22.17, with no Hebrew speech-frame word -- the same translator-only quotation opening recurs at WEB's v.18. The opening-edge argument rests instead on signals present in both witnesses: the addressee shift to second-person plural forms across vv.18-19, and the fresh command verb of v.17 itself, not on any unmarked speech frame.) The content shares its climax with the Solomon charge that precedes it — both pivot on עַתָּ֣ה (עַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֔י; עַתָּ֗ה תְּנ֤וּ) and close on a ק֣וּם-plus-action imperative (ק֣וּם וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה; וְק֗וּמוּ וּבְנוּ֙) — so the two charges are not built to distinct shapes; what differs is the lead-in and the addressee's number. This charge opens on a rhetorical question grounding the command in present security, הֲלֹ֨א יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם וְהֵנִ֥יחַ (18, ‘“Isn’t Yahweh your God with you? Hasn’t he given you rest’), where the Solomon charge instead opens on an oracle-recap (22:8-10); and it addresses the princes in the second-person plural throughout (אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם, לְבַבְכֶם֙, תְּנ֤וּ, וְק֗וּמוּ) against the 2ms David-to-Solomon forms of vv.7-16, the discriminator that actually separates the two charges. It leads into עַתָּ֗ה תְּנ֤וּ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְנַפְשְׁכֶ֔ם לִדְר֖וֹשׁ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם (19) and וְק֗וּמוּ וּבְנוּ֙ אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ֙ יְהוָ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים (‘arise and build the sanctuary of Yahweh God’), which closes both this charge and the chapter. The closing edge has its own textual warrant, not merely the assigned range: 23:1 opens with a disjunctive waw-plus-subject clause rather than continuing the wayyiqtol chain, וְדָוִ֥יד זָקֵ֖ן וְשָׂבַ֣ע יָמִ֑ים (WEB ‘Now David was old and full of days;’), and a pe stands at 22:19 itself (oshb:1Chr.22.19, pe, single-witness), weak tier-3 corroboration of that seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching v.17 to the Solomon charge that precedes it would ignore that David is now speaking to a different party for a different purpose -- mobilizing the princes rather than instructing his son -- which the object of the help-clause makes explicit.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens with the aged-king notice "וְדָוִ֥יד זָקֵ֖ן וְשָׂבַ֣ע יָמִ֑ים" (David was old and full of days) fused in the same verse to the succession act "וַיַּמְלֵ֛ךְ...שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" (he made Solomon his son king over Israel), matching WEB's own line "Now David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel." Verse 2 closes the notice with the gathering verb "וַיֶּאֱסֹף֙ אֶת כָּל שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּֽם" (he gathered together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites), naming the constituency for chs 23-27 without yet doing any administrative work itself. Verse 3 pivots to a fresh census-formula subject, "וַיִּסָּֽפְרוּ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה" (Levi's own men being tallied from age thirty upward), so the seam falls at 2/3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: One could fold 23:1-2 into 23:3-5 since the gathered assembly is precisely who gets counted next, but the gathering notice and the numeric census are functionally different acts, and the census formula is independently attested elsewhere in the book as its own device.

boundary_rationale: Begins with the census idiom וַיִּסָּֽפְרוּ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה (WEB ‘The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward;’). The counting verb וַיִּסָּֽפְרוּ֙ is a book-wide consonantal hapax, and the census idiom's own age frame ('mibben ... shanah wamalah', 'from N years old and upward') recurs once more in the book, at 23:24, but with a lowered numeral -- מִבֶּ֛ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה here at 23:3, against מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָֽעְלָה at 23:24; a consonantal sweep of all 943 verses confirms each numeral-string is itself a book-wide singleton, so the two are not the same formula, only the same frame — not, as might be expected, in the Reuben/Gad/half-Manasseh muster at 5:18, which counts instead by capability (נֹשְׂאֵ֨י מָגֵ֤ן וְחֶ֨רֶב֙ וְדֹ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת וּלְמוּדֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה), or David's own census at 21:5, which counts by אִישׁ֙ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֔רֶב; this age formula belongs to ch.23 alone. Verses 4-5 break the 38,000 total into four named functions (temple overseers, officers and judges, doorkeepers, praise-singers), continuing the tally rather than opening reported speech: v.4 opens in the MT on the partitive מֵאֵ֗לֶּה (WEB ‘Of these’); the Hebrew itself supplies no verb of speaking, and the sole first-person form in it is עָשִׂ֖יתִי at v.5's close. WEB, by contrast, supplies a full subject-plus-finite-verb clause at its own v.4, 'David said, “Of these,”' -- not mere punctuation but an inferred attribution to David absent from the MT; resting the functional breakdown on the four named categories and their totals rather than on WEB's supplied speech verb, the inference that the attribution to David is supplied rather than stated is unaffected. Verse 6's wayyiqtol וַיֶּֽחָלְקֵ֥ם דָּוִ֖יד (WEB ‘David divided them’) switches to an entirely different organizing principle, division by ancestral clan rather than by function, so 5/6 is the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The functional breakdown might seem to anticipate the clan scheme that follows, but nothing in vv3-5 names Gershon, Kohath, or Merari -- the two organizing schemes never overlap in vocabulary, so they cannot share one row.

boundary_rationale: Verse 6, וַיֶּֽחָלְקֵ֥ם דָּוִ֖יד מַחְלְק֑וֹת לִבְנֵ֣י לֵוִ֔י לְגֵרְשׁ֖וֹן קְהָ֥ת וּמְרָרִֽי (WEB ‘David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.’), announces the tripartite scheme governing all of 23:6-23; it is one of the book's ten double-samekh verses per the campaign's book-wide mark survey, oshb:1Chr.23.6 (double samekh, single-witness) — tier-3 corroboration only, never the driver. Single-witness marks also stand after 23:7, 23:8, 23:9, and 23:11 -- the last sitting exactly at this row's own 11/12 closing seam -- plus one further samekh immediately beyond the span, after 23:12; the marks fall at finer, sub-clan grain than the clan-level division this row adopts, so both the supporting mark (23:11) and the complicating ones (23:7-9, cutting inside the span at the Ladan/Shimei sub-heads) are on the record. The operative register-head device is this scheme's own clan-level heading, one per clan: לַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י לַעְדָּ֥ן וְשִׁמְעִֽי opens Gershon at v.7, בְּנֵ֣י קְהָ֗ת opens Kohath at v.12 (decision 121), and בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ opens Merari at v.21 (decision 122) -- one row per clan, ranked by genealogical tier rather than by a shared formula: vv.7, 12, and 21 name the three sons of Levi announced in v.6, while vv.8-10 name Gershon's own sons. A real asymmetry the finer-division rival may fairly press is that the Gershon heading itself, לַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י לַעְדָּ֥ן וְשִׁמְעִֽי (lamed-gentilic), is a different construction from the construct-plural bene-X pattern shared by vv.12 and 21 and also by the subordinated sub-clan heads at vv.8-10, בְּנֵ֣י לַעְדָּ֗ן and בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְעִ֗י. This row's earlier discriminator — that only Gershon carries its own internal closing tallies, at v.9 and v.11 — is withdrawn as false and is not needed: Kohath's own head-verse at v.12 ends in a numeric tally (אַרְבָּעָֽה) exactly as Gershon's do (v.8 שְׁלֹשָֽׁה, v.10 אַרְבָּעָֽה), Merari's v.23 closes the same way (שְׁלֹשָֽׁה), the chief-and-second ranking of v.11 recurs identically at v.20 (מִיכָ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְיִשִּׁיָּ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי) and more elaborately at v.19's full first-through-fourth run, and the ‘these are...’ summary formula closes the whole three-clan block again at v.24. Two further register-heads of the same בני-X type stand inside this span without dividing it — בְּנֵ֣י לַעְדָּ֗ן at v.8 and בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְעִ֗י at v.9 (whose own tally, שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה, closes under a summary tag that names Ladan rather than Shimei, אֵ֛לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י הָאָב֖וֹת לְלַעְדָּֽן, a head/referent mismatch present in both witnesses) and again at v.10 (וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְעִ֔י, a four-name, four-count list) — and the granularity principle that keeps them from forcing a finer split is that they name sub-clan lineages (Ladan, Shimei) within Gershon, one register level below the clan headings themselves; only the clan-level headings at vv.7/12/21 chunk the material into rows, matching how decisions 121 and 122 are themselves bounded. Read this way, the case for keeping this row at 23:6-11 rests on the surviving clan-heading device and its parity with siblings 121-122, not on the withdrawn tally claim; the case for merging into a single 23:6-23 span is that no verse-internal device is in fact unique to Gershon, so a reader could reasonably ask why the clan level is the chosen grain rather than the finer sub-clan level (which would also divide at vv.8/9/10) or the coarser undivided level. Both dispositions are argued here for the ruling body; the frozen span is not altered by this response.
strongest_rejected_alternative: 23:6-23 as one undifferentiated three-clan list remains the named rival; it is not defeated by any device unique to this row's own span; the clan-level headings at vv.7/12/21 (Gershon/Kohath/Merari) are what keep this row distinct as filed, on parity with siblings 121 and 122, but the tally-and-ranking discriminator this row previously relied on is withdrawn as false, since Kohath and Merari carry the identical devices; that withdrawal is the reason 'medium' confidence is not raised by this repair.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the clan head בְּנֵ֣י קְהָ֗ת עַמְרָ֥ם יִצְהָ֛ר חֶבְר֥וֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעָֽה (WEB ‘The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.’), the same clan-level ‘sons of X’ register head that opens Gershon at v.7 and Merari at v.21 (decisions 120 and 122), naming four sons who structure everything through v.20. All four of those four sons carry their own ‘sons of X’ heads inside this span -- בְּנֵ֥י עַמְרָ֖ם at v.13, בְּנֵ֥י יִצְהָ֖ר at v.18, בְּנֵ֖י חֶבְר֑וֹן at v.19, and בְּנֵ֖י עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל at v.20 itself -- a head-initial verse can still terminate this row, since the true tier-1 seam is v.21's parallel clan-level head opening the next clan, not any device internal to v.20, and the same formula type as v.12's own; this row concedes those interior heads rather than denying them, and ranks them by tier rather than by literal roster-membership: interior heads stand at or below the generation of v.12's named sons and expand the lineage below them, rather than each literally naming one of v.12's own four sons. On that tier principle, four further bene-X heads inside Amram's own material are conceded on the same basis: בְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה at v.15 (Moses), בְּנֵ֥י גֵרְשׁ֖וֹם at v.16 (Gershom, Moses's own son), and בְנֵי אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר / וּבְנֵ֥י רְחַבְיָ֖ה at v.17 (Eliezer and Rehabiah) -- none of Moses, Gershom, Eliezer, or Rehabiah appears by name in v.12's four-son roster (Amram, Izhar, Hebron, Uzziel), but all stand one or more generations below Amram and expand his line, the same subordinate tier as vv.13/18/19/20's direct son-heads, rather than opening a fifth, independent clan alongside Gershon/Kohath/Merari. Amram's own material is qualitatively heavier than its siblings' — v.13-14 runs a consecration formula for Aaron, וַיִּבָּדֵ֣ל אַהֲרֹ֡ן לְֽהַקְדִּישׁוֹ֩ קֹ֨דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֤ים הֽוּא וּבָנָיו֙ עַד עוֹלָ֔ם לְהַקְטִיר֩ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה לְשָׁרְת֛וֹ וּלְבָרֵ֥ךְ בִּשְׁמ֖וֹ עַד עוֹלָֽם (WEB ‘Aaron was separated that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons forever,’), against the terse single-rank-or-paired tallies governing Gershom's, Izhar's, and Uzziel's lines (vv.16, 18, 20) -- only v.20's pair, מִיכָ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְיִשִּׁיָּ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי, is a genuine chief-and-second pairing; v.16 names one son as chief alone, and v.17's Eliezer entry, וְלֹא הָיָ֤ה לֶאֱלִיעֶ֨זֶר֙ בָּנִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים, explicitly has no other sons — but the weight difference does not change its structural rank: it stays subordinate material under Amram's son-level head, at the same rank as Izhar's and Hebron's briefer entries, rather than promoting to its own row. The section closes on Uzziel's pair in v.20, בְּנֵ֖י עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל מִיכָ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְיִשִּׁיָּ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי (WEB ‘The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.’). Verse 21's parallel clan-level head, בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙, opens the next clan, giving this row both a sharp open and a sharp close at the level that actually divides rows in this chapter. Single-witness marks stand inside this span at the sub-clan tier while the row divides at the clan tier: a samekh follows 23:12 itself (oshb:1Chr.23.12, samekh, single-witness), another follows 23:18 (oshb:1Chr.23.18, samekh, single-witness), and a third follows 23:20 (oshb:1Chr.23.20, samekh, single-witness) -- tier-3 material that corroborates this row's own close (the samekh after v.20 sits exactly at the 20/21 seam already argued) but complicates the interior, disclosed here matching the practice of siblings 114, 115, 116, 117, and 120.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A finer division at each interior head (23:13, 23:15, 23:16, 23:17, 23:18, 23:19, 23:20) is a live alternative now that those heads are conceded rather than denied; it is not preferred here because each names one of v.12's own four sons rather than an independent clan, the same subordination that keeps Ladan's and Shimei's heads (23:8-10) inside decision 120's Gershon row rather than splitting it further — but if that subordination argument is rejected, the finer split is the reading the mesh should weigh instead, per OL-121-1's own alternative.

boundary_rationale: Opens with בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֔י (WEB ‘The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.’), the third and final clan-level head of the tripartite division that opened this stretch (decision 120's v.6). Two further fronted bene-X heads recur inside this span, and are conceded here as the same register-head device this row's own opening (בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙) instantiates: בְּנֵ֥י מַחְלִ֖י אֶלְעָזָ֥ר וְקִֽישׁ ('the sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish') stands inside this row's own opening verse, v.21b, and בְּנֵ֣י מוּשִׁ֗י itself heads the closing tally at v.23. Ranked by the tier principle used in decisions 120 and 121, both name Merari's own grandsons, expanding the two sons (Mahli, Mushi) just announced in v.21a, rather than opening an independent clan; on the same principle, a finer division would cut inside v.21 itself, this row's own opening verse, the same granularity tension disclosed for siblings 120 and 121. It closes on the Mushi tally in v.23, בְּנֵ֣י מוּשִׁ֗י מַחְלִ֥י וְעֵ֛דֶר וִירֵמ֖וֹת שְׁלֹשָֽׁה (WEB ‘The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.’), whose closing count of ‘three’ repeats the same tally-word that closes the Ladan sub-list at v.8, בְּנֵ֣י לַעְדָּ֗ן הָרֹ֧אשׁ יְחִיאֵ֛ל וְזֵתָ֥ם וְיוֹאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשָֽׁה (WEB ‘The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three.’) — an in-book echo of form, not content. (The similarly worded שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה at v.9 belongs to a different tally, Shimei's three sons, and is followed by a summary tag naming Ladan, אֵ֛לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י הָאָב֖וֹת לְלַעְדָּֽן, which itself carries no numeral; the echo argued here is to v.8's genuine Ladan tally, not v.9's tag.) Verse 24 then shifts register with the summary tag אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵֽי לֵוִי֩ לְבֵ֨ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֜ם (WEB ‘These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses,’), which could be read either as this clan's own close or as the head of a reprise; that ambiguity belongs to the next boundary, not this one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through vv24-27 to keep the closing 'these' tag attached to Merari is plausible, but v24 explicitly regathers all three clans by a fresh name-count, not Merari alone, so it reads as a book-keeping bridge rather than Merari's own close.

boundary_rationale: This is the flagged joint between the courses list and the duties material. Verse 24 opens with אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵֽי לֵוִי֩ לְבֵ֨ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֜ם (WEB ‘These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses,’) and its own clause ends מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָֽעְלָה (WEB ‘from twenty years old and upward.’); v.27 closes an almost identical phrase, מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָֽעְלָה (WEB ‘from twenty years old and upward.’), bracketing vv.24-27 as the age-reduction rationale. Three coordinated causal clauses then carry the argument: v.25 כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר דָּוִ֔יד (‘for David said’), v.27 כִּ֣י בְדִבְרֵ֤י דָוִיד֙ הָאַ֣חֲרֹנִ֔ים הֵ֖מָּה (‘for by the last words of David...’), and v.28 כִּ֣י מַעֲמָדָ֞ם (‘for their duty was’). The service phrase לַעֲבֹדַת֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה is not confined to bracketing vv.28-32: it already stands in this row's own opening verse, v.24's לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה, and a book-wide consonantal sweep confirms exactly three occurrences of the phrase, at 23:24, 23:28 (where it is the fifth word-group of the verse, following כִּ֣י מַעֲמָדָ֞ם לְיַד בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֗ן, not its opening) and 23:32 (לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה, closing). Read this way the phrase is a three-fold refrain spanning v.24, v.28 and v.32 — the whole row, not an inner enclosure inside it — which strengthens rather than weakens the case for holding vv.24-32 together as one unit. That inner symmetry holds vv24-32 together as one argumentative unit even though its own opening relation to 23:6-23 remains genuinely disputable: v24's ‘these’ could equally be read as that earlier list's own close rather than this reprise's head. A pe follows this row's own closing verse, 23:32, itself (oshb:1Chr.23.32, pe, single-witness), weak corroboration of the closing seam into 24:1 without driving it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two rival readings compete for this row's own opening edge, and both are argued here rather than only one. Reading v.24's אֵ֣לֶּה as 23:6-23's own closing tally, attaching backward rather than heading this reprise, is the alternative the rationale itself calls genuinely disputable: 23:6-23 already closes its Merari sub-list on a numeral at v.23, שְׁלֹשָֽׁה, and ‘these were the sons of Levi... by their polls’ could summarize that count rather than open new material. It is not adopted here because v.24 immediately supplies its own new content — the age-twenty threshold and the census-idiom apparatus (לִפְקוּדֵיהֶ֗ם בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שֵׁמוֹת֙ לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָ֔ם) that 23:6-23 never uses — which reads as a fresh accounting rather than a repeated summary of the same one. Splitting at v.27/28 into a separate rationale row and a duties row is the second, forward-facing alternative; it is not adopted because the three coordinated for-clauses (25, 27, 28) and the v.24/28/32 service-phrase refrain build one continuous argument rather than two independent units.

boundary_rationale: The chapter break itself carries a register head, "וְלִבְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן מַחְלְקוֹתָ֑ם בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן נָדָב֙ וַאֲבִיה֔וּא אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאִיתָמָֽר" (and to the sons of Aaron [belonged] their divisions), rendered by WEB as "These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.", and reusing the same division-root already met at the head of 23:6, "וַיֶּֽחָלְקֵ֥ם דָּוִ֖יד מַחְלְק֑וֹת לִבְנֵ֣י לֵוִ֔י לְגֵרְשׁ֖וֹן קְהָ֥ת וּמְרָרִֽי" (David divided them, [the sons of Levi], into divisions), now applied to the priestly line rather than the wider Levite clans. 23:6 itself carries a WLC double-samekh (SAMEKH+SAMEKH, single-witness; oshb:1Chr.23.6, confirmed in pmarks_1Chr.json), disclosed here per the marker-doubling policy because the row cites the verse's wording as a comparandum; the doubling is noted strictly as a disclosure and is not treated as corroboration for this row's own seam. The unit narrates two of Aaron's sons dying without heirs, the king's division of the surviving Eleazar/Ithamar lines, and closes on the scribe Shemaiah's written record, "וַֽיִּכְתְּבֵ֡ם שְֽׁמַֽעְיָה֩ בֶן נְתַנְאֵ֨ל הַסּוֹפֵ֜ר מִן הַלֵּוִ֗י לִפְנֵ֨י הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים֙ וְצָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וַאֲחִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ בֶּן אֶבְיָתָ֔ר וְרָאשֵׁי֙ הָֽאָב֔וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם בֵּֽית אָ֣ב אֶחָ֗ד אָחֻז֙ לְאֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְאָחֻ֥ז אָחֻ֖ז לְאִיתָמָֽר" -- WEB: "Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, who was of the Levites, wrote them in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; one fathers’ house being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar.". Verse 7 opens a new idiom, "וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֤ל הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ לִיה֣וֹיָרִ֔יב לִֽידַעְיָ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי" (the first lot came out to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah), which resurfaces in nearly the same shape at 25:9, "וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֧ל הָרִאשׁ֛וֹן לְאָסָ֖ף לְיוֹסֵ֑ף גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֽוּא וְאֶחָ֥יו וּבָנָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר" (Asaph's line, through Joseph, drawing first there too) -- the shared opener marking the enumerated-lot sequence as a distinct sub-form from the procedural prose that precedes it here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching vv1-6 onto the tail of ch23's duties material is conceivable since both concern priestly service, but the chapter division plus the fresh divisions-of-Aaron head signal a new administrative act rather than a continuation of the reprise.

boundary_rationale: Opens with "וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֤ל הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ לִיה֣וֹיָרִ֔יב לִֽידַעְיָ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי" (the first lot came out to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah), which launches the priestly lot register -- but v7 itself mixes constituent order across its own two items (ordinal-then-name for Jehoiarib, name-then-ordinal for Jedaiah), so it cannot by itself license a single 'ordinal-plus-name' description of the refrain. The order that actually governs the refrain from the third lot on is name-then-ordinal: v8 reads "לְחָרִם֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לִשְׂעֹרִ֖ים הָרְבִעִֽי" (to Harim, the third; to Seorim, the fourth), and every remaining item through v18 repeats that lamed-prefixed name-first order without exception -- the reverse of a simple ordinal-first description, and the order this list's own refrain uses, not ch 25's: 25:10 opens ordinal-first, "הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֣י זַכּ֔וּר בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר" (the third, Zaccur). It closes on the summary tag "אֵ֣לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֞ם לַעֲבֹדָתָ֗ם לָב֤וֹא לְבֵית יְהוָה֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד אַהֲרֹ֣ן אֲבִיהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔הוּ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" (these were their offices for their service, to come to the house of Yahweh), a summary-style "these" closure capping the enumeration rather than adding independent content of its own. Verse 20's register head, "וְלִבְנֵ֥י לֵוִ֖י הַנּוֹתָרִ֑ים לִבְנֵ֤י עַמְרָם֙ שֽׁוּבָאֵ֔ל לִבְנֵ֥י שׁוּבָאֵ֖ל יֶחְדְּיָֽהוּ" (turning next to the Levites still left over), opens a differently-framed list, placing the seam at 19/20.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The closing ordinance of v19 could be pulled out as its own single-verse row -- a pe stands after 24:18 itself (oshb:1Chr.24.18, pe, single-witness), weak tier-3 corroboration for detaching v.19 that this row discloses rather than passes over -- but grammatically v.19 is the enumeration's own dependent summary clause, אֵ֣לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֞ם..., rather than free-standing narration; that syntactic dependency outranks the single-witness mark, so keeping it with the list it caps remains the more defensible reading.

boundary_rationale: Opens with "וְלִבְנֵ֥י לֵוִ֖י הַנּוֹתָרִ֑ים לִבְנֵ֤י עַמְרָם֙ שֽׁוּבָאֵ֔ל לִבְנֵ֥י שׁוּבָאֵ֖ל יֶחְדְּיָֽהוּ" (and of the sons of Levi who remained), where "who remained" explicitly flags a second, distinct list running back through the same clan lines ch23 already named -- but the chain must be read from MT alone, not from WEB's harmonized rendering. Amram's line continues through Shubael, "לִבְנֵ֤י עַמְרָם֙ שֽׁוּבָאֵ֔ל לִבְנֵ֥י שׁוּבָאֵ֖ל יֶחְדְּיָֽהוּ" (to the sons of Amram: Shubael; to the sons of Shubael: Jehdeiah), and Rehabiah, "לִרְחַבְיָ֑הוּ לִבְנֵ֣י רְחַבְיָ֔הוּ הָרֹ֖אשׁ יִשִּׁיָּֽה" (to Rehabiah: to the sons of Rehabiah, the chief was Isshiah); the Izharite line continues through Shelomoth, "לַיִּצְהָרִ֣י שְׁלֹמ֔וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י שְׁלֹמ֖וֹת יָֽחַת" (to the Izharite: Shelomoth; to the sons of Shelomoth: Jahath) -- לַיִּצְהָרִ֣י is the gentilic 'the Izharite,' not the personal name Izhar; the Uzzielite line continues through Micah, "בְּנֵ֤י עֻזִּיאֵל֙ מִיכָ֔ה לִבְנֵ֥י מִיכָ֖ה שמור שָׁמִֽיר" (the sons of Uzziel: Micah; to the sons of Micah: Shamir -- ketiv שמור, qere שָׁמִֽיר; the gloss 'Shamir' follows the qere); and the Merarite line continues through Mahli and Mushi, "בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֔י בְּנֵ֖י יַעֲזִיָּ֥הֽוּ בְנֽוֹ" (the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; the sons of Jaaziah, his son), down to Mushi's own three sons at v30. Hebron does not occur anywhere in this chapter -- a consonantal sweep of ch 24 returns zero hits -- and v23 itself, "וּבְנָ֖י יְרִיָּ֑הוּ אֲמַרְיָ֨הוּ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י יַחֲזִיאֵל֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י יְקַמְעָ֖ם הָרְבִיעִֽי", opens with 'and the sons of Jeriah' and names no clan of its own; WEB's rendering at v23, "The sons of Hebron: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.", supplies 'The sons of Hebron' as a harmonization to 23:19 with no counterpart in this MT clause, and this row does not rely on it. The list closes on the comparison formula "וַיַּפִּילוּ֩ גַם הֵ֨ם גּוֹרָל֜וֹת לְעֻמַּ֣ת אֲחֵיהֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי אַהֲרֹ֗ן לִפְנֵ֨י דָוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְצָד֣וֹק וַאֲחִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְרָאשֵׁי֙ הָֽאָב֔וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם אָב֣וֹת הָרֹ֔אשׁ לְעֻמַּ֖ת אָחִ֥יו הַקָּטָֽן" (these also cast lots like their brothers the sons of Aaron), which explicitly ties this list's lot-casting back to the priestly lots of 24:1-19. That comparison formula is not, however, this list's only closing candidate: v30 itself ends with its own full summary, "וּבְנֵ֣י מוּשִׁ֔י מַחְלִ֥י וְעֵ֖דֶר וִירִימ֑וֹת אֵ֛לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם" (these were the sons of the Levites after their fathers' households), which echoes 23:24's own closing formula, "אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵֽי לֵוִי֩ לְבֵ֨ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֜ם רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֣וֹת לִפְקוּדֵיהֶ֗ם בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שֵׁמוֹת֙ לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָ֔ם עֹשֵׂה֙ הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָֽעְלָה" (these were the sons of Levi after their fathers' households...), almost word for word, differing chiefly in הַלְוִיִּ֖ם (the gentilic-plural 'the Levites') for לֵוִי֩ (the tribal name 'Levi'). Whether that 'elleh' closure ends the register at v30, leaving v31's lot-casting as a dependent procedural coda rather than part of the same unit, is a live question this rewrite does not fully resolve: v31 opens with the wayyiqtol וַיַּפִּילוּ֩ ('and they cast'), with the emphatic subject גַם הֵ֨ם ('they also') following it rather than opening the verse itself; that emphatic subject presupposes and looks back on the roster v30 just closed rather than opening free-standing content of its own, and its own referent (הֵ֨ם, 'they,' i.e. the Levites just listed) has no antecedent without vv20-30 -- on that dependency the row keeps v31 attached rather than splitting at 24:30/31. The verse-initial wayyiqtol itself is conceded on the record as tier-1 evidence for the rival 30/31 seam already flagged for the boss round, even as the גַם הֵ֨ם dependency is what actually keeps this row's own disposition. How this corrected list relates to the fuller ch23 clan register remains a genuine open question this row does not resolve -- it is neither asserted as a duplicate nor merged with 23:6-23 -- so confidence stays tempered rather than treated as settled.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 24:20-31 into 24:1-19 as one continuous lot register is possible since v31 says 'these also' cast lots, but v20's independent register head and its wholly different name-chain content argue for keeping it a separate unit.

boundary_rationale: Introduces a subject and verb absent from everything earlier in this part: "וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל דָּוִיד֩ וְשָׂרֵ֨י הַצָּבָ֜א לַעֲבֹדָ֗ה" (David and the captains of the army set apart for the service), naming "captains of the army" for the first time in this part and reusing the "set apart" verb already quoted above rather than the division/lot vocabulary that governed the priests and Levites. The roster closes its own tally with "וַיְהִ֤י מִסְפָּרָם֙" (and their number, with their brothers... was) followed by "כָּל הַ֨מֵּבִ֔ין מָאתַ֖יִם שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים וּשְׁמוֹנָֽה" (all who were skillful, two hundred eighty-eight), echoing the identical opening words of v1's own tally clause, "וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם" (and their number was) -- the same two words bracket the whole singer-family roster front to back. Verse 8's fresh lot-casting formula then opens a differently shaped sub-unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with 24:20-31 is tempting since both end in enumeration language, but the new cast of characters (army captains, three named singer-fathers) and the new verb mark 25:1 as a scene-opening, not a continuation of the Levite lot lists.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the explicit lot-casting formula "וַיַּפִּ֜ילוּ גּוֹרָל֣וֹת מִשְׁמֶ֗רֶת לְעֻמַּת֙ כַּקָּטֹ֣ן כַּגָּד֔וֹל מֵבִ֖ין עִם תַּלְמִֽיד" (they cast lots for their offices, the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the student), then runs a uniform refrain -- an ordinal, a name, his sons and his brothers, twelve -- through items three to twenty-four (25:10-31); v.9 is the list's own opening pair, not the refrain's first instance: its first item, לְאָסָ֖ף לְיוֹסֵ֑ף ('for Asaph: Joseph'), lacks a tally element entirely, and its second, גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֽוּא וְאֶחָ֥יו וּבָנָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר ('Gedaliah the second, he and his brothers and his sons, twelve'), inverts both orders the refrain proper uses from v.10 on -- name before ordinal, and brothers before sons -- against v.10's הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֣י זַכּ֔וּר בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר ('the third, Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve'), ordinal before name and sons before brothers. No verse from 10 through 31 introduces a new subject, verb, or closing tag -- v9 alone carries the finite verb וַיֵּצֵ֞א that opens the refrain -- and the list ends only because the count of twenty-four is exhausted, which is why the brief's instruction to keep this one formulaic unit through the end of the part is textually warranted, not merely a convenience. A pe follows v.8 itself (oshb:1Chr.25.8, pe, single-witness), weak tier-3 corroboration for detaching v.8 from the list that follows -- a reading this row does not take, since v.8's lot-casting formula grammatically governs the entire following enumeration and so outranks the single-witness mark. A further pe follows this row's own closing verse, v.31 (oshb:1Chr.25.31, pe, single-witness), corroborating the close without driving it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The refrain's ordinal morphology does shift at the list's midpoint -- bare or article-only ordinals run from v10 through v19, "הַשְּׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לַחֲשַׁבְיָ֔ה בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר" (the twelfth, Hashabiah), then a prefixed lamed governs every ordinal from v20, "לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ שֽׁוּבָאֵ֔ל בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר" (for the thirteenth, Shubael), through v31, "לְאַרְבָּעָ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ לְרוֹמַ֣מְתִּי עָ֔זֶר בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר" (for the twenty-fourth, Romamti-Ezer) -- but the shift introduces no new head, subject, or closing tag, only a preposition, so it does not by itself carry a tier-1 seam; no other textual marker separates any subgroup from the next, and the semantic shape of the refrain itself never varies.

boundary_rationale: A dedicated topic head opens the row and marks it off from ch 25's singer lots: "לְמַחְלְק֖וֹת לְשֹׁעֲרִ֑ים לַקָּרְחִ֕ים מְשֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֥הוּ בֶן קֹרֵ֖א מִן בְּנֵ֥י אָסָֽף" (for the divisions of the doorkeepers... of the sons of Asaph). The same lamed-PN plus בָּנִ֑ים ('had sons') head recurs five times, not three, carrying the office forward without opening a fresh register: "וְלִמְשֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֖הוּ בָּנִ֑ים זְכַרְיָ֤הוּ הַבְּכוֹר֙ יְדִֽיעֲאֵ֣ל הַשֵּׁנִ֔י זְבַדְיָ֨הוּ֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י יַתְנִיאֵ֖ל הָרְבִיעִֽי" 'Meshelemiah had sons' (v2), "וּלְעֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֖ם בָּנִ֑ים שְׁמַֽעְיָ֤ה הַבְּכוֹר֙ יְהוֹזָבָ֣ד הַשֵּׁנִ֔י יוֹאָ֤ח הַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ וְשָׂכָ֣ר הָרְבִיעִ֔י וּנְתַנְאֵ֖ל הַחֲמִישִֽׁי" 'Obed-Edom had sons' (v4), "וְלִֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֤ה בְנוֹ֙ נוֹלַ֣ד בָּנִ֔ים הַמִּמְשָׁלִ֖ים לְבֵ֣ית אֲבִיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי גִבּ֥וֹרֵי חַ֖יִל הֵֽמָּה" 'sons were also born to Shemaiah his son' (v6), "וְלִמְשֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗הוּ בָּנִ֧ים וְאַחִ֛ים בְּנֵי חָ֖יִל שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר" 'Meshelemiah had sons and brothers' again (v9, consonants identical to v2's head), and "וּלְחֹסָ֥ה מִן בְּנֵי מְרָרִ֖י בָּנִ֑ים שִׁמְרִ֤י הָרֹאשׁ֙ כִּ֣י לֹא הָיָ֣ה בְכ֔וֹר וַיְשִׂימֵ֥הוּ אָבִ֖יהוּ לְרֹֽאשׁ" 'Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons' (v10; gloss -- WEB's own v10 reads 'Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him chief),'). A sixth register head, "בְּנֵ֣י שְׁמַֽעְיָ֗ה עָ֠תְנִי וּרְפָאֵ֨ל וְעוֹבֵ֧ד אֶלְזָבָ֛ד אֶחָ֖יו בְּנֵי חָ֑יִל אֱלִיה֖וּ וּסְמַכְיָֽהוּ" ('the sons of Shemaiah'), opens a third generation under the same line at v7. Two marks corroborate without driving: a pe closes Obed-Edom's own eight-son tally at v5 (oshb:1Chr.26.5, single-witness) -- Meshelemiah's own list, vv.2-3, runs seven sons and carries no mark at its close -- and the samekh at v9 (oshb:1Chr.26.9, single-witness) closes v9's restated Meshelemiah tally itself, not an Obed-Edom-to-Hosah transition -- v9 is a reprise of v2's own head, not a new turn, so the mark punctuates that reprise's own close, standing as the sole mark on a genuine Meshelemiah tally. v8's sub-clan tally, "כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה מִבְּנֵ֣י עֹבֵ֣ד אֱדֹ֗ם הֵ֤מָּה וּבְנֵיהֶם֙ וַאֲחֵיהֶ֔ם אִֽישׁ חַ֥יִל בַּכֹּ֖חַ לַעֲבֹדָ֑ה שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנַ֖יִם לְעֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹֽם" ('all these, of the sons of Obed-Edom... sixty-two'), and v11's matching Hosah tally, "חִלְקִיָּ֤הוּ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ טְבַלְיָ֣הוּ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֔י זְכַרְיָ֖הוּ הָרְבִעִ֑י כָּל בָּנִ֧ים וְאַחִ֛ים לְחֹסָ֖ה שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה עָשָֽׂר" ('all the sons and brothers of Hosah, thirteen'), are each a sub-clan total nested inside this one register, not the register's own close -- the 'elleh machlequot' formula that actually terminates the whole doorkeeper complex does not appear until v19 (D130, see M8-1Chr-130), so v8's tally is internal bookkeeping for the Obed-Edom line rather than a rival unit boundary. Read together, the five parallel sub-heads plus the Shemaiah register head still read as one doorkeeper-clan register, closing with Hosah's own tally at v11 already quoted above. The row ends before v12, where the vocabulary pivots from ancestry to office: "לְ֠אֵלֶּה מַחְלְק֨וֹת הַשֹּֽׁעֲרִ֜ים לְרָאשֵׁ֧י הַגְּבָרִ֛ים מִשְׁמָר֖וֹת לְעֻמַּ֣ת אֲחֵיהֶ֑ם לְשָׁרֵ֖ת בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה" ('of these were the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men') opens a lot-and-duty unit that has no counterpart in vv1-11.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at each lamed-PN sub-head (Meshelemiah v2, Obed-Edom v4, Shemaiah's sons v6-7, Meshelemiah's own reprise v9, Hosah v10) into five rows is not defeated by an absence of marks: two of the five are in fact closed by single-witness marks -- a pe after v.5 (closing the Obed-Edom block opened at v.4) and a samekh after v.9 (closing v.9's own restated Meshelemiah tally) -- conceded here rather than denied. The merge nonetheless holds because neither mark, nor any of the other three sub-heads, introduces a topic change or a register-level closure formula of its own; per book_strategy_draft.md §3, the chs 23-27 marks are weak corroboration tracking list-item granularity finer than this row, not register-level dividers, so only the register-level v.1 head and the v.11 tally bracket the whole complex.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens where D129 ends: "לְ֠אֵלֶּה מַחְלְק֨וֹת הַשֹּֽׁעֲרִ֜ים לְרָאשֵׁ֧י הַגְּבָרִ֛ים מִשְׁמָר֖וֹת לְעֻמַּ֣ת אֲחֵיהֶ֑ם לְשָׁרֵ֖ת בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה" ('of these were the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men') reframes the same families as office-holders and immediately moves to action rather than ancestry: "וַיַּפִּ֨ילוּ גוֹרָל֜וֹת כַּקָּטֹ֧ן כַּגָּד֛וֹל לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָ֖ם לְשַׁ֥עַר וָשָֽׁעַר" ('they cast lots'), a device matrix lot-casting formula. Two marks sit inside this span, undisclosed in the row's earlier citation: a pe closes v13's casting clause (oshb:1Chr.26.13, single-witness) and a samekh follows v14's outcome (oshb:1Chr.26.14, single-witness); both fall at an internal join and would, read alone, weakly favor a division there. But the wayyiqtol continuation from v13's casting to v14's outcome, "וַיִּפֹּ֧ל הַגּוֹרָ֛ל מִזְרָ֖חָה לְשֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֑הוּ וּזְכַרְיָ֨הוּ בְנ֜וֹ יוֹעֵ֣ץ בְּשֶׂ֗כֶל הִפִּ֨ילוּ֙ גּֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וַיֵּצֵ֥א גוֹרָל֖וֹ צָפֽוֹנָה" ('the lot fell eastward, to Shelemiah'), overrides them: the chain runs unbroken from v.13 to v.14, so no tier-1 seam arises there despite the two single-witness marks. The lot outcomes (east/north/south/west, vv14-16) and the resulting duty numbers (vv17-18) belong to that single casting, so the sequence is not re-split at the switch from named outcomes to headcounts. It closes with a summary formula that echoes v1's opening noun pair: "אֵ֗לֶּה מַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַשֹּׁ֣עֲרִ֔ים לִבְנֵ֥י הַקָּרְחִ֖י וְלִבְנֵ֥י מְרָרִֽי" ('these were the divisions of the doorkeepers'), compare "לְמַחְלְק֖וֹת לְשֹׁעֲרִ֑ים לַקָּרְחִ֕ים מְשֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֥הוּ בֶן קֹרֵ֖א מִן בְּנֵ֥י אָסָֽף". That inclusio closes the whole gatekeeper complex before v20 opens an unrelated topic: "וְֽהַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֲחִיָּ֗ה עַל אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּלְאֹֽצְר֖וֹת הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים" ('of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God's house') -- matching WEB's own opening clause, 'Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house', not the possessive-inverted rendering earlier attributed to it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the numeric duty roster (vv17-18) as its own row apart from the named lot outcomes (vv14-16) loses because vv.15-18 are verbless prepositional-phrase clauses governed by the single casting narrated in vv.13-14, with no head formula intervening anywhere in the stretch.

boundary_rationale: v20 supplies a fresh governing head, "וְֽהַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֲחִיָּ֗ה עַל אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּלְאֹֽצְר֖וֹת הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים", distinct in subject matter from the gate duties just closed. Two officer lines are cited under that one head rather than in separate registers: the Gershonite line, "בְּנֵ֣י לַ֠עְדָּן בְּנֵ֨י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֜י לְלַעְדָּ֗ן רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֛וֹת לְלַעְדָּ֥ן הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י יְחִיאֵלִֽי" ('the sons of Ladan'), and the Amramite/Mosaic line via Shebuel, "וּשְׁבֻאֵל֙ בֶּן גֵּרְשׁ֣וֹם בֶּן מֹשֶׁ֔ה נָגִ֖יד עַל הָאֹצָרֽוֹת" ('and Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries'). v23's bare four-clan list, "לַֽעַמְרָמִי֙ לַיִּצְהָרִ֔י לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֖י לָֽעָזִּיאֵלִֽי", has no register-head formula of its own, so it reads as a hinge into the Shebuel notice rather than a new unit start -- though two of its four lamed-gentilics recur verse-initially only later, at 26:29 and 26:30-31, inside the following row D132, so v23 opens a four-clan programme this row completes for only one of its four members (Amram); that split is a question for the boss round to weigh, not one resolved here by moving this row's frozen span. v25's continuation clause naming Eliezer's branch stays syntactically dependent on v24, closing on a ketiv/qere pair for the branch's youngest name -- ketiv ושלמות, qere וּשְׁלֹמִ֥ית -- embedded in the verse's own full wording, וְאֶחָ֖יו לֶֽאֱלִיעֶ֑זֶר רְחַבְיָ֨הוּ בְנ֜וֹ וִֽישַׁעְיָ֤הוּ בְנוֹ֙ וְיֹרָ֣ם בְּנ֔וֹ וְזִכְרִ֥י בְנ֖וֹ ושלמות וּשְׁלֹמִ֥ית בְּנֽוֹ (oshb:1Chr.26.25), disclosed here because the row's own closure argument depends on this name. The administrator so named recurs at v26, "ה֧וּא שְׁלֹמ֣וֹת וְאֶחָ֗יו עַ֣ל כָּל אֹצְר֤וֹת הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִקְדִּ֜ישׁ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְרָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֛וֹת לְשָׂרֵֽי הָאֲלָפִ֥ים וְהַמֵּא֖וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֥י הַצָּבָֽא" ('this Shelomoth and his brothers'), and again at v28, "וְכֹ֨ל הַֽהִקְדִּ֜ישׁ שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל הָרֹאֶה֙ וְשָׁא֣וּל בֶּן קִ֔ישׁ וְאַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן נֵ֔ר וְיוֹאָ֖ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֑ה כֹּ֚ל הַמַּקְדִּ֔ישׁ עַ֥ל יַד שְׁלֹמִ֖ית וְאֶחָֽיו" ('all that Samuel the seer... had dedicated... under the hand of Shelomoth and his brothers') -- but the three occurrences are not one repeated fixed form: שְׁלֹמ֣וֹת (v26) and שְׁלֹמִ֖ית (v28) are consonantally distinct spellings of the same referent, and WEB's uniform 'Shelomoth' at both verses is what makes the pair read as a lexical inclusio. What does repeat exactly is the surrounding וְאֶחָ֗יו / וְאֶחָֽיו ('and his brothers') pairing at both v26 and v28, plus the shared root of dedication (הִקְדִּ֜ישׁ / הַֽהִקְדִּ֜ישׁ / הִקְדִּ֑ישׁוּ) running v26-28 -- a referential and lexical-root continuity across the same administrator's custody, not a repeated-phrase inclusio. The dedication note, v27, "מִן הַמִּלְחָמ֥וֹת וּמִן הַשָּׁלָ֖ל הִקְדִּ֑ישׁוּ לְחַזֵּ֖ק לְבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה", WEB renders 'They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair Yahweh’s house.' (this is WEB's own wording, confirmed against 1Chr_web_clean.txt; the row's earlier citation had reversed that clause order), leads into v28's final clause naming that same custody again under the שְׁלֹמִ֖ית spelling. oshb:1Chr.26.28 carries a pe at its close (single-witness), weak corroboration sitting exactly where the treasury topic gives way, at v29, to outward administration: "לַיִּצְהָרִ֞י כְּנַנְיָ֣הוּ וּבָנָ֗יו לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה הַחִֽיצוֹנָה֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים וּלְשֹׁפְטִֽים" ('of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Gershonite treasury notice (vv21-22) from the Amramite/Shebuel-Shelomoth notice (vv23-28) into two rows loses because v23's clan list carries no independent head formula and functions only as a hinge inside v20's single governing topic.

boundary_rationale: "לַיִּצְהָרִ֞י כְּנַנְיָ֣הוּ וּבָנָ֗יו לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה הַחִֽיצוֹנָה֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים וּלְשֹׁפְטִֽים" ('of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business') opens on the same Izharite gentilic already listed at 26:23 (inside the preceding row D131), so the verse resumes a four-clan programme already under way rather than opening an unheralded topic; scanning oshb:1Chr.26.29 word by word turns up neither the divine name nor the royal noun, so the verse itself does not fall inside the Yahweh/king envelope that brackets what follows -- the tie it carries forward includes more than the shared root לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה ('for the... business'), answered by מְלֶ֣אכֶת ('the business of...') in v30: both v.29 and v.30 open on the same lamed-plus-gentilic register-head type (לַיִּצְהָרִ֞י / לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י), and both share the על...ישראל jurisdiction-over-Israel formula (עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל in v.29; עַ֚ל פְּקֻדַּ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל in v.30) -- an inventory that strengthens, rather than weakens, the case for holding v.29 with what follows. This row falls under the single governing head opened at 26:20, וְֽהַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֲחִיָּ֗ה עַל אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים (WEB 'Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God's house...'), which continues unbroken through this row's own span with no register-head formula of a different shape intervening at v.29. A pe follows 26:28 itself (oshb:1Chr.26.28, single-witness), weak corroboration standing exactly at this row's own opening edge -- inside the stretch this row claims one head (26:20) governs unbroken -- disclosed here rather than passed over.
