That Yahweh/king envelope proper does bracket vv30-32: v30 reads "לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ֩ וְאֶחָ֨יו בְּנֵי חַ֜יִל אֶ֣לֶף וּשְׁבַע מֵא֗וֹת עַ֚ל פְּקֻדַּ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן מַעְרָ֑בָה לְכֹל֙ מְלֶ֣אכֶת יְהוָ֔ה וְלַעֲבֹדַ֖ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ", WEB 'Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Yahweh and for the service of the king.', and v32 closes on the matching pair from "וְאֶחָ֣יו בְּנֵי חַ֗יִל אַלְפַּ֛יִם וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֑וֹת וַיַּפְקִידֵ֞ם דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עַל הָראוּבֵנִ֤י וְהַגָּדִי֙ וַחֲצִי֙ שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשִּׁ֔י לְכָל דְּבַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וּדְבַ֥ר הַמֶּֽלֶךְ", which WEB renders 'His relatives, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom King David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.' (checked word-for-word against 1Chr_web_clean.txt). v30 and v31 both open on the same repeated head, לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י / לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִי֙ ('of the Hebronites'), a possible internal seam that does not in fact carry one: v31 supplies the search notice, "לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִי֙ יְרִיָּ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֥י לְתֹלְדֹתָ֖יו לְאָב֑וֹת בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הָֽאַרְבָּעִ֜ים לְמַלְכ֤וּת דָּוִיד֙ נִדְרָ֔שׁוּ וַיִּמָּצֵ֥א בָהֶ֛ם גִּבּ֥וֹרֵי חַ֖יִל בְּיַעְזֵ֥יר גִּלְעָֽד", that grounds only v32's total of 2,700 (Jerijah's kin, dated to David's fortieth year at Jazer of Gilead), not v30's separate 1,700 (Hashabiah's men, a notice carrying no search language of its own) -- so the repeated לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י head marks two members of one census report rather than two independent units, and the row does not split there. The chapter division itself gets a weak second: v32 ends with a pe (oshb:1Chr.26.32, single-witness), sitting exactly at the seam into 1Chr 27's census-and-course material: "וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the children of Israel after their number').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating Chenaniah's Izharite oversight (v29) from the Hebronite oversight (vv30-32) into two rows is the genuinely live rival: v29 carries neither the divine name nor the royal noun that brackets vv30-32, and its own strongest tie forward is the shared מלאכה/מלאכת root plus its resumption of 26:23's four-clan list (D131) rather than a shared Yahweh/king envelope. The row holds v29 with vv30-32 anyway because both fall under 26:20's single governing head with no register-head formula of a different shape intervening at v29, not because one envelope phrase encloses all four verses alike.

boundary_rationale: "וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the children of Israel after their number') opens a census-and-course register unrelated to the treasuries and business notices just closed, and immediately sets the refrain quantity, הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף -- gloss: 'the one division: twenty-four thousand' -- הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ is the cardinal 'one' agreeing with the definite noun, not an ordinal; 'first' is reserved for the true ordinal, הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙, which the row itself quotes two sentences later at v.2 (oshb:1Chr.27.1; WEB smooths the clause into the general statement 'of every division were twenty-four thousand.', so the English here is the author's own literal rendering of the Hebrew, not a WEB quotation), which recurs almost verbatim after every captain through v15, e.g. "עַ֞ל הַמַּחֲלֹ֤קֶת הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן יָֽשָׁבְעָ֖ם בֶּן זַבְדִּיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַֽחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('and over his division were twenty-four thousand'). A samekh follows nearly every one of these month-entries (oshb:1Chr.27.1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 samekh, single-witness) -- exactly the list-item density the marker policy warns against letting pull row granularity down, since the whole cycle is one formulaic course rotation. v6 briefly breaks the refrain's closing formula to note Benaiah's command of the Thirty, "ה֧וּא בְנָיָ֛הוּ גִּבּ֥וֹר הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֖ים וְעַל הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֑ים וּמַ֣חֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עַמִּיזָבָ֖ד בְּנֽוֹ" ('he was Benaiah, the mighty man of the thirty, and over the thirty; and his division was Ammizabad his son'); that aside stays inside the row because the very next verse resumes the same captain-and-number pattern without any new head. The sequence closes at the twelfth month, "הַשְּׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לִשְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חֶלְדַּ֥י הַנְּטוֹפָתִ֖י לְעָתְנִיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the twelfth, of the twelfth month'), after which a pe mark follows (oshb:1Chr.27.15 pe, single-witness), corroborating the shift at v16 to a differently-headed list: "וְעַל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֣י נָגִ֔יד אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן זִכְרִ֑י לַשִּׁ֨מְעוֹנִ֔י שְׁפַטְיָ֖הוּ בֶּֽן מַעֲכָֽה" ('now over the tribes of Israel').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving each of the twelve captains its own row loses because the pervasive samekh chain marks list-item punctuation inside one formulaic 12-fold refrain, the exact case the campaign's granularity guidance names as a single decision.

boundary_rationale: oshb:1Chr.27.15's closing pe (single-witness) sits right where the topic changes: "וְעַל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֣י נָגִ֔יד אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן זִכְרִ֑י לַשִּׁ֨מְעוֹנִ֔י שְׁפַטְיָ֖הוּ בֶּֽן מַעֲכָֽה" 'Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri was the ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;' (web:1Chr.27.16/oshb:1Chr.27.16) opens a differently-formed list, one officer per tribe rather than one captain per month. Internally the list carries its own fine punctuation -- double samekh follows both v16 and v21 (oshb:1Chr.27.16 samekh+samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.21 samekh+samekh; both single-witness; two of the book's ten double-samekh verses per the campaign's verified marker profile) -- but that granularity sits below the row, inside the tribe-by-tribe listing. The roll closes with its own formula, "לְדָ֕ן עֲזַרְאֵ֖ל בֶּן יְרֹחָ֑ם אֵ֕לֶּה שָׂרֵ֖י שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('these were the captains of the tribes of Israel'), yet what follows is not a fresh register head but a continuing negative clause, "וְלֹא נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם לְמִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָ֑טָּה כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לְהַרְבּ֥וֹת אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם" ('and David didn't take their number'), which reaches back lexically to v1's opening, "וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָֽאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חָדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף" ('the children of Israel after their number'), on the same root. Because vv23-24 open no independent unit -- v24's continuation, "יוֹאָ֨ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֜ה הֵחֵ֤ל לִמְנוֹת֙ וְלֹ֣א כִלָּ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י בָזֹ֛את קֶ֖צֶף עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א עָלָה֙ הַמִּסְפָּ֔ר בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר דִּבְרֵֽי הַיָּמִ֖ים לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד" ('Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number'), simply extends the same aside -- the census note stays inside this row per the inset rule rather than forcing a fresh row at v23. The row ends before v25's differently-headed steward list, "וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן עֲדִיאֵ֑ל וְעַ֣ל הָֽאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ" ('and over the king's treasures'). A samekh follows this row's own terminal verse, 27:24, itself (oshb:1Chr.27.24, samekh, single-witness), tier-3 corroboration of the closing edge (the 27:24/27:25 seam), without driving the call.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carving vv23-24 into their own row loses on close reading because the clause opens with a waw-disjunctive background clause (וְלֹא נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙, waw + negative particle + qatal -- the disjunctive, interrupting pattern, not a continuing wayyiqtol), which is what makes vv.23-24 a comment on the preceding registers rather than a new register head; its 'number' vocabulary answers v1's opening rather than starting anything new; folding it back into 27:1-15 instead is a live but weaker alternative, since the tribal-officer roll (16-22) intervenes between the two 'number' notices.

boundary_rationale: "וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן עֲדִיאֵ֑ל וְעַ֣ל הָֽאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ" ('and over the king's treasures') begins a run of parallel we'al-headed ('and over...') appointment notices -- fields, tillage, vineyards, olive and sycamore trees, herds, camels, donkeys, flocks -- with no intervening register-head formula of a different shape anywhere in the run. Fine list-item marks punctuate individual entries (oshb:1Chr.27.25 samekh+samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.27 samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.28 samekh+samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.29 samekh; oshb:1Chr.27.30 samekh; all single-witness, with vv25 and 28 counted among the book's ten double-samekh verses in the campaign's verified marker profile), but none of them coincides with a topic change, so they corroborate list density rather than a row seam. A witness-specific caution applies at 27:30/31: WEB 27:30 runs three clauses through 'Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite. Over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite. Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite.' (1Chr_web.usfm), while MT 27:30 stops at יֶחְדְּיָ֖הוּ הַמֵּרֹנֹתִֽי ('Jehdeiah the Meronothite') and MT 27:31 opens with the flocks clause itself, "וְעַל הַצֹּ֖אן יָזִ֣יז הַֽהַגְרִ֑י" ('and over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite'), immediately followed by the run's own closing formula. Both witnesses count 34 verses in this chapter, so this is a clause-level content divergence under matching verse numbers, not a numbering-scheme difference; the samekh keyed to oshb:1Chr.27.30 (single-witness) therefore falls inside WEB's v30 rather than at a WEB verse boundary, and citing web:1Chr.27.30 alongside oshb:1Chr.27.30 as co-extensive material is not accurate at the clause level. This row's own span is unaffected, since v32 begins at the same content point in both witnesses (WEB 'Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.' = MT "וִֽיהוֹנָתָ֤ן דּוֹד דָּוִיד֙ יוֹעֵ֔ץ אִישׁ מֵבִ֥ין וְסוֹפֵ֖ר ה֑וּא וִֽיחִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן חַכְמוֹנִ֖י עִם בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ"). The run closes with its own summary, "וְעַל הַצֹּ֖אן יָזִ֣יז הַֽהַגְרִ֑י כָּל אֵ֨לֶּה֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרְכ֔וּשׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד" ('all these were the rulers of the property'), a formula built the same way as the tribal roll's close just before it ("לְדָ֕ן עֲזַרְאֵ֖ל בֶּן יְרֹחָ֑ם אֵ֕לֶּה שָׂרֵ֖י שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל", 'these were the captains of the tribes of Israel'). v32 then drops the we'al pattern entirely for a named-person-plus-apposition notice, WEB 'Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.' (web:1Chr.27.32/oshb:1Chr.27.32, checked against 1Chr_web_clean.txt), marking the row's close by a genuine syntactic shift rather than by a mark.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the field/orchard stewards (vv25-28) from the herd/flock stewards (vv29-31) loses because both halves use the identical we'al-plus-name format with no head-formula change between them, and both fall under the single closing formula of v31.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:1Chr.27.30 (WEB clause content diverges from MT at 27.30/31 -- see rationale)
oshb:1Chr.27.30 (samekh, single-witness; falls inside WEB v30, not at a WEB verse end)

boundary_rationale: Against the we'al-headed steward list just closed (e.g. "וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן עֲדִיאֵ֑ל וְעַ֣ל הָֽאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ"), v32 shifts to naming the person first and appending his role: WEB 'Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.' (web:1Chr.27.32/oshb:1Chr.27.32). The same shape continues through v33, "וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל יוֹעֵ֣ץ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְחוּשַׁ֥י הָאַרְכִּ֖י רֵ֥עַ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ" ('Ahithophel was the king's counselor. Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.'), with a samekh after it (oshb:1Chr.27.33 samekh, single-witness) marking that internal item boundary, and closes with a succession note followed by a second clause naming the army's commander that in the MT is role-phrase-first, with the name in final position: וְשַׂר צָבָ֥א לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יוֹאָֽב ('and commander of the army for the king, יוֹאָֽב'), the reverse of the name-first pattern that opens vv.32-33 (וִֽיהוֹנָתָ֤ן..., וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל..., וְחוּשַׁ֥י...); WEB's own rendering inverts this to a subject-first English clause, 'Joab was the captain of the king’s army.' (web:1Chr.27.34/oshb:1Chr.27.34, WEB's own wording per 1Chr_web_clean.txt -- the row's prior citation had further inverted WEB's own order and inserted an unwarranted leading 'and'). Unlike the two preceding rows, this short counselor notice has no 'these are' summary of its own; its unity rests on the shared named-person-plus-role pattern across all three verses rather than on a closing formula, which is why the row is held at a lower confidence than the we'al-headed lists around it. oshb:1Chr.27.34 does close on a pe (single-witness), a weak second placed exactly at the part's own terminal edge, where 1Chr 28 opens an assembly scene outside this range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv32-34 into the preceding stewards row (25-31) as one combined unit loses because v32 replaces the we'al-headed appointment pattern with a named-person-plus-apposition pattern, a syntactic break that is sufficient on its own; the closing pe after v34 (oshb:1Chr.27.34, single-witness) would fall at the same location whether this is read as a standalone 32-34 row or as part of a combined 25-34 row, so it cannot discriminate between the two options and is not treated here as evidence for either.

boundary_rationale: The part begins with a hiphil summons, "וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל דָּוִ֣יד אֶת כָּל שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שָׂרֵ֣י הַשְּׁבָטִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמַּחְלְק֣וֹת הַמְשָׁרְתִ֪ים אֶת הַמֶּ֟לֶךְ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י כָל רְכוּשׁ וּמִקְנֶה֩ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וּלְבָנָ֜יו עִם הַסָּרִיסִ֧ים וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וּֽלְכָל גִּבּ֥וֹר חָ֖יִל אֶל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם", that governs a single enumerated catalogue of officeholder classes -- tribal princes, rotation-captains who served the king, captains of thousands and hundreds, stewards of royal property and livestock, officers, and mighty men -- terminating in the phrase WEB renders 'David assembled all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, the captains of the companies who served the king by division, the captains of thousands, the captains of hundreds, and the rulers over all the substance and possessions of the king and of his sons, with the officers and the mighty men, even all the mighty men of valor, to Jerusalem.' Verse 2 opens with a consecutive wayyiqtol, "וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל רַגְלָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר" ('the king stood up on his feet and said'), which formally continues rather than breaks the narrative chain v1's own וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל opens -- Hebrew wayyiqtol chains run through unit boundaries rather than sealing them, so the seam here is discourse-level, not syntactic closure. It is real on its own narrower ground: v1's roster opens no quotation frame of any kind, and the imperative that follows, "שְׁמָע֖וּנִי אַחַ֣י וְעַמִּ֑י" ('hear me, my brothers and my people'), is a bare vocative that names no group by itself -- its referent is recoverable only from the enumerated officer-classes v1 just gathered. A closed participant-list handing straight into a newly inaugurated speech is the seam: v1 anticipates no quotation, and v2 supplies both the first inquit and the audience v1's own roster set up.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v1 into the address that follows (making 28:1-7 or longer one row) is the genuinely live rival the corrected grounds must still answer: no syntactic break forces the split, since v2's wayyiqtol continues v1's own chain. The split holds because v1 opens no quotation frame and v2 supplies both the first inquit and the addressee v1's roster sets up -- a register-to-speech-inauguration transition, not a chain break.

boundary_rationale: David's speech, inaugurated in the preceding verse, runs continuously through this span: his own account of wanting to build 'a house of rest for the ark of Yahweh's covenant' and God's refusal, "וְהָאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔י לֹא תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י כִּ֣י אִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמ֛וֹת אַ֖תָּה וְדָמִ֥ים שָׁפָֽכְתָּ" ('But God said to me, ‘You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.’', 28:3), then the election chain opened by the wayyiqtol וַיִּבְחַ֡ר ('and he chose') -- Yahweh chose David out of his father's house (28:4), then chose Solomon among many sons for the throne, וַיִּבְחַר֙ בִּשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֔י (28:5, 'and he chose Solomon my son') -- culminating in a quoted divine promise about Solomon's kingdom (28:6-7). That quoted promise closes on its own temporal tag, כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה / 'as it is today,' ending the embedded divine word David is reciting. The next verse pivots on the adverb וְ֠עַתָּה ('now therefore') at 28:8, a single pivot marking the move from rehearsed background into imperative charge -- רְאֵ֣ה עַתָּ֗ה at 28:10 is a related but distinct hinge, and the later וְ֠עַתָּה instances at 29:13 and 29:17 belong to the prayer, a separate speech-act, where they open thanksgiving rather than imperative charge -- so the true seam falls between v7 and v8 on the strength of the pivot itself, without any claim to frequency.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking before v4, where the wayyiqtol election-chain begins, would separate David's personal account from the election chain it grounds, but no inquit reopens there -- it stays one uninterrupted first-person address. Two embedded inquits inside this same span do report speech but do not seam it either: "וְהָאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔י " ('God said to me', v3) and "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י" ('he said to me', v6) are first-person recollections nested inside David's own recital -- 'X said TO ME' -- not narrator-level frames that redirect the addressee the way the framing inquits at 28:20, 29:1, and 29:10 do; an inset that stays syntactically resumed within its host speech stays inside the row it is embedded in, so neither supplies a stronger seam than the וְ֠עַתָּה pivot at v8.

boundary_rationale: The pivot וְ֠עַתָּה just discussed opens a self-contained charge addressed with second-person plural imperatives, שִׁמְר֣וּ וְדִרְשׁ֔וּ ('observe and seek out'). The addressee is not named by the witness-phrase that follows: "וְ֠עַתָּה לְעֵינֵ֨י כָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל קְהַל יְהוָה֙ וּבְאָזְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ" ('in the sight of all Israel, Yahweh's assembly, and in the audience of our God') stands as two parallel adverbial witness-phrases governed by לְעֵינֵ֨י/וּבְאָזְנֵ֣י, not as a vocative -- since God plainly cannot be the addressee of the imperatives that follow, neither parallel member is; the 2mp addressee itself is unnamed here and recoverable only from 28:1's own participant list. The verse closes on its own inheritance formula, עַד עוֹלָֽם ('forever'). The very next verse reopens with a new vocative and a grammatically singular addressee, "וְאַתָּ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה בְנִ֡י" ('but you, Solomon, my son'), paired with singular imperatives (דַּע֩ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֨י אָבִ֜יךָ וְעָבְדֵ֗הוּ, 2ms) -- a plural-to-singular addressee shift that is grammatical, not merely rhetorical, and v9's casus-pendens vocative has no counterpart at all in v8. This particular seam also carries a WLC petuchah at 28:8 (single-witness), which happens to land exactly at the addressee change described above -- offered strictly as corroboration, never as what drives the call.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 28:8-10 as a single exhortation because both halves share the surrounding 'now therefore...be strong' envelope discounts the fact that the addressee and grammatical number both change at v9, which is the stronger signal.

boundary_rationale: Following the addressee shift argued above, the singular charge דַּע֩ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֨י אָבִ֜יךָ וְעָבְדֵ֗הוּ ('know the God of your father and serve him') runs to its climax in the imperative pair חֲזַ֥ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה ('be strong and do it,' v10), which closes the entire 28:2-10 address. Verse 11 opens a new wayyiqtol with a different subject-verb pattern, וַיִּתֵּ֣ן דָּוִ֣יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֡וֹ אֶת תַּבְנִ֣ית הָאוּלָם֩ ('David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch'), shifting from second-person imperative speech to third-person narration of a handed-over object -- a change in both grammatical person and verb-type marks the seam. Worth noting only in passing: the WLC divides here too, with a petuchah after 28:10 (single-witness) -- a detail that lines up with, but does not establish, the person/verb-type break just argued.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this span through v19 -- one row for the charge plus the whole pattern-transfer -- would erase the person/verb-type break at v11 and swallow the internal pattern-word inclusio that the next row argues on its own terms.

boundary_rationale: The narrative wayyiqtol that closes the prior row, "וַיִּתֵּ֣ן דָּוִ֣יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֡וֹ אֶת תַּבְנִ֣ית הָאוּלָם֩ וְֽאֶת בָּ֨תָּ֜יו וְגַנְזַכָּ֧יו וַעֲלִיֹּתָ֛יו וַחֲדָרָ֥יו הַפְּנִימִ֖ים וּבֵ֥ית הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת" ('David gave...the pattern of the porch'), opens a register in which תַּבְנִ֣ית ('pattern') is the recurring spine: v12 "וְתַבְנִ֗ית כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה בָר֨וּחַ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ לְחַצְר֧וֹת בֵּית יְהוָ֛ה וּלְכָל הַלְּשָׁכ֖וֹת סָבִ֑יב לְאֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּלְאֹצְר֖וֹת הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים" ('the pattern of all he had by the Spirit'), v18 "וּלְמִזְבַּ֧ח הַקְּטֹ֛רֶת זָהָ֥ב מְזֻקָּ֖ק בַּמִּשְׁקָ֑ל וּלְתַבְנִ֣ית הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֗ה הַכְּרֻבִ֤ים זָהָב֙ לְפֹ֣רְשִׂ֔ים וְסֹכְכִ֖ים עַל אֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית יְהוָֽה" ('the pattern of the chariot, the cherubim'), and the closing tally at v19, "הַכֹּ֥ל בִּכְתָ֛ב מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה עָלַ֣י הִשְׂכִּ֑יל כֹּ֖ל מַלְאֲכ֥וֹת הַתַּבְנִֽית" ('all the works of this pattern') -- an inclusio bracketing the intervening itemized list of courts and treasuries (12) and priestly/Levite divisions (13), and the weighed gold and silver vessels marked by the recurring word בַּמִּשְׁקָל֙ ('by weight,' 14-17). WEB's inserted quotation-tag at v19, 'David said,' has no Hebrew inquit-verb behind it -- הַכֹּ֥ל בִּכְתָ֛ב מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה is David's own summary clause, not a new speech-opening -- so it is a translator's continuity marker, not textual evidence of a fresh unit. The enumeration therefore runs unbroken from 11 to 19. A WLC pe closes 1Chr.28.19 (oshb:1Chr.28.19, single-witness), agreeing with but not driving this edge -- disclosed here since every sibling row in this cluster discloses its own adjacent mark as corroboration. Verse 20 is where a genuine new inquit appears, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֗וֹ חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָ֑ת כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֱלֹהַי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֤א יַרְפְּךָ֙ וְלֹ֣א יַֽעַזְבֶ֔ךָּ עַד לִכְל֕וֹת כָּל מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית יְהוָֽה" ('David said to Solomon his son'), and that is the true close of this register-inset.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v14, where the weight-refrain begins, would cut a single prepositional chain that the pattern-word inclusio shows is one list; an itemized register this formulaic should not be sliced at the verse level.

boundary_rationale: The fresh inquit that ends the previous row, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֗וֹ" (David said to Solomon his son), carries the imperative triplet "חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָ֑ת" ('be strong and courageous, and do it; don't be afraid, nor be dismayed'), which echoes -- rather than purpose-builds a bracket around -- 28:10's own briefer חֲזַ֥ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה: an in-book sweep for חזק co-occurring with אמץ across 1 Chronicles returns only two verses, 22:13 and 28:20. 22:13 supplies the same imperative pair and the same negated pair that 28:20 reproduces, "חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָ֔ץ אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָֽת" (oshb:1Chr.22.13, 6 tokens), against 28:20's "חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָ֑ת" (oshb:1Chr.28.20, 7 tokens) -- not word-for-word identical, since the do-imperative וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה is wedged between the two pairs at 28:20 only. 22:16's "ק֣וּם וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה וִיהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ" (oshb:1Chr.22.16) separately supplies the do-imperative-plus-accompaniment pairing that 28:20's own עִמָּ֔ךְ repeats. The charge at 28:20 thus draws on a Chronicles-wide David-to-Solomon charge repertoire spanning ch 22 and ch 28, of which 28:10 is itself an abbreviation, rather than a bracket purpose-built around the intervening 28:11-19 pattern-register; the element 28:20 shares uniquely with 28:10 is only the shared do-imperative. Verse 21 continues the same address -- וְעִמְּךָ֙ ('and with you') -- to list the human support available to Solomon: priestly and Levite divisions ("וְהִנֵּ֗ה מַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְכָל עֲבוֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים"), willing skilled workers, captains, and, closing the verse, "וְהַשָּׂרִ֥ים וְכָל הָעָ֖ם לְכָל דְּבָרֶֽיךָ" ('the captains and all the people at your every word'). Then 29:1 opens an entirely new speech-inauguration formula, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל" ('David the king said to all the assembly'), addressed now to the wider assembly rather than to Solomon, and turning to a new subject, funding the temple -- a clean chapter-crossing seam. The WLC's own paragraphing agrees, for what that is worth: a petuchah (single-witness) follows 28:21, right where the chapter-crossing seam falls -- supporting evidence, not the argument itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 28:20-21 to the preceding pattern-register as one long row would submerge the inclusio-closing echo of 'be strong...do it' inside the list it answers, when the fresh inquit at v20 marks it as its own closing movement.

boundary_rationale: The new inquit that opens this row, "וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל", has David naming Solomon נַ֣עַר וָרָ֑ךְ ('young and tender') for a task too great for a man, then cataloguing his own preparation and private gift of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and precious stones (29:2-4) before posing the appeal itself: "וּמִ֣י מִתְנַדֵּ֔ב לְמַלֹּ֥אות יָד֛וֹ הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהוָֽה" ('who then offers willingly to consecrate himself today to Yahweh,' 29:5b). Verse 6 answers with a matching wayyiqtol, "וַיִּֽתְנַדְּבוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת" ('then the princes of the fathers' households'), and the itemized totals and Jehiel's oversight (29:7-8) resolve into one joy-notice naming both parties, "וַיִּשְׂמְח֤וּ הָעָם֙ עַל הִֽתְנַדְּבָ֔ם כִּ֚י בְּלֵ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם הִֽתְנַדְּב֖וּ לַיהוָ֑ה וְגַם֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׂמַ֖ח שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה" ('the people rejoiced... and David the king also rejoiced with great joy,' 29:9), binding appeal and response into a single episode. Verse 10 opens a different speech-act altogether, David's blessing of Yahweh rather than his appeal to the assembly, "וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל", so that is where this row ends. For completeness, a petuchah (single-witness) is keyed to 29:9 in the WLC, coinciding with the joy-notice that closes this episode; the coincidence corroborates rather than proves the boundary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v6, where the subject shifts from David's appeal to the princes' response ("וַיִּֽתְנַדְּבוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת", a subject-changing wayyiqtol), has genuine grammatical support, but the נדב stem-chain running from v5's appeal verb through v9's double hitpael, plus the shared joy-notice at v9 that names both David and the people together in one clause, binds appeal to response into one cause-and-effect episode on tier-1 grounds alone.

boundary_rationale: David's blessing-inquit, "וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל" ('David blessed Yahweh before all the assembly, and said'), is answered at once by the address formula "בָּר֨וּךְ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙" ('blessed are you, Yahweh') that opens the doxology (29:11-12). A second-person vocative toward Yahweh recurs at every internal pivot of what follows -- v13's "וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ מוֹדִ֥ים אֲנַ֖חְנוּ לָ֑ךְ" ('now therefore, our God, we thank you'), the self-examining movement of 14-17, and the patriarchal invocation of v18, "יְהוָ֗ה אֱ֠לֹהֵי אַבְרָהָ֞ם יִצְחָ֤ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ" -- without any inquit ever reopening the address; the prayer stays one uninterrupted utterance from its blessing-formula to the climactic petition for Solomon, "וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֗י תֵּ֚ן לֵבָ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם" ('and to Solomon my son give a perfect heart,' 29:19), which itself closes by echoing a term first introduced in the preceding row, not by returning to this row's own opening: "וְלִבְנ֖וֹת הַבִּירָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר הֲכִינֽוֹתִי" ('and to build the palace, for which I have made provision') picks up the word הַבִּירָ֔ה ('the palace') from 29:1, inside D143, not from inside this row's own 29:10 opening. Verse 20 turns outward again with a fresh third-person narrative inquit directed at the congregation rather than at God, "וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל", which is where the prayer ends. The WLC likewise breaks after 29:19 with a petuchah (single-witness), matching the point where the prayer's address to Yahweh gives way to David's address to the assembly -- again, corroboration only.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking at v13's now-therefore pivot would isolate the thanksgiving from the doxology it thanks God for, but no new inquit or change of addressee happens there -- the second-person address to Yahweh runs straight through. A second rival, reading 29:1-19 as one combined arc bracketed by the two הבירה occurrences (29:1 and 29:19), is the genuinely live alternative once the misattributed echo above is corrected; it loses to the v10 blessing-inquit because that inquit pairs with a real addressee shift -- from the assembly (29:1's own address) to Yahweh (29:10's בָּר֨וּךְ אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙) -- and book_strategy_draft.md's own device matrix names 'the great blessing 29:10-19' as a standing Chronicles speech-and-prayer-frame device keyed to that same shift; a named, recurring device is the stronger seam-driver here, not a two-point lexical inclusio on a single rare noun.

boundary_rationale:
The fresh third-person inquit at v20, "וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל בָּֽרְכוּ נָ֖א אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם" ('David said to all the assembly, now bless Yahweh your God'), carries its own second-person plural imperative directed at the assembly. The strongest rival to opening a fresh unit here is lexical, not merely pragmatic: a consonantal sweep of the ברך root across ch 29 returns exactly two verses, 29:10 and 29:20, and no others -- 29:10 opens "וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל" ('David blessed Yahweh in the sight of all the assembly') and 29:20 pairs "בָּֽרְכוּ נָ֖א" with "וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֗ל" ('and all the assembly blessed'), so the same three elements -- the ברך root, דָּוִיד֙, and כָֽל הַקָּהָ֗ל -- stand at both ends of 29:10-20 and nowhere else in the chapter, which could as easily be read as a closing inclusio for the prayer as an opening re-head for this row. It functions as the latter: v20 supplies David's own second address inaugurating a new congregational act (an imperative followed by the assembly's own enactment, "וַיִּקְּד֧וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ לַיהוָ֖ה וְלַמֶּֽלֶךְ", 'and they bowed down and worshiped Yahweh and the king'), where v10 supplied only David's own solitary act of blessing before the assembly as onlookers; the addressee and grammatical shape change even though the root repeats, so the repetition re-heads rather than closes.

The row continues through the next-day sacrifice at v21, "וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה זְ֠בָחִים וַיַּעֲל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת לַיהוָ֗ה לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ פָּרִ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף אֵילִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף כְּבָשִׂ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֑ם וּזְבָחִ֥ים לָרֹ֖ב לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('they sacrificed sacrifices to Yahweh and offered burnt offerings to Yahweh on the next day after that day... for all Israel'), which the book strategy's own §7 item 15 flags as a live interior question ('29:21-25 enthronement notice: close of assembly vs its own unit'), naming the day-shift clause לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ this row's rationale must argue rather than merely narrate. Argued here: the wayyiqtol subject at v21 (וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ, 3mp) continues the same collective-plural subject the assembly held at v20 (וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ...וַיִּקְּד֧וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ), with no new addressee or inquit intervening -- the day-shift moves the scene forward in time but not to a new speaker or audience, so v21 stays inside one unbroken liturgical occasion rather than opening a fresh unit, on this first leg alone. A second leg does not help this argument and is dropped: v.21 has already displaced the scene to לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ ('the morrow of that day'), so v.22's own demonstrative, בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא ('on that day'), most naturally denotes that newly introduced morrow rather than reaching back to v.20's original day; the join is carried unaided by v.21's continuing subject, without help from an 'explicit anchor' claim the text does not in fact support. The subject then narrows from the collective assembly to Solomon alone at v23, "וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה לְמֶ֛לֶךְ" ('Solomon sat on the throne of Yahweh as king'), a focus-narrowing within the same liturgical day rather than a register-level break of the kind the gathering verbs at 11:1 and 28:1 mark. The row closes on an evaluative summary, "וַיְגַדֵּ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַ֔עְלָה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא הָיָ֧ה עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('Yahweh magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and gave to him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel,' 29:25; the relative clause's antecedent, ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת, is carried in full here rather than elided, and WEB's own closing restriction, 'not been on any king before him in Israel.', is retained). Verse 26 opens the regnal résumé with a subject-first clause, "וְדָוִיד֙ בֶּן יִשָׁ֔י מָלַ֖ךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel'), which shifts away from the enthronement scene into a summary of the completed reign.

The book strategy's own §6 block map affirmatively lists '29:10-19 David's blessing-prayer; 29:20-25 worship + Solomon enthroned' as settled, and its only live flag in this range is §7 item 15's interior question at 29:21-25, not a dispute over whether v20 itself belongs with the prayer that precedes it; I hold this row's confidence at medium because, even with the day-shift and subject-narrowing arguments given above, the interior seam §7.15 names remains one the strategy itself treats as genuinely open, not because the 29:19|20 edge is in question.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuinely strongest rival is not whether v20 attaches to the prayer before it -- the ברך root's repetition at 29:10/29:20 is a real echo, but v20's imperative-plus-new-addressee shape re-heads rather than closes, as argued above -- but whether v21 opens its own unit at the day-shift the book strategy flags at §7.15; that rival loses because the wayyiqtol subject at v21 continues v20's own collective assembly with no new inquit or addressee -- the join needed to keep v.21 inside this row rests on that continuity alone, not on v.22's own demonstrative, which on the row's continuity principle points to the newly introduced morrow rather than back to v.20's day.

boundary_rationale: The subject-first regnal clause that opens this row, "וְדָוִיד֙ בֶּן יִשָׁ֔י מָלַ֖ךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל", answers the previous row's own closing verse on the מלך root rather than reproducing a throne formula: 29:25 closes "עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" ('than any king before him, over Israel'), and this row's opening verb, מָלַ֖ךְ ('reigned'), answers that same noun מֶ֛לֶךְ with its own עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל tail -- the throne-sitting formula proper, "וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה לְמֶ֛לֶךְ" ('Solomon sat on the throne of Yahweh as king'), sits two verses earlier, inside the preceding row's own span rather than at its closing edge. Here the מלך root opens a new unit -- no scene-verb, no addressee -- answered by the reign-length count, "וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַךְ֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֥ם מָלַ֖ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֽוֹשׁ" ('the days that he reigned over Israel, forty years'), and the death notice (29:28). The same unit turns into the source-citation colophon at v29, "וְדִבְרֵי֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאֲחרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל דִּבְרֵי֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל הָרֹאֶ֔ה וְעַל דִּבְרֵי֙ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וְעַל דִּבְרֵ֖י גָּ֥ד הַחֹזֶֽה" ('the acts of David the king, first and last, are written in the records of Samuel the ro'eh-seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the chozeh-seer' -- WEB itself renders both הָרֹאֶ֔ה and הַחֹזֶֽה as 'seer' at 29:29, matching 1Chr_web_clean.txt and collapsing the same lexical distinction; the two Hebrew nouns are in fact different roots, disclosed here since the colophon's three-way title variation, alongside 'the prophet,' is part of what marks this as a source-citation colophon), which picks up the same completed reign just totaled in 26-28 with no intervening scene-change, and the row closes on 29:30's summary tag, "עִ֥ם כָּל מַלְכוּת֖וֹ וּגְבוּרָת֑וֹ וְהָעִתִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבְר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ וְעַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעַ֖ל כָּל מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאֲרָצֽוֹת" ('with all his reign and his might, and the events that involved him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the lands'), which ends both this row and the book itself, leaving no further verse to argue a closing edge against. Two petuchah breaks (both single-witness) bracket this closing unit in the WLC, one after 29:25 and one after 29:30 -- neither supplies the reason for these edges, both merely agree with them.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 29:26-28 (the résumé) from 29:29-30 (the colophon) into two rows would cut a single closing movement in two: v29's report of David's acts picks up the very reign just totaled, with no new scene-verb or addressee intervening between them.
